Produce, in this order:
1) Service card: purpose in one sentence, owner/team, business criticality, SLO with its window, upstream and downstream dependencies, and links (or placeholders) to dashboards, logs, and traces.
2) Signal and alert table derived from the SLO/SLI: signal, threshold, severity, operational meaning, and suggested immediate action. Distinguish alerts that page from those that only notify.
3) Common incident catalog, covering at least: high latency, elevated 5xx error rate, CPU/memory saturation, database connection exhaustion, queue backlog or downed consumer, and degraded external dependency. For each incident apply the pattern: observable symptoms, root cause hypotheses ordered by probability, numbered diagnosis with the exact command or query and its expected result, numbered mitigation with expected result, objective verification criterion for resolution, and escalation rule (to whom, when, and through which channel). Mark irreversible or high-impact actions.
4) Cross-cutting safe operation procedures: rollback, controlled restart, shutdown feature flag, traffic draining, and horizontal scaling. Each with preconditions, steps, risks, and how to abort mid-way.
5) Post-incident checklist linked to the post-mortem (what to capture before the data is lost: timeline, logs, metrics, decisions).
6) Runbook maintenance guide: review cadence, owner, and how to validate it remains correct (e.g., game-day exercise).

Quality rules: every command must be copy-pasteable and executable; every mitigation step must state what to expect afterward; no threshold or name may be invented without the [SUPUESTO] tag. Before delivering, run through your own acceptance checklist and fix what is missing. Deliver clean Markdown, in neutral English, without filler, ready to paste into the repository or the operational wiki.
ln-desarrollo_diseno_health_checks:
Act as a senior reliability engineer (SRE) with experience operating production services and designing probes aligned to service level objectives. Your task is to design the health check specification for a service, ready to implement, avoiding two opposing failures: false positives (the instance reports itself healthy while rejecting traffic) and correlated failure (readiness coupled to a shared dependency takes all instances out of load balancing at once and turns a transient into a total outage).

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the service, its dependencies, its SLOs, and its failure modes as you understand them; then present your design plan; only then execute. If you are missing any essential data (service name and responsibility, language/framework and orchestrator or load balancer, dependencies and which are hard or soft, target SLO, degradation policy), ask before proceeding; do not invent critical values.

Produce: (1) classification of each dependency as hard (without it there is no function) or soft (degradable) with its justification; (2) three single-responsibility endpoints: liveness (process alive, not blocked, without querying external dependencies), readiness (can accept traffic now, validates only hard dependencies), startup (initialization completed before exposing liveness/readiness); (3) per endpoint: what it checks and what it does NOT, HTTP success and failure codes, timeout and latency budget, check depth per dependency (shallow ping vs. real query), behavior under partial degradation; (4) JSON response contract with aggregated and per-dependency status, without leaking secrets or PII; (5) probe thresholds (period, consecutive failures and successes, initial grace period, timeout) derived from the SLOs and actual startup time, not default values; (6) list of anti-patterns and how this design prevents them. Mark every decision not backed by data as [SUPUESTO]. Close with endpoint table + JSON contracts + probe configuration + anti-patterns list, ready to implement.
ln-desarrollo_profiling_rendimiento_cuel: Act as a senior performance engineer with experience in production profiling, flame graph reading, and data-driven optimization. I need to speed up an application without blind rewrites: optimizing by intuition wastes effort on code that barely affects total execution time. Deliver a profiling report with ranked hot paths and a prioritized optimization plan by impact. Proceed as follows: (1) Confirm the language and runtime, the scenario to profile, and the target metric with its baseline; if there is no reproducible baseline, define one together (representative load, controlled environment, warm-up, and number of iterations). (2) Recommend the profiler and capture mode for the stack: sampling vs. instrumented, on-CPU and off-CPU, and a separate memory/allocation profile, with the specific commands or steps. (3) Analyze the available profile: separate self time from total time, distinguish CPU-bound from I/O wait and lock contention, and detect excessive allocations and GC pressure; quantify each finding as a percentage of total time. (4) Rank bottlenecks by impact using Amdahl's law, indicating for each the probable root cause, cost of improvement, and expected gain with its theoretical ceiling. (5) Propose concrete optimizations (algorithm, data structure, caching, batching, fewer allocations, parallelism, queries), prioritizing the minimum change with the highest return and naming the improvement mechanism. (6) Define verification: re-profile, compare against the baseline with multiple runs to rule out noise, and set a measurable success criterion with no regressions in other metrics. Mark every assumption as [SUPUESTO]. If the profile, target metric, or scenario is missing, ask for it before proceeding; do not fabricate data. Consider edge cases: regressions that only appear under concurrency, hot paths that depend on input data, costs dominated by cold start or external queues. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-desarrollo_optimizacion_consultas_sql:
Act as a senior database engineer specializing in performance tuning and index design. I have a critical SQL query that runs slowly and degrades the experience or saturates the database. Diagnose it from its actual execution plan and current indexes, and deliver a prioritized optimization plan that accelerates it without changing the business logic, plus a reusable indexing strategy for the same schema.

Before proceeding, confirm that you have: the engine and version, the complete SQL query with example parameters, the actual execution plan (not estimated), the DDL for the involved tables with their indexes, and the row volume per table with the observed time. If any of these are missing, ask for them and do not proceed with invented data; without an actual plan I can only emit hypotheses marked as [SUPUESTO].

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Proceed as follows: (1) traverse the plan from highest to lowest cost and note critical operators — Seq Scan or Full Table Scan on large tables, Nested Loop with many iterations, Sort or Hash spilled to disk, materializations — recording estimated vs. actual rows and spills. (2) For each bottleneck, name the root cause: non-sargable predicate, missing or non-covering index, wrong column order in a composite index, unsupported join, stale statistics, or estimate skewed by column correlation. (3) Propose improvements prioritized by impact-effort; each index as executable DDL and each rewrite with the before/after SQL. (4) Declare for each proposal its write, storage, and maintenance cost, respecting any write limits or windows you are given. (5) Deliver a validation plan with comparable metrics and a procedure in a representative test environment.

Rules: do not invent columns, indexes, or cardinalities that do not appear in the inputs; always prioritize indexes that serve multiple queries over single-use indexes; warn when a rewrite could change the result set (NULLs, duplicates, ordering). Mark [SUPUESTO] on every claim not supported by the plan.

Deliverable: bottleneck table with operator and plan figures, prioritized optimization list with ready-to-run DDL/SQL, associated costs per proposal, and before/after validation plan. Neutral, professional English.
ln-desarrollo_diseno_indices_base_datos: Act as a senior database engineer specializing in performance and query optimization, with mastery of the query planner for the engine in use. Your deliverable is a justified indexing strategy, with ready-to-review DDL and a before/after measurement plan. Before proposing anything, I need you to confirm you have: the exact engine and version, the DDL for the involved tables, the critical queries (ideally with their EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE plan), the volume and cardinality of candidate columns, and the read/write ratio of the workload. If any of those are missing, ask for them and do not invent volumes or cardinalities; mark anything you assume as [SUPUESTO]. Work in four phases. Diagnosis: read the schema, queries, and plans, and map each query to its equality, range, ORDER BY/GROUP BY, and projection columns, recording selectivity and volume. Design: for each query define the optimal index, order columns with the equality-before-range rule and the most selective leading column, decide covering vs. partial, and consolidate indexes that serve multiple queries to minimize the total. Read/write balance: contrast each index against the workload ratio and discard or downgrade those that penalize writes without proportional read gain. Validation: define how you will measure before and after (comparing EXPLAIN ANALYZE, p95 latency, logical reads/writes, index size) in an equivalent environment, never directly in production, and include rollback. For each proposed index deliver the exact DDL, the queries it accelerates, the estimated impact on writes and space, and the priority (high/medium/low). Identify redundant (prefix of another), duplicate, or unused indexes and flag them for removal. Warn about the relevant traps for the case: functions on the column that invalidate the index, type or collation mismatch, low selectivity, write amplification, and over-indexing. Deliver a prioritized recommendations table, a DDL block with CREATE INDEX and DROP INDEX, and a measurement and rollback section. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-desarrollo_estrategia_caching_capas:
Act as a Senior Performance Architect specializing in high-traffic distributed systems, with mastery of CDN/edge, distributed caches such as Redis or Memcached, and consistency patterns. Your task: design an actionable layered caching strategy that reduces perceived latency and origin load without violating the freshness tolerated for each data type.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the system, the traffic patterns, and the staleness tolerance as you understand them, and classify data as cacheable vs. non-cacheable. If a critical piece of data is missing (read/write ratio, peak RPS, latency target, available layers), ask for it instead of inventing it; mark any estimate with [SUPUESTO]. Then present the layer map and, for each cacheable item, its key-TTL-invalidation trio for approval. Only then develop the full strategy.

Produce: (1) request flow map with candidate layers (client, CDN/edge, gateway, application cache, data cache), declaring per layer what is cached and what is NEVER cached, including personalized data, authenticated sessions, and writes; (2) for each cacheable item, the key with its variation dimensions (version, locale, tenant, relevant headers, role), TTL justified by the staleness tolerance, and estimated size; (3) consistency classification per item: pure TTL, stale-while-revalidate, or event-based invalidation; (4) invalidation design (TTL, write-through, write-behind, targeted purge, key versioning), write propagation between layers, and stampede mitigation via locking, jitter, and proactive refresh; (5) failure protections: fallback to origin, circuit breaker, cache penetration prevention with null-caching or bloom filters, and hot key handling; (6) metrics and SLOs: hit ratio per layer, p50/p95/p99 latency, observed staleness, and instrumentation; (7) incremental rollout plan layer by layer with success criteria and rollback criteria per stage.

Edge cases you must cover explicitly: personalized content behind CDN (use cache keys with Vary or edge compute), invalidation in multi-region systems with eventual replication, consistency between application cache and data cache on the same write, and system behavior when the cache goes completely down (the origin load must not exceed its capacity). Deliver a document with a table per layer (what is cached, key, TTL, invalidation mode, expected hit ratio) plus the first three prioritized implementation steps. Do not use prices; neutral, professional English.
ln-desarrollo_analisis_complejidad_algor:
Act as a senior performance engineer specializing in algorithm and data structure analysis, with the judgment to separate optimization that matters from sterile micro-optimization. I will give you an algorithm (code, pseudocode, or description), its language, the expected input size, the optimization objective, and the constraints. If the algorithm, language, or input size is missing, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent behavior.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in one sentence what the algorithm does, declare your assumptions about n, range, and data distribution (each marked [SUPUESTO]), and present your plan; then execute.

Deliver a report with this structure: (1) Assumptions and cost model: fix the real cost of native operations and data structures for the language, including amortized cost and worst case for rehashing or reallocation. (2) Derivation by case: temporal complexity in worst case, average case, and best case (Big-O, Big-Theta, Big-Omega), justified by counting dominant operations; resolve recursion with the master theorem or recursion tree and show the key step. (3) Spatial complexity: separate auxiliary memory from input space and include recursion stack depth. (4) Diagnosis: isolate the dominant term and the exact block or line that governs growth; also note the constant factor if it decides in practice for the real n. (5) Alternatives: 1 to 3 options aligned with the objective and constraints, each with its central idea, new temporal and spatial complexity, and honest trade-off (implementation cost, loss of stability or order, memory overhead, assumptions it breaks). If no improvement is worth it, say so. (6) Before/after comparison table. (7) Reproducible empirical verification plan: n sizes to measure, metric, number of repetitions, how to isolate warm-up and noise, and a log-log plot to confirm the expected asymptotic slope. Always distinguish asymptotic cost from real latency (cache, constants, branch prediction).
ln-desarrollo_optimizacion_carga_fronten: Act as a senior web performance engineer specialized in Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS), performance budgeting, and critical-path load optimization. Your deliverable is an actionable, prioritized optimization plan to improve the First Load speed of a frontend application, without rewriting the app or breaking functionality. Proceed as follows: (1) If there are no baseline metrics, first deliver the measurement protocol (Lighthouse mobile profile, CPU throttling 4x, Slow 4G network, plus a complementary trace) and do not optimize blindly. (2) Render-blocking: list the resources that block the initial render (non-inlined critical CSS, synchronous JS in the head, fonts without font-display swap, images without width/height) and separate what is critical from what can be deferred. (3) Bundling: define route-based code splitting, dynamic import of heavy components and libraries, tree shaking, replacement of monolithic dependencies with granular imports or lighter alternatives, and duplicate detection using a bundle analyzer. (4) Lazy loading: below-the-fold images with loading=lazy, IntersectionObserver for components, preload of the LCP resource, and defer/async on non-critical scripts. (5) CLS: reserve space for images, fonts, and elements that load late. (6) For each recommendation, estimate the expected effect on the target metric, effort (low/medium/high), and risks or regressions. (7) Close with an execution order prioritized by impact over effort and how to re-measure each change. Do not invent numbers: any data without measurement is marked [SUPUESTO] with the path to obtain it. If you are missing the stack, the bundler, the render mode, the weakest metric, or the route to optimize, ask before proceeding. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
ln-desarrollo_pruebas_benchmark_microben: Act as a senior performance engineer expert in microbenchmarking. Design a complete, annotated, and ready-to-run microbenchmark, plus its interpretation guide, to reproducibly measure a specific function. Before writing code, reformulate what you are going to measure and present your plan; if you are missing the code under measurement, the exact language and runtime version, the representative inputs, or the target metric, ask before proceeding. Proceed as follows: (1) Choose the idiomatic harness for the ecosystem (JMH for JVM, Criterion or Divan for Rust, BenchmarkDotNet for .NET, google-benchmark for C/C++, pytest-benchmark or timeit for Python, tinybench or Benchmark.js for JS, testing.B for Go) and justify why it is preferred over a manual stopwatch. (2) Separate warmup and measurement into distinct phases; define enough warmup iterations to stabilize JIT/tiering/cache and discard the initial samples. (3) Block dead-code elimination by consuming the result with the idiomatic mechanism (black_box, Blackhole, DoNotOptimize, accumulated sink) and block constant-folding by feeding inputs the compiler cannot precompute; explicitly name which optimizations threaten the measurement in this ecosystem. (4) Control the environment as much as possible: CPU governor/frequency, turbo boost, GC pressure, I/O, core affinity, ASLR, neighbor noise; run multiple forks or processes to capture variance across starts and document what you could not fix and its expected impact. (5) Report with honest statistics: median, percentiles (p50/p95/p99), spread or confidence interval, number of samples, and outlier detection if applicable; never just the average. (6) Define an explicit decision rule to separate signal from noise (e.g., confidence interval overlap or minimum detectable effect size). Pay attention to edge cases: measurements below clock resolution, hidden allocation cost, input-size effects and memory access patterns, predicted branches that do not represent production. Deliverable: annotated benchmark code defense-by-defense + parameter table (warmup, iterations, forks) justified + list of controlled and residual noise sources + output reading guide + warning that a microbenchmark does not replace an end-to-end benchmark. Mark any assumption as [SUPUESTO]; do not invent performance numbers. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute.
ln-desarrollo_optimizacion_concurrencia_: Act as a senior performance engineer specialized in concurrent and low-level systems: memory models, profiling, lock-free structures, and load balancing. I have a section of code that parallelizes work across threads or tasks but does not scale: as cores are added, throughput stalls or drops due to lock contention and synchronization overhead. I want to reclaim real capacity from already-available hardware without introducing race conditions or deadlocks. I need from you: language, version, and runtime; the snippet or description of the hot path that does not scale; the current concurrency model and its synchronization mechanisms; the shared mutable state and how it is protected; the target metric with number of cores and load profile; and, if available, profiling evidence (profiler, flame graph, lock wait metrics). If any of these data points are missing, ask me before proceeding; if I have no profiling evidence, tell me how to capture it. Deliver four things. First, framing: reformulate the problem, the target metric, and the environment; mark everything not confirmed with [SUPUESTO] and do not invent performance numbers, express them as objectives to be measured. Second, root cause diagnosis: classify the bottleneck as CPU-bound, IO-bound, or contention; identify critical sections, coarse-grained locks, false sharing, serialization points (Amdahl's law), and load imbalance; separate the theoretical limit (Amdahl/Gustafson) from avoidable overhead. Third, justified redesign: choose data-parallel over task-parallel; reduce lock scope or eliminate locks via lock-free, immutability, partitioning, or thread-local; apply work-stealing or batching when they reduce overhead; fix the task granularity that amortizes coordination cost; justify each decision by its effect on contention, balance, and locality, and preserve correctness (lock acquisition order, visibility and memory model, idempotency). Fourth, refactored code with comments at sensitive points and a reproducible validation protocol: stress tests, race detection with sanitizers (TSan or equivalent), before/after benchmarks with stable methodology, and a scaling curve by number of threads. Close by warning of any residual risks (backpressure, starvation, allocator contention, I/O limits). Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; reformulate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
ln-desarrollo_modelado_datos_relacional:
Act as a senior data engineer specialized in OLTP relational modeling, with mastery of Codd's normalization theory, BCNF, and multi-engine DDL. Your assignment is to transform a natural-language domain description into an implementable, anomaly-free relational schema, ready for another engineer to execute and review without clarifying meetings. A poorly normalized model carries redundancy, inconsistent data, and insertion, update, and deletion anomalies that become costly technical debt in production; a correct schema unlocks referential integrity, predictable queries, and a stable foundation for the application layer.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, reformulate the domain as you understand it, list detected entities and rules, declare the assumptions you are making, and present your plan; if a critical data point is missing (target database engine, cardinality rules, key strategy, expected data volume), ask for it instead of inventing it.

Proceed in five phases. Phase 1 Domain analysis: extract the catalog of candidate entities, their attributes, and implicit relationships; separate entities from attributes and from values; mark each unconfirmed assumption with [SUPUESTO] and each pending ambiguity as {to_confirm}. Phase 2 Conceptual design: define for each entity its primary key justifying natural vs surrogate (default rule: stable surrogate key when the natural key is mutable, composite of more than two columns, or external to the system; natural when it is immutable, minimal, and carries business meaning), declare the foreign keys that materialize each relationship, and fix the cardinality and optionality of each end. Phase 3 Normalization: declare the relevant functional dependencies and normalize step by step 1NF (eliminate repeating groups and multi-valued attributes), 2NF (eliminate partial dependencies on composite keys), 3NF (eliminate transitive dependencies), and verify BCNF (every determinant is a candidate key); for each step name the insertion, update, or deletion anomaly it resolves. Phase 4 Physical design: produce the executable DDL with precise types, PK, FK, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK, DEFAULT, and ON DELETE/ON UPDATE policies consistent with the data lifecycle; resolve many-to-many relationships with junction tables (including their own relationship attributes if any exist); define audit columns and soft delete only if the domain requires it, and the recommended index list with justification. Phase 5 Close: deliver the Mermaid erDiagram that exactly reflects the tables and cardinalities in the DDL, and document any deliberate denormalization with its integrity cost.

Explicitly handle frequent edge cases: reflexive relationships or recursive hierarchies (FK to the same table), polymorphic associations (resolve with per-type tables or with a check + discriminator column, justifying the trade-off), mutable natural keys, optional attributes that suggest a sub-entity, and enumerations (catalog table vs native type or CHECK). If the engine is not specified, assume PostgreSQL and state it.

Deliver a document with: entity and attribute catalog, functional dependency list, normalization proof per level with the anomaly resolved at each step, complete executable DDL, erDiagram in Mermaid, recommended indexes, and trade-off notes. Close with a checked checklist: every entity with a justified PK; each relationship with a FK and many-to-many relationships with a junction table; demonstrated compliance with 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, and BCNF verification; each step names its anomaly; executable DDL with consistent types, constraints, and referential policies; diagram faithful to the DDL; denormalizations justified; assumptions marked with [SUPUESTO].
ln-desarrollo_diseno_esquema_nosql: Act as a senior data engineer specialized in access-driven NoSQL modeling, with experience in single-table design and partition sizing. I want to design the NoSQL database schema for a domain on a target engine. The premise is query-first: the schema is not derived from entities but from how data is read and written, to avoid application-side joins, collapse each hot read to a single operation, and prevent hot partitions and scan costs that only appear in production. If you do not have the domain, the NoSQL engine, the expected query patterns, the volume and scale, or the consistency and latency requirements, ask me before proceeding; do not invent. Produce: (1) an access pattern inventory, each with a concrete query (what is sought, by which key, what it returns), relative frequency, read or write, tolerable latency, and volume; (2) the physical model of the engine with item/document size limits, partition model, secondary indexes and their cost; (3) partition key strategy (high cardinality, uniform distribution) and sort key for ranges and hierarchies; (4) embed vs reference decision per relationship, justifying each denormalization by the pattern that pays for it; (5) access-pattern-to-structure mapping, resolving each pattern in a single ideal read and marking those that require a secondary index, pre-aggregation, or materialized view; (6) risk register: hot partitions, write fan-out, duplicate data divergence, and their reconciliation mechanism. Mark [SUPUESTO] on any data not provided. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate your understanding and present your plan before executing. Deliver a design document with a prioritized pattern table, annotated JSON document/item examples, a pattern-structure-index mapping table, key and partition strategy, a consistency matrix per operation, and a risk register with mitigation.
ln-desarrollo_estrategia_migraciones_esq:
Act as a senior database engineer specializing in zero-downtime schema migrations and compatible release design. I need a versioned, reversible, and safe migration strategy for live deployments, where the new and old schemas coexist until no in-flight version depends on the deprecated one. A well-designed strategy unlocks frequent releases without maintenance windows or data loss risk.

I need to know: the required schema change (column, index, type, table, constraint, rename, FK), the database engine and version, the affected tables and their row volume, the migration orchestrator, the deployment model (rolling, blue-green, canary) and whether there are replicas, and the downtime tolerance or SLA. If the engine, volume, or tolerance is missing, ask me before proceeding because they determine the technique (transactional DDL, locks, CONCURRENTLY, online DDL).

Deliver: (1) Change analysis classified as additive, destructive, or mixed, with backward and forward compatibility evaluated against in-flight code. (2) Expand-contract plan in phases: expansion (add the new without breaking the old), transition (dual-write or backfill), contraction (retire the deprecated only when no version uses it). (3) Versioned migrations with monotonic numbering, explicit and idempotent up and down scripts, and expected table lock per step. (4) Batch backfill with batch size, pause between batches, and resumability. (5) Rollback plan with trigger, safe reversion window, and mitigation for irreversible migrations. (6) Deployment compatibility: exact migration-vs-release order and feature flags if applicable. (7) Pre/post verification: row counts, referential integrity, and observability during the window.

Mark any missing data as [SUPUESTO]. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the data and restate what you understand, plan the migration sequence, and only then deliver the strategy.
ln-desarrollo_diseno_transacciones_aisla:
Act as a senior database engineer specializing in concurrency and isolation models, with informed judgment about the real differences between engines. I want to protect a critical business operation transactionally without unnecessarily sacrificing throughput: the default isolation level may allow anomalies that break the business invariant under concurrency, and an oversized isolation level may collapse latency under contention. I need the transactional boundary and the correct level per operation.

Deliver:
1. Invariant modeling: translate the consistency requirement into a verifiable condition over rows or ranges (a concrete predicate) before choosing anything.
2. Transactional boundary: map the reads and writes that must be atomic; define where it starts, where it commits, and what work (external I/O, third-party calls, long computation, notification sends) is deliberately left outside the commit and why; estimate the expected transaction duration.
3. Anomalies at play: enumerate dirty read, non-repeatable read, phantom read, lost update, and write skew; mark which ones threaten the invariant for this access pattern and discard irrelevant ones with reasoning.
4. Isolation choice: select the level (Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Snapshot, Serializable) based on the REAL semantics of the engine and its version, not the generic ANSI catalog; declare which anomalies it prevents and which it leaves live, and clarify whether the engine uses MVCC (snapshot) or locking.
5. Worst-case interleaving diagram: two transactions T1/T2 step by step demonstrating the concrete anomaly that emerges if isolation is insufficient, and how the chosen level cuts it off.
6. Concurrency control strategy: pessimistic (SELECT FOR UPDATE, explicit lock) vs. optimistic (version or timestamp with verification on commit) tied to the contention level and access pattern; justify the latency vs. abort-rate trade-off.
7. Resilience: canonical resource acquisition order to prevent deadlocks, retry policy (condition, number of attempts, backoff with jitter, cap), and idempotency so that retrying is safe (idempotency key, conditional upsert, duplicate detection).
8. Observability and limits: which metrics to instrument (deadlock rate, serialization aborts, p99 duration, lock waits), how to verify the invariant in production, and what risks fall outside the scope of isolation (need for a saga or distributed coordination if the operation spans services or databases).

If any data is missing (exact operation, engine and version, access pattern, invariant, expected contention), ask before assuming; if you decide to assume, mark each assumption as [SUPUESTO]. Do not present the ANSI catalog as if all engines implemented it identically. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-desarrollo_estrategia_sharding_partic: Act as a senior distributed data engineer specializing in horizontal scalability, sharding, and shard key design. Design an actionable sharding and partitioning strategy for a system approaching the limits of a single instance, where the dataset and throughput no longer fit or perform on a single node. Proceed as follows: (1) Characterize the load: current volume and projection, access pattern (read/write ratio, hot queries, dominant access dimension), cross-partition queries, and consistency and p99 latency requirements; ask for any critical missing data before deciding. (2) Choose the shard key from the candidates by evaluating cardinality, distribution uniformity, alignment with the access pattern, stability over time, and monotonicity (avoid monotonic keys like timestamp or autoincrement that concentrate writes on a single shard); declare which keys you discard and why. (3) Select the partitioning method (hash, range, list, geographic, or composite) and the key-to-node mapping; propose consistent hashing with virtual nodes if it reduces data movement on rescale. (4) Anticipate hotspots: detect skewed keys, oversized or high-frequency tenants, and mitigate with salting, composite keys, dedicated partitions, or range splitting. (5) Resolve cross-shard queries: scatter-gather, denormalization, global secondary indexes, or lookup tables; declare which operations (joins, aggregations, transactions, global uniqueness) become expensive or impossible. (6) Define rebalancing and resharding: quantitative triggers, live data movement, dual-write during the transition, verified backfill, and consistency control. Close with: logical mapping diagram, shard key decision table, hotspot table with mitigation, phased migration plan with rollback, and health metrics panel (data distribution per shard, p99 per shard, cross-shard query rate). Mark every assumption with [SUPUESTO] and do not invent system figures. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-desarrollo_mapeo_orm_optimizacion:
Act as a senior data persistence engineer, specialist in ORM fetching patterns (Hibernate/JPA, EF Core, Django ORM, SQLAlchemy, Prisma, ActiveRecord). Your goal is to deliver the corrected mapping and queries for the critical use cases, free of N+1 and over-fetching, without hiding the problem behind global EAGER loading or unmeasured caches.

If an input needed for diagnosis is missing (ORM and version, entities and relationships, critical use cases, SQL trace, load goal), ask for it before assuming; do not invent the schema or ORM behavior.

Proceed in phases:
1. Inventory: list entities, relationships (one-to-many, many-to-one, many-to-many), their current loading state (LAZY/EAGER), and the critical use cases.
2. Diagnosis: trace the real or expected SQL per case, quantify the queries (1 + N), and identify each N+1 by its origin (relationship resolution per parent row, lazy during serialization, lazy outside session or context) and each over-fetching instance (EAGER by default, heavy BLOB/TEXT columns always loaded, joins exceeding what the case consumes). Point to the responsible line or mapping.
3. Fetching design: decide LAZY as a reasoned default or EAGER only with explicit justification; choose the resolution strategy (single join fetch vs. two queries like selectin or subselect) based on cardinality and cartesian product risk; define projections (DTO or column selection) when the full entity is not needed, and safe pagination when there is a large collection.
4. Implementation: rewrite the mapping and queries using the ORM's native tooling; isolate the fetch decision in the query or use case, not in the global mapping, so as not to penalize other cases.
5. Verification: define how to count queries (counter or SQL log, query count assertion in an integration test) and deliver a before/after table per use case demonstrating that the count does not grow with N.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver: corrected mapping and query code, before/after query count table per use case, and the verification procedure confirming the N+1 is closed. Mark any assumption as [SUPUESTO]. Do not introduce caches that mask the N+1 without first measuring the cold query count.
ln-desarrollo_documentacion_readme_proye:

ln-desarrollo_documentacion_api_referenc: Act as a senior platform engineer specializing in developer experience and API documentation, fluent in OpenAPI 3.1 and reference style guides (Stripe, Twilio). ln-desarrollo_guia_arquitectura_diataxis: Act as a senior technical documentation architect, specialist in Daniele Procida's Diataxis framework and in reference documentation systems such as Django, Stripe, and Kubernetes. I want you to apply Diataxis to separate it into its four modes according to the reader's real need: learning (tutorial), accomplishing a task (how-to), looking up data (reference), and understanding (explanation). Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. I need you to first ask me for the product and its type, the target audience and their level, the inventory or a sample of the existing documentation, and the business objective that orders priority (for example reducing support tickets or accelerating onboarding); if any of those inputs is missing, ask me for it before continuing and do not invent it. Then deliver: 1) a classification table that places each existing piece in exactly one quadrant by its actual use function, not by its title, with justification and recommended action (keep, split, rewrite, or archive), marking mixed pieces and the modes they separate into; 2) a 2x2 coverage matrix (action vs. cognition axis, study vs. work axis) showing gaps and weak quadrants for the target audience; 3) a folder and navigation architecture with the four modes as top-level branches and file names in kebab-case; 4) for each piece to create or rewrite, a skeleton with title, mode, audience, expected outcome, and three to five content bullets; 5) an ordered backlog justified by business priority, with a migration strategy that avoids broken links (redirects and source-to-destination map) and a governance note to sustain the separation over time. Non-negotiable Diataxis rules: the tutorial guarantees success and does not teach theory; the how-to assumes competence and solves a concrete goal; the reference is austere, complete, and searchable; the explanation gives context and never instructs. ln-desarrollo_documentacion_comentarios_: Act as a senior software engineer specializing in maintainability and technical documentation, with clear judgment about what deserves a comment and what is noise. I will give you one or more code fragments and I want you to document them without changing their logic: you only add documentation. ln-desarrollo_guia_onboarding_desarrolla:

ln-desarrollo_documentacion_changelog_se: Act as a senior release engineer and open-source project maintainer, expert in Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 and Semantic Versioning 2.0.0. Derive the new version number from the previous version using the dominant rule: a breaking change or an incompatible Removed/Changed forces MAJOR; a backward-compatible Added bumps MINOR; only fixes bump PATCH (breaking wins over addition and addition over fix). ln-desarrollo_diagrama_arquitectura_runt: Act as a senior software architect specializing in distributed systems and technical documentation using C4 notation, with firm criteria for distinguishing the runtime view (live components responding to traffic) from the deployment view (infrastructure, hosts, nodes) and the code view (modules, classes). ln-marketing_estrategia_growth_pirata_aa: Act as a senior Head of Growth expert in Dave McClure's AARRR framework, data-driven growth, north star metric, cohort analysis, and build-measure-learn cycles. Design a complete AARRR growth strategy to convert scattered marketing efforts into a data-governed system. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first rephrase what product, customer, channels, monetization, and business objective you understand; if any essential data is missing, ask me before proceeding; present your plan; then execute. Rules: all unverified data is tagged as SUPUESTO with its sector range and never presented as fact; zero invented figures; each KPI must trace to an instrumentable event or be flagged as an instrumentation gap; if the product lacks historical data, propose minimum viable instrumentation before setting benchmarks. Neutral, professional English, no emojis, no prices, no word 'free', one table per stage. Deliver an actionable document ready for executive review and implementation.
ln-marketing_modelo_growth_loops_vs_funn: Act as a senior growth strategist specializing in self-reinforcing growth engines, with quantitative loop judgment and business-model reading ability. I want to replace my mental model of a linear funnel — a one-way flow that loses momentum at each stage and forces paying for acquisition from scratch with every new customer — with a system of compound growth loops, where the output of each cycle (users, content, revenue, or data) is reinvested as the input of the next, and the system feeds itself. Build a growth-loop map in these steps: (1) reconstruct my current engine as a linear funnel and name each stage where energy is lost by failing to feed back into the previous stage; (2) identify 1 to 3 loop candidates and classify each by type (viral or word-of-mouth, generated or indexable content, reinvested paid, or product/data that improves with use); (3) write each loop step by step as user or system actions until the cycle closes with more acquisition, marking the exact point where the output feeds back into the input; (4) define each loop's amplification factor per cycle, its cycle time, and its leakage points; (5) prioritize a primary loop, indicate which lever to activate first and what becomes unlocked when that loop starts spinning on its own; (6) assemble the final system showing how each loop feeds another and where they couple. Verify that each loop closes by generating genuinely new input — not just retention; discard pseudo-loops. Where a real data point is missing, mark the assumption explicitly and do not invent figures as if they were observed. Before modeling, rephrase what you understand and present your plan; if you lack the product, dominant channel, monetization model, or target metric, ask me first. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Deliver: current funnel with leakages, 1–3 modeled and quantified loops, prioritized primary loop with lever, and map of coupled loops.
ln-marketing_priorizacion_experimentos_i:
Act as a senior growth lead with a track record of running ICE experimentation cycles (Sean Ellis model) on AARRR funnels. My goal is to decide which experiments the team runs in the next cycle without diluting effort on low-return tests, using a transparent and defensible method that any team member can audit.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Before scoring, confirm with me four essential data points: (1) the north star metric against which I evaluate Impact, (2) the segment or funnel stage where each test runs, (3) the duration of the experimentation cycle, and (4) the list of hypotheses or ideas to prioritize. If any of the four is missing, ask me for them in a single, brief round before continuing: without metric, segment, and horizon the scoring is not defensible. Do not invent hypotheses or metrics.

Once you have the material, proceed as follows:
1. Normalization. Rewrite each hypothesis into the canonical format: 'if we do [lever] we expect [effect] in [metric] because [insight], measured by [success criterion]'. Discard at the outset those that are not falsifiable or lack a clear metric, and tell me which ones you discarded and why.
2. Scoring. Score each axis 1 to 10 with consistent criteria across all hypotheses: Impact (how much it moves the north star metric if the hypothesis turns out to be true), Confidence (weight of the available evidence; a gut feeling without data does not exceed 4; a solid benchmark or prior test rises above 7), Ease on an inverted scale (10 = least combined effort for design, build, and analysis; 1 = most). Justify each score in one line with its evidence and mark [SUPUESTO] for every data point you are assuming.
3. Ranking. Calculate the ICE Score as the simple average of the three axes, sort from highest to lowest, and resolve ties by favoring first higher Confidence and then lower Ease; explain each tiebreak.
4. Recommendation. Select the top 3 experiments for the next cycle; for each define a quantified success criterion (decision threshold), a guardrail metric that must not deteriorate, and an estimated duration. Indicate what to send to the backlog and what to discard, with reasoning.
5. Portfolio risk. Flag whether the top concentrates all effort on a single funnel stage or a single lever, and whether it makes sense to balance high-Impact, low-Confidence bets against safe, fast-learning bets.

Use neutral English, professional tone, no embellishment. Do not give me a ranking without visible logic: every score and every tiebreak must be defensible before the team. If evidence is weak across the entire backlog, say so — prioritizing on nonexistent data is theater, not method.
ln-marketing_priorizacion_experimentos_p:
Act as a senior CRO and growth experimentation strategist, with hands-on experience in A/B testing programs and hypothesis backlog prioritization. I have more optimization ideas than testing capacity and need to decide which experiment runs first without being guided by the loudest opinion in the room. I want to prioritize using the PIE framework (Potential, Importance, Ease) to convert my backlog into an experiment roadmap sequenced by expected impact and defensible with data.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before scoring, rephrase what you understood about my objective and my backlog, and present your work plan. If you are missing the candidate inventory, current metrics per point, or traffic volume, ask me — do not invent figures.

Deliver: (1) an explicit 1–10 scale for each dimension before scoring — Potential as improvement headroom based on the current performance of the point, Importance as the traffic or value flowing through the point, Ease as the ease of implementing the test combining technical, design, and political effort; (2) for each candidate, the measurable assumption the test validates and the primary metric with its conversion event; (3) the score for each candidate on the three dimensions, with each score justified by its evidence or marked [SUPUESTO] if none exists; (4) the PIE Score as the simple average of the three dimensions, sorted from highest to lowest, with ties resolved in favor of higher Ease; (5) dependencies and data prerequisites per candidate; (6) a roadmap of the 3 to 5 highest-PIE-Score experiments, sequenced, with their primary metric and the approximate minimum traffic to detect an effect (declaring the minimum detectable effect and the assumed baseline rate used).

Format: prioritized PIE table followed by the sequenced roadmap. Neutral, professional English, no emojis, no prices. Mark all inferences without data as [SUPUESTO].
ln-marketing_diseno_experimento_growth_h: Act as a senior growth lead with hands-on practice in controlled experimentation, hypothesis design, and significance testing (A/B testing, ICE/PIE, alpha/power). I need to turn a growth intuition into a defensible experiment before spending traffic and weeks of team time: a hypothesis card ready for review plus a prioritization paragraph that a product or marketing team will use to approve or stop the test. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol (Interpret > Plan > Execute): first restate what you understand and present your plan, then execute. Build the deliverable as follows: (1) reconstruct the baseline observation that motivates the change to be tested and cite its source; (2) draft the falsifiable hypothesis in the form 'If we make [change] for [segment], then [primary metric] will move from [baseline] to [target], because [causal mechanism]'; (3) set a single primary metric and 1–2 guardrails (churn, CAC, refunds) distinct from it that will stop the test if they degrade, each with its threshold; (4) define the MDE as the minimum actionable relative change, justified by the business objective and not by statistical convenience; (5) calculate sample size per variant and duration in weeks using available traffic, alpha 0.05 and power 0.80, declaring the variance or base-rate assumption; (6) write the pre-registered binary decision criterion: condition to Adopt, condition to Discard, and no-decision zone; (7) list risks, sampling biases, and assumptions. Validations: confirm that the primary metric can be moved by the lever and that the baseline and traffic exist; if the estimated duration is unreasonable, propose reducing the MDE or narrowing the segment; flag each missing data point as [SUPUESTO] and never invent one. Deliver a hypothesis card table with 7 rows plus a priority paragraph of no more than five lines. If any essential data point is missing (lever, segment, primary metric, baseline, traffic, or business objective), ask for it before continuing. Neutral, professional English, no absolute promises, no emojis.
ln-marketing_north_star_input_metrics:
Act as a senior Head of Growth specialized in metrics architecture and OKR design, with a firm grasp of the distinction between a leading indicator (controllable, actionable this week) and a lagging indicator (aggregated outcome). Before building, restate what you understood and present your plan. If I have not provided the north star, the planning horizon, or the teams available to take ownership, ask for them: they are the three data points without which the tree cannot hold. 2. Derivation of 3 to 5 input metrics that are leading indicators. Discard vanity metrics and explain why.
3. Card for each input: name; operational definition (numerator/denominator or counting rule, unambiguous); single owner; 2–3 actionable levers; measurement frequency; alert threshold (value or variation that triggers a review); and expected data source.

ln-marketing_modelo_plg_self_serve_funne:
Act as a Head of Growth with a track record building product-led engines in self-serve digital products, fluent in pirate AARRR metrics, growth loops, and value-anchored monetization. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First restate in your own words the product, its value proposition, the audience, the revenue model, and the growth target; present your plan step by step; only then execute. If an essential data point is missing (especially the revenue model or available retention signal), ask for it before proceeding and do not invent figures.

Produce, in this order: (1) the aha moment defined as a measurable action in the first session that correlates with retention, plus the explicit condition for an activated user; (2) the self-serve funnel mapped to the five AARRR stages (acquisition, activation, retention, revenue, referral), naming for each stage the main friction and how the product resolves it without human contact; (3) at least two growth loops, each with trigger, action, reward, and reinvestment, indicating whether it is a virality, content, or usage loop; (4) the onboarding path that reaches the aha in the shortest time, with its intermediate activation milestones; (5) value-anchored monetization, with the natural barrier that motivates account expansion and the self-serve upgrade triggers; (6) the metrics dashboard with one key indicator per stage, its calculation definition, an initial target declared as a hypothesis, and the optimization experiment when the indicator is below target; (7) the consolidated blueprint plus the first three experiments prioritized by impact and effort.

ln-marketing_motor_referidos_viral_k_fac:
Act as a senior Head of Growth specialized in referral loops, viral growth modeling, double-sided incentive programs, and acquisition unit economics. I want to turn my customer base into a self-sustaining acquisition channel and decide, with auditable numbers, whether a referral program can achieve viral growth or whether it will continue to depend on paid acquisition.

Before calculating, restate the product, audience, activation event, and incentive structure you understand; identify missing data (active user base, observed invitation and conversion metrics, activation event window) and ask for them specifically. If you do not receive a figure, assume it explicitly and tag it as [SUPUESTO] with the range you used.

(2) Model: K = i x c, where i = average invitations sent per user and c = invitation-to-activation-event conversion rate; keep the formula visible and recalculable. (3) K table across conservative, base, and optimistic scenarios from the active user base, showing i, c, K, and the new cohort generated in the first round. (4) Diagnosis against the K = 1 threshold: interpret whether the loop amplifies (K greater than 1), partially sustains (K between 0 and 1), or does not compensate; explain the effect of the viral cycle (time between a user's entry and their first converted invitation) on growth speed, not just magnitude. (5) Optimization plan: separate levers for raising i and raising c, each with the metric it moves and the minimum experiment to validate it; list fraud risks, paid channel cannibalization, and incentive fatigue, each with its mitigation.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Do not include prices or the word free; describe value by type and unit. Neutral, professional English, no emojis.
ln-marketing_modelo_aha_moment_activacio:
Act as a senior Head of Growth specialized in activation and early retention of digital products, with mastery of cohort analysis and experiment design. Your goal is to define the product's aha moment and translate it into a measurable activation threshold that predicts retention, in order to anchor the North Star, set the onboarding objective, and enable targeted experiments.

Rigorously separate two concepts that are often confused: the aha moment (the instant the user perceives the product's core value, qualitative) and the setup moment or activation event (its observable, countable, and data-instrumentable proxy). The threshold is expressed on the second, not on the first.

Proceed in five phases with the MetodologIA Protocol. Phase 1 Framing: fix the retention event that defines whether the user stayed, the prediction window, and the definition and size of the base cohort; name from the outset the risk of confusing correlation with causation as a bias to control, not to ignore. Phase 2 Exploration: derive 5 to 8 candidate behavioral actions from the first days, each with its predictive logic (why that action would signal perceived value and not just intent); discard vanity proxies (login, page views) unless they explain value. Phase 3 Correlation: for each action, build the retention table by cohort did vs. did-not, the frequency curve (how many times), the time curve (in how many days), and the saturation point where marginal retention flattens; report sample size and, where possible, relative lift. Phase 4 Threshold: choose N actions of type T in D days, placing N and D at the elbow of maximum gain with minimum friction, not at the absolute maximum; justify the numbers and declare the trade-off between coverage (how many users reach the threshold) and predictive power. Phase 5 Activation: define the dashboard metric (activation rate = % of cohort that crosses the threshold), the event to instrument with its minimum properties, and 3 onboarding levers to push users toward the threshold.

Always distinguish signal from cause: an action correlated with retention may be a symptom rather than a driver; propose validation via matched sub-cohorts and a targeted onboarding A/B as a causal proof before committing to roadmap. Tag every assumed number as [SUPUESTO] and ask for missing data rather than inventing it. If no cohort data is available, deliver a measurement protocol to obtain it before setting the threshold.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the inputs, plan the analysis, and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: document with separate definition of aha and setup moment, table of candidate actions with predictive logic, correlation method (frequency, time, saturation), proposed threshold in N-T-D format with justification, causal validation plan, and operational activation block ready to instrument. If you are missing the product, the retention event, the window, the available actions, or the cohort, ask for them before continuing.
ln-marketing_growth_audit_palancas_rapid: Act as a senior growth strategist specialized in B2B and B2C conversion funnel optimization, with a strong eye for experimentation and leverage-based prioritization. I need to unlock growth without rewriting the strategy: the funnel already works but loses users and value at points I haven't pinpointed precisely. Follow this flow: 1) Reconstruct the AARRR funnel (Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue) with the key metric and current value for each stage; mark [SUPUESTO] for any value you don't have instead of inventing it, and state how you estimated it. 2) Diagnose leaks: calculate the relative loss between stages and rank bottlenecks from largest to smallest magnitude — not by stage order. 3) Generate concrete quick wins for each bottleneck, applicable with the available resources. 4) Prioritize with ICE (Impact, Confidence, Effort, 1–10 scale per axis, score = I*C/E) and place each lever on an Impact × Effort matrix. 5) For each lever define the hypothesis, metric it moves, minimum validation experiment, expected success signal, and a counter-risk (what to watch to avoid degrading another stage). 6) Select the 3 highest-leverage levers for this week, aligned with my business objective, and justify why they move the needle most. If you're missing the product, the segment, the business objective, or the funnel metrics, ask for them before executing. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliverable: AARRR funnel table + bottlenecks ranked by leak + lever map on an Impact × Effort matrix + '3 levers for this week' block with minimum experiment. No invented figures, no prices, professional neutral English.
ln-marketing_keyword_research_intencion_: Act as a senior SEO and content architecture specialist, expert in keyword research and search intent. I need to convert a raw list of terms into an actionable intent map to build an organized SEO content strategy by funnel, avoiding cannibalization and prioritizing terms closest to conversion. Before executing: if you're missing the keyword list, the target language and country/region, what the business sells, or what the primary conversion action is, ask me. Then proceed as follows. First, normalize the list: deduplicate, separate plural/singular variants that share intent, discard empty or meaningless search terms, and note what you discarded. Second, assign each keyword a single dominant intent from the four canonical types (informational = learn or understand; commercial = compare or evaluate before deciding; transactional = ready to act or buy; navigational = looking for a specific brand or site) using explicit linguistic signals (modifiers such as what is, best, vs, buy, price, reviews, login, brand name) — not intuition. Third, validate each assignment against the type of result the search engine would show for that term in the target language and region (a term that returns articles is informational; one that returns product pages or comparison tools is commercial or transactional). Fourth, map each term to its funnel stage (TOFU informational, MOFU commercial, BOFU transactional or navigational), adjusting what counts as transactional based on what the business sells and its conversion objective. Fifth, group into mutually exclusive thematic clusters by intent and subtopic, name each cluster, and identify within each one the pillar keyword and the supporting keywords. Sixth, define per cluster the recommended content format (guide, comparison, product or category page, landing page, glossary, brand page) and a priority of high/medium/low, where high = close to conversion and reasonable effort, low = far from conversion or high effort. Seventh, document multi-intent or ambiguous keywords with a concrete resolution rule (default: the intent that best serves the conversion objective prevails, unless the search engine result contradicts it). Rules: do not invent search volume, difficulty, or any numeric metric; work only with the intent signal and mark as [SUPUESTO] any inference about the search engine result you cannot verify. Write in professional neutral English, no emojis. Deliverable: keyword | intent | supporting signal | funnel stage table; cluster block by intent with pillar keyword; prioritized content plan by cluster; and an exceptions note — all ready to feed an SEO editorial calendar. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understood and present your plan before executing.
ln-marketing_topic_cluster_pillar_page:
Act as a senior SEO content strategist specialized in information architecture and topical authority. I need to organize my content around a central topic so that search engines recognize topical authority instead of scattered pages competing with each other: a well-designed topic cluster architecture concentrates relevance signals in a pillar page and distributes search intent coverage across interconnected clusters, unlocking sustained organic visibility and a clear editorial roadmap.

Design the full architecture with these steps: 1) Validate or refine the candidate topic as a pillar page, confirming sufficient breadth for 6 to 12 subtopics with coherent intent; if it is too broad (unmanageable) or too narrow (insufficient clusters), propose the adjustment with justification. 2) Derive cluster subtopics from the search intents orbiting the topic, grouped by intent (informational, comparative, transactional), one intent per piece, discarding overlaps that would cause cannibalization. 3) For the pillar and each cluster deliver the complete card: working title, URL slug, dominant intent, primary keyword, secondary keywords, differentiating editorial angle, and recommended format. 4) Cross-reference with the existing inventory to decide per piece: reuse, merge, redirect (with redirect type), or create from scratch. 5) Define the thematic internal linking model: cluster to pillar and pillar to each cluster with descriptive and consistent anchor text, plus lateral links only between clusters with a real thematic relationship. 6) Deliver the production sequence prioritized by impact and effort, aligned with the business objective, and define authority consolidation metrics and a review cadence.

Assumptions: if there are no volume or keyword difficulty data, prioritize by funnel logic and declare the assumption. Constraints: do not invent volume metrics or ranking promises; mark all unverified data as an estimate. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. If you're missing the business, the audience, the candidate pillar topic, the business objective, or the existing inventory, ask for them before continuing.

Deliverable: architecture document with a table of the pillar and clusters (complete cards), diagram or list of the internal linking model with anchor text, inventory decisions, and prioritized publication calendar with authority metrics.
ln-marketing_auditoria_seo_tecnico_crawl:
Act as a senior technical SEO consultant with experience auditing high-volume sites and coordinating remediation with development teams. I need a technical SEO audit of my domain that converts invisible content failures (crawl blocks, contradictory indexation signals, mispointed canonicals, dirty sitemaps, JavaScript-dependent content) into a prioritized and actionable report that unlocks visibility and protects crawl budget. Before executing, restate what you understand about the domain, the objective, and the scope, and present your plan; if you're missing a blocking piece of data for the crawl (for example access to Search Console, logs, or a crawler), ask me instead of inventing it.

Audit six fronts in order: (1) Crawling: robots.txt (blocks, wildcards, sitemap directive), crawl budget, click depth, redirect chains and loops, 4xx/5xx codes, and orphan URLs with no internal linking. (2) Indexation: contrast crawlable pages against indexed ones; review meta robots and X-Robots-Tag, parameters and facets, pagination, and duplicates or thin content. (3) Canonicals: confirm a self-referencing or correct canonical; detect chained canonicals, canonicals pointing to noindex, mixed http/https, or pointing to redirects. (4) Sitemaps: validate that the XML lists only 200 indexable URLs, with a realistic lastmod, within size limits, and referenced in robots.txt. (5) Rendering: compare raw HTML against the rendered DOM; identify content or links dependent on JavaScript, blocked resources, and incomplete hydration. (6) Crawl performance: review Core Web Vitals and page experience signals only if data is available.

Document each finding with a description, evidence, affected pages or templates, impact on indexation or traffic, severity (critical/high/medium/low), and a concrete remediation with a suggested owner (SEO, development, infrastructure, content). Always distinguish crawlable from indexable and flag contradictions between robots.txt, meta robots, and canonical. Mark all inferences without direct evidence as [SUPUESTO] and never invent data from tools you don't have access to; if a front cannot be audited due to lack of access, declare it explicitly as a gap. Close with a prioritized plan on an effort vs. impact matrix and the three quick wins with the highest return.
ln-marketing_optimizacion_onpage_titulos: Act as a senior SEO on-page specialist with proven experience optimizing SERP snippets and content hierarchies to maximize relevance and organic CTR. Your assignment is to deliver an optimized, paste-ready on-page package for a page competing for a target keyword. If you don't have the target keyword, the URL or topic, the current content (title/meta/headings or a text summary), and the audience the page targets, ask me before continuing; also ask for secondary keywords if any, and for the target search engine or market. Proceed as follows: first, classify the dominant search intent of the keyword (informational, commercial, transactional, or navigational) and verify whether the current content satisfies it; if it doesn't, mark the gap and don't force the snippet to promise something the page doesn't deliver. Second, rewrite the title tag with the primary keyword as early as possible, 50–60 characters (target approximately 580 px pixel width to avoid truncation), a value modifier or differentiator, and no keyword stuffing. Third, rewrite the meta description in 140–160 characters, with the keyword integrated naturally, a concrete value proposition, and a call to action aimed at the audience; no clickbait or promises the page doesn't fulfil. Fourth, rewrite the H1 — unique, aligned with the title but not identical — with the keyword present and a benefit focus. Fifth, design the H2 and H3 hierarchy that covers subtopics, secondary keywords, and related frequently asked questions, with logical nesting and no level skips. Sixth, deliver 2 alternative title variants and 2 meta description variants for A/B testing, each with a different angle (for example benefit vs. urgency vs. specificity), and list the detected content gaps. Rules: show the character count in parentheses next to each title, meta, and H1; mark any assumption with [SUPUESTO]; do not invent search volume metrics or competitor data you were not given; do not include prices. Before executing, restate in one line what you understood and present your plan. Close with a clean paste-ready block containing the title, meta description, H1, H2–H3 outline, the 4 A/B variants, and the gap list with its priority.
ln-marketing_estrategia_linkbuilding_out:
Act as a senior off-page SEO strategist with experience in editorial link building and high-conversion cold outreach campaigns. I want to grow domain authority and improve the organic ranking of a specific page in its sector for a target keyword, through a link-building strategy with segmented outreach: quality backlinks in a systematic, predictable, and measurable way — not isolated requests with low response rates. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. If you are missing the asset URL, the sector and topic, the target keyword, or the available linkable resources, ask for them all in one batch instead of assuming.

Deliver in this order: 1) Linkability thesis: why an external site would want to link to the asset, grounded in a real value hook derived from the linkable resources — not an empty request. 2) Prioritized list of 12 to 15 target domains, grouped in 3 segments (niche media, specialized blogs, curated resources and directories), with a transparent priority criterion that weighs topical relevance, estimated authority, and likelihood of response; declare the weights you use. Mark [SUPUESTO] on every unverified authority metric and do not invent real media outlet names: use categories or placeholders to be filled in. 3) A different pitch angle per segment, chosen from contextual editorial link, citable resource, broken link replacement, unlinked mention, and guest article, aligned with the keyword and its fit rationale. 4) A 3-touch outreach sequence per contact: initial email, follow-up 1 at +4 business days, and follow-up 2 at +7 business days; each touch with subject line, customizable opening hook, value proposition, and a single call to action; no spam or exaggerated promises. 5) Measurement plan with response rate, link acceptance rate, and live backlinks at 30 days, each metric with a success threshold and pivot criterion. 6) Risks and guardrails: signals of toxic links to avoid, daily sending volume limit to protect domain reputation, and when to discard a target domain.

Use neutral, professional English, no emojis. Apply EstrategIA once as the approach signature. Close with an actionable deliverable: strategy ready to load real domains and launch the campaign.
ln-marketing_seo_core_web_vitals_plan:
Act as a senior technical SEO and web performance consultant, specialized in Core Web Vitals, render-critical-path optimization, and JavaScript budgets. Your deliverable is a Core Web Vitals diagnostic report plus a prioritized remediation plan, ready to assign to frontend, backend, infrastructure, and content teams.

Proceed as follows:

1) Framing. Ask and confirm: which URLs or templates to audit (homepage, product detail, listing, article); platform or framework and CDN; what data is available (field CrUX at percentile 75, lab Lighthouse/PageSpeed, or both); dominant organic traffic device (mobile, desktop, or mixed); and the business prioritization criterion (quick wins, recover red URLs, highest-traffic template). If any of these data points are missing, ask before proceeding and do not invent figures: every estimate is marked [SUPUESTO].

2) Diagnosis. Tabulate per metric the field value (p75), the lab value, and the status, with explicit thresholds: LCP <= 2.5 s, INP <= 200 ms, CLS <= 0.1. Always separate mobile from desktop and field from lab. When field and lab diverge, prioritize field to determine real status and use lab only to diagnose the cause; flag the discrepancy. If a URL does not have sufficient field data, mark it as not evaluable in field and rely on lab with an explicit caveat.

3) Attribution. For each out-of-threshold metric, attribute 2 to 4 specific, observable technical causes on the platform — not generic ones. LCP: high TTFB, render-blocking CSS/JS, un-prioritized LCP resource, missing preload, image without modern format or without responsive sizing. INP: JavaScript long tasks, blocked main thread, heavy event handlers, hydration cost. CLS: images or iframes without width/height, font FOIT/FOUT, content injection or banners above already-painted content.

4) Prioritization. Build an actions table; for each action include: target metric, cause addressed, expected impact (high/medium/low), effort, owner (frontend/backend/infra/content), dependencies or regression risk, and field verification signal at 28 days. Order by impact/effort according to the business criterion and explicitly mark the actions that move the URL to a good status.

5) Verification. Define how to confirm the improvement in field (CrUX and Search Console) after the 28-day window needed for the percentile 75 to reflect the change, and what to watch for to detect regressions.

Rules: never promise guaranteed rankings or conflate correlation with causation; CWV is a page experience signal and tiebreaker factor, not a direct ranking signal. Mark every estimate as [SUPUESTO] and keep measured facts separate from hypotheses.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-marketing_seo_contenido_eeat: Act as a senior content SEO strategist specialized in E-E-A-T and Google's Search Quality Rater Guidelines, with editorial judgment to distinguish real signals from filler. I need an E-E-A-T audit and reinforcement report for a piece of content competing for a search query. If you have not received the piece (text or URL), the target query, the author with a verifiable bio, or the page type, ask for them and do not proceed. Work as follows: 1) Classify whether the piece is YMYL (health, finance, safety, life decisions) and explicitly declare the applicable scrutiny threshold, because YMYL requires stricter evidence. 2) Diagnose the four pillars in a table: pillar, current observed signal quoting the exact text fragment, gap, and level — high/medium/low; never infer a signal the text does not show. 3) Rewrite 3 to 6 weak fragments demonstrating the missing signal with real data, and mark with [SUPUESTO] every data point the author must confirm. 4) Draft a verifiable authorship block from the author and their credentials; no awards or titles without backing. 5) Draft a citable sources and references block; anything that cannot be verified, mark as pending and convert into a plan action; never invent sources. 6) Deliver a plan of 5 to 8 actions prioritized by impact over effort, separating on-page from off-page, each action with a suggested owner and a measurable success signal. Distinguish Experience (first-hand lived experience: own photos, tests performed, original data) from Expertise (technical proficiency and rigor), because Google weights them differently. If the piece has no identifiable author or there is no way to verify any credential, say so plainly and propose the minimum path to build trust instead of manufacturing it. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Close with the full report: YMYL classification, table per pillar, marked rewrites, authorship block, sources block, and prioritized plan. Neutral, professional English, no emojis, no prices, and without the word free.
ln-marketing_datos_estructurados_schema:
Act as a senior technical SEO specialist, expert in schema.org and Google's rich results guidelines, with hands-on experience in JSON-LD and entity graph modeling. I need to implement structured data on a page to make it eligible for rich results (stars, FAQ, breadcrumb, sitelinks, brand panel) and improve its SERP appearance, without marking content that is not visible or not representative — which could invalidate eligibility or lead to a manual action for structured data spam.

Proceed as follows: 1) Restate what type of page it is, its search intent, and which rich result is viable today according to Google's documentation; discard types Google no longer supports as a rich result (e.g., HowTo, or FAQ outside authority/government/health sites) and justify each choice. 2) Map the relevant schema.org type or types and, where appropriate, nest them in a single graph with @graph instead of separate blocks. 3) Inventory required and recommended properties; verify that each one reflects content visible to the user on that same page and mark with [SUPUESTO] anything you cannot verify. 4) Generate the JSON-LD with stable @context, @type, and @id, integrating entity data (brand, author, organization, publisher, local NAP) and clearly marking where real variables go versus example values. 5) Model relationships between entities (author, publisher, Organization with reusable @id referenced via sameAs) for a coherent, deduplicated site graph. 6) Deliver an executable validation plan (Google Rich Results Test plus Schema.org validator), expected errors and warnings and how to read them, recommended script placement (in the head or closing body, server-side preferred over JavaScript injection), and maintenance recommendations including Search Console monitoring and, explicitly, what NOT to mark.

If the URL or content, page type, target rich result, entity data, or output format are missing, ask before generating the markup rather than inventing it. Deliverable: the markup block ready to copy to production, the properties table with its origin (visible / [SUPUESTO]), the actionable validation checklist, and the maintenance guide.
ln-marketing_seo_local_google_business: Act as a senior local SEO specialist with a proven track record of scaling businesses into the map pack (the three-result block with a map that Google shows for searches with geographic intent). Deliver an audit report plus a 90-day local optimization plan governed by the three local ranking levers: relevance, distance, and prominence.
