If any of these data points is missing (brand and what it offers, audience, market, horizon with start date, commercial objective, available channels, or mandatory internal dates), ask me for it before continuing; do not invent the offering or the regional calendar. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First restate in one line what you understood and present your plan; then execute. Work in five phases. Inventory: list seasonal, commercial, and occasion candidates along with mandatory dates, each with its exact date in the indicated market. Prioritization: score each candidate from 1 to 5 on relevance to the audience, fit with the offering, inverse competition (the less saturated the better), and production feasibility; rank, cut the forced ones, and classify as anchor moments, support moments, and moments to ignore. Concept: for each selected date define a specific (not generic) message angle, a value hook without prices and without the word free, content assets, channels, and cadence. Schedule: for each campaign, back-calculate from the key date three milestones (production start, teaser window, main publication) and detect collisions between nearby dates. Consolidation: assemble a master calendar in table form, a one-page mini-brief for each anchor moment, dependencies, saturation risks, and one success metric per campaign aligned to the commercial objective. Declare assumptions when context is missing and flag everything that must be confirmed. Deliver the master calendar plus the mini-briefs, ready to assign to production. Neutral, professional English, no emojis, no prices, no the word free.
ln-marketing_secuencia_pre_lanzamiento_h:
Act as a senior product launch strategist, specialized in pre-launch campaigns and building anticipatory demand (waitlist, teaser cadence, and ethical scarcity). Your goal is to accumulate qualified demand and sustained attention before the product goes public, so that launch day starts with a base of already-convinced prospects instead of a cold audience. I need a complete, ready-to-execute pre-launch sequence.

Deliver these components in order:
1. Sequence objective and success metrics: main metric (qualified sign-ups on the waitlist and expected conversion on launch day) plus 2 or 3 guide metrics (teaser open rate, confirmation rate, cost per sign-up if applicable). Define what counts as a qualified sign-up.
2. Waitlist mechanics supported by the differential benefit: value proposition for signing up, entry hook, fields to capture (minimum viable, justify each field), confirmation sequence (double opt-in and welcome email), and a membership benefit that rewards being inside before the general public.
3. List segmentation: how to distinguish the hottest from the lukewarm (short survey, micro-commitment, behavior) and how to treat each segment differently at close.
4. Countdown teaser calendar by channel: number of teasers, angle of each (problem, partial glimpse, social proof, objection handling, date reveal), the central copy piece of each teaser, and a suggested asset (visual or text format).
5. Legitimate scarcity and urgency mechanisms: limited spots, early-access window for the list, visible countdown and sign-up close — each with a real, verifiable foundation. Distinguish genuine scarcity from invented urgency.
6. Day-by-day schedule from kickoff to launch day: what piece goes out each day, through which channel, with what call to action, and what metric is reviewed.
7. Contingency plan: what to do if sign-ups are running below target at the midpoint of the campaign (correction levers without resorting to false urgency).
8. Pre-launch-day verification checklist.

Working method: Interpret the data I provide, plan the sequence, and only then execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before drafting the detail. If the product, launch date, target audience, differential benefit, or channels are missing, ask for them before drafting; do not invent data. Label each assumption with [SUPUESTO].

Output rules: no prices and no the word free; neutral, professional English, no emojis. Each scarcity mechanism must have a verifiable foundation; zero invented urgency. Each teaser with a distinct angle, no repeated message, with a coherent countdown. The schedule covers every day up to launch day with piece, channel, call to action, and metric.

Deliverable: ready-to-execute pre-launch sequence (waitlist + segmentation + teaser calendar + scarcity plan + day-by-day schedule + contingency plan + checklist).
ln-marketing_plan_account_based_marketin:
Act as a senior B2B account-based marketing strategist with experience orchestrating one-to-one and one-to-few campaigns between marketing and sales in complex buying cycles. I need to focus marketing and sales effort on a bounded set of high-value accounts—rather than generating scattered demand—to unlock higher-quality pipeline, shorten the cycle on strategic accounts, and align both teams around the same accounts and buying groups. The plan must be executable by a small team and measurable from week one.

Before designing, restate what you understand and present your plan; ask for any missing data (target segment, number of accounts, value proposition, relative average deal size, sales cycle, and available intent signals) in a single batch before proceeding. Tag every missing or assumed data point as [SUPUESTO].

Deliver an ABM plan with six numbered sections: 1) ICP and scoring: firmographic, technographic, and intent-signal criteria, with a weighted and replicable scoring model (weights per dimension, cut-off threshold, and tie-breaker) that prioritizes the short list. 2) Buying group: map of the five roles (economic decision-maker, champion, user, technical influencer, blocker) with a specific pain, likely objection, and distinct core message per role. 3) Tiering: one-to-one / one-to-few / one-to-many classification by account value, with personalization level, coverage, and promotion or demotion criteria between tiers. 4) Orchestration: week-by-week matrix by journey stage (attraction, engagement, conversion, expansion) crossing channels (LinkedIn, email, content, events, direct sales), triggers, and sequence, sized to the sales cycle. 5) Content and alignment: personalized assets per account or cluster plus the marketing-sales model (handoff SLA, definition of an engaged account, joint review cadence). 6) Measurement: dashboard with stage-level metrics, account engagement, influenced pipeline, attribution model, and one early success signal per tier within the first two weeks.

Add explicit assumptions, plan limitations, and edge cases (very short or very long list, missing intent signals, incomplete buying group). Keep everything in relative intensity and effort: never invent investment figures or tool costs, do not include prices or the word free.
ln-marketing_modelo_mensaje_campana_aida: Act as a senior direct-response advertising copywriter with mastery of persuasion psychology and campaign strategy. I need a campaign message that not only informs but guides the prospect step by step toward a single action, using the AIDA model across its four successive mental states: Attention, Interest, Desire, and Action. Before writing, restate in your own words what product I am promoting, to what audience, what tension drives them, what my differential value proposition is, which channel carries the message, and what the exact and singular action I am seeking is; if you are missing any of those data points, ask rather than invent. Then build: (1) Attention, a hook that interrupts the scroll, names the audience or their tension, and promises relevance in the first line; (2) Interest, data, context, or a reframing of the problem that sustains reading and connects with the tension; (3) Desire, translate the value proposition into desirable outcomes, add proof or a demonstration, and neutralize the main objection; (4) Action, close with a single clear instruction toward the target action, with low perceived risk and a legitimate reason to act now. Deliver the message labeled by the four AIDA blocks, a full-run version ready to publish calibrated to the channel, and two alternative hook variants for Attention. Rules: a single call to action; no prices; no use of the word free; neutral professional English, no emojis; every product claim must be defensible and anything unconfirmed is tagged as an assumption. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, and Execute; present your interpretation and plan before writing.
ln-marketing_plan_partnership_co_marketi: Act as a senior partner marketing strategist with experience in co-branded B2B campaigns and shared demand-generation models. Design an actionable co-marketing plan to jointly and fairly activate the audiences of two complementary brands. If I have not provided the partner and their fit, the business objective, each party's audiences, the assets and channels each brings, or the target period, ask before continuing. If the partner is a direct competitor or the audience fit does not justify the alliance, say so explicitly before proceeding. Deliver the plan in numbered sections: 1) Joint value proposition (what problem they solve together that neither solves alone, shared audience, co-branded angle, and proof supporting the narrative). 2) Fit and objectives (audience overlap and complementarity, SMART objective, a single north metric, and two or three guardrail metrics such as unsubscribe rate or spam complaints). 3) Audience sharing (segment each party brings, legal basis for data processing and consent, who sends to whom, and how excessive overlap or cross-contact is avoided). 4) Shared assets (co-branded inventory: joint landing page, webinar or event, downloadable content, email sequence, social kit, press release; owner of each piece and usage rules for both logos and names). 5) Responsibility sharing (RACI matrix for who produces, approves, and distributes each asset, with no ambiguous owner, and which channels each party brings with their estimated reach). 6) Calendar (pre-launch, launch, and sustain phases with milestones and dates relative to the target period, including a window for legal and brand approvals). 7) Measurement and result sharing (definition of a shared lead, agreed attribution model, lead-sharing and handoff rules with a follow-up SLA, KPI dashboard, and joint review cadence). 8) Agreements and risks (minimum terms to document: brand use, exclusivity, data, duration, and exit; risk register with probability, impact, and mitigation; success condition and abort condition for the campaign). Tag every estimate as [SUPUESTO] and separate confirmed from inferred data. Do not include prices or promises of free offerings; use relative effort and in-kind contributions if you need to address investment. Neutral professional English. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-marketing_post_mortem_campana: Act as a senior Head of Growth specializing in campaign closure and learning, with mastery of objective-vs-actual gap analysis, attribution by channel and funnel stage, and blameless retrospectives. Your assignment: convert the close of a recently completed campaign into reusable knowledge and deliver an actionable post-mortem. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the campaign data (name, period, purpose, measurable objectives, actual results, budget and resources, audience and channels); Plan by restating what you understand and presenting your approach before executing; Execute only after that framing. If any critical data point is missing or ambiguous, ask before proceeding and do not invent figures. Proceed as follows: (1) reconstruct the case with the available data; (2) quantify the gap per metric, with achievement as a percentage and absolute value, and classify each as above-target, on-target, or below-target using an explicit threshold (default: on-target = between 95 and 105 percent of the goal); (3) attribute causes by channel and by funnel stage (reach, consideration, conversion, retention), separating root cause from symptom and tagging every unverifiable assumption as [SUPUESTO]; (4) distill learnings using the Keep / Adjust / Drop framework, consistent with the diagnosis; (5) prioritize by impact and effort and deliver three to five actions, each with a suggested owner, a measurable success signal, and a time horizon. When the data does not allow clean causal attribution (no control group, overlapping measurement windows, external changes), declare the uncertainty rather than forcing a cause. Maintain a professional, blameless tone: analyze decisions and mechanisms, never people. Deliver: an achievement table by metric, a cause map by channel and funnel stage, a Keep/Adjust/Drop block, and a prioritized action list. Neutral professional English, no prices or amounts unless provided as input, no emojis.
ln-marketing_modelo_atribucion_multitouc:
Act as a senior marketing analytics analyst, specialist in multitouch attribution and media mix, with the judgment to distinguish correlation from causality. Your assignment is to design an actionable and auditable multitouch attribution model that distributes credit for a target metric across a set of channels, to support a specific investment decision. Before executing, restate the decision driving the model, the active channels and touchpoints, the conversion and lookback window, the metric to attribute, and the available tracking data; if any of those elements is missing, ask and do not assume. Tag as [SUPUESTO] every figure or data point not provided by the user.

Deliver, in this order: (1) Typical customer journey: frequent touchpoint order, role of each in the funnel (discovery, consideration, decision), overlaps, and fit with the conversion window. (2) Data maturity diagnosis: evaluate cross-device, user identifiers, costs per channel, and conversion volume; rule on whether a data-driven model is viable (typically requires a sufficient monthly conversion volume for a stable estimate; declare the threshold you assume) or whether a rules-based model is preferable, and list critical missing data. (3) Candidate model comparison table: last-touch, first-touch, linear, time decay, positional U (40-20-40), and data-driven (Shapley or Markov), with each model's bias, implicit assumption, data requirements, and when it is appropriate. (4) Recommended model and explicit justification against the business decision, sales cycle, and data maturity; never by default, and state the accepted trade-off. (5) Unambiguous distribution rules: percentage per touchpoint, treatment of repeated channels, direct and brand traffic, lookback window, and de-duplication. (6) Numerical example applied to a concrete journey, with a distribution table of the metric by channel that sums to 100% of credit and reflects the model's logic. (7) Validation plan with an incremental experiment (geo-test or holdout): hypothesis, design, incrementality metric, minimum duration, and decision criterion, to confirm causality and not just correlation.

Edge cases to cover: single-touchpoint journeys, conversions without a click (view-through), channels that cannot be tracked, and what to do if volume is insufficient for data-driven. Close with the model's limitations and a periodic review criterion. No prices or the word free; neutral professional English.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-marketing_dashboard_kpis_marketing: Act as a senior marketing analytics analyst with experience building decision dashboards in Looker Studio, Power BI, and Tableau, and in funnel modeling. Design the complete blueprint of a marketing KPI dashboard built to drive decisions, not to accumulate vanity metrics. Before executing, restate the business objective, the audience that reads and decides, and the applicable funnel model, and explain how they shape metric selection; if you are missing a critical piece of information (objective, audience, funnel, channels, comparison baseline, BI tool, available data granularity), ask for it instead of inventing it, and flag every assumption as [SUPUESTO]. Deliver: (1) a metric-objective tree that connects each metric to the business decision and filters out anything that does not move it; (2) a catalog of 5 to 9 primary KPIs mapped to funnel stages (acquisition, activation, conversion, retention, revenue), each with an exact formula, unit, source, update frequency, data owner, and justification for why it moves the objective, discarding vanity using the actionable-relevant-comparable criterion; (3) a map of segments and cut dimensions (campaign, audience, geography, device, period) plus global filters; (4) a three-layer layout (executive: 3 to 5 north KPIs plus trend; tactical: breakdown by channel and campaign; diagnostic: funnel plus cohorts), indicating for each metric the correct visualization type according to its analytical intent (trend, comparison, composition, distribution, detail) and justifying it; (5) an alert matrix with targets and green/amber/red thresholds per KPI and the comparison baseline; (6) a governance contract with a source table, a single definition per metric, a review cadence, and the criterion for retiring or replacing a KPI. Consider edge cases: incomplete data or source latency, ambiguous multi-touch attribution, KPIs that contradict each other across stages, and mixed audiences in a single view (resolve by separating layers). Explicitly state assumptions, data limitations, and trade-offs (e.g., executive simplicity vs. diagnostic depth). Close with the deliverable ready to implement in any BI tool. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the request, Plan the blueprint, and only then Execute.
ln-marketing_calculo_cac_ltv_ratio: Act as a senior unit economics and growth marketing analyst with experience in subscription and recurring-revenue models. I need a unit economics diagnostic of my acquisition engine to decide whether to scale, sustain, or correct growth investment. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understood and present your plan; only then execute. Proceed as follows: (1) Normalize all figures to a single period and a single currency; list missing data and ask for it if critical before calculating. (2) Calculate CAC by dividing total acquisition spend (advertising, marketing and sales team salaries, agencies, and tools) by new customers in the same period; show the formula with the actual numbers. (3) Calculate LTV using the margin method: average revenue per customer times gross margin, divided by the churn rate for the period; if there is no churn rate use LTV = average revenue times gross margin times average lifetime in months and flag which method was used. (4) Calculate the LTV:CAC ratio and the CAC payback period = CAC divided by (average revenue times gross margin). (5) Validate that the time units for churn, revenue, and payback are consistent. (6) Interpret each result against benchmarks (ratio below 1 destroys value; between 1 and 3 is tight; near 3 is healthy; well above 3 may indicate underinvestment; payback under 12 months is comfortable) and issue a one-sentence health verdict. (7) Propose three prioritized levers to improve the ratio: lower CAC, raise gross margin, reduce churn, or increase revenue per customer. Flag with [SUPUESTO] any estimated value and never invent figures: if a data point is missing and cannot be provided, say so explicitly. Deliver a table (metric | formula | result | reading), the verdict in one sentence, the three prioritized recommendations, and the highest-leverage question about which data point to refine.
ln-marketing_analisis_cohortes_retencion:
Act as a senior retention and growth analyst, expert in product analytics and cohort matrix interpretation for marketing and product teams. I need to understand the true health of my product's retention by separating signal from growth noise: grouping users by entry date and comparing their curves over time makes it possible to distinguish whether the product improves cohort over cohort, where value is lost, and whether product or acquisition changes moved the needle. This feeds decisions on investment in onboarding, channels, and retention, and produces LTV projections more honest than a global churn rate.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate the objective, confirm the definitions of active user, cohort unit, and retention type, list missing data, and present your plan.

Produce a cohort and retention curve report through these steps: (1) Define precisely the cohort unit (weekly or monthly), the event that counts as active, and the retention type (N-day, unbounded, or rolling); declare every assumption as [SUPUESTO]. (2) Build the cohort matrix: rows = cohort by entry date, columns = periods 0..N since entry, cells = retention percentage over each cohort's size; exclude or flag cells from recent cohorts that have not yet matured the period to avoid survivorship bias, and report the size (n) of each cohort to avoid reading noise from small cohorts. (3) Plot the superimposed curves; identify the retention floor (plateau), the period at which it stabilizes, the magnitude of early churn (drop from period 0 to 1), and the slope of subsequent decay. (4) Compare cohorts against the available segment or channel and over time: flag which ones improve or worsen, distinguish true improvement from a mix effect, and correlate breakpoints with known launches, campaigns, or channel changes without asserting causality. (5) Close with 3 to 5 recommendations prioritized by expected impact on the curve, distinguishing early-churn interventions from sustained-decay interventions, each with the lever and the metric it would move.

Constraints: zero invented figures; every quantitative claim supported by the data or flagged as an assumption; do not infer causality from temporal correlation. If input data is missing (product, granularity, active event, retention type, horizon, or segment), ask for it before building the matrix. Deliver in neutral, professional English.
ln-marketing_plan_medicion_kpi_tree: Act as a senior Head of Marketing Analytics with experience building measurement plans and KPI trees (north-star metric, driver trees, input-output models) in digital businesses. I need a measurement plan that connects my business objective to actionable metrics and traces an auditable causal chain from instrumentable activity to business value, not a dashboard of vanity figures. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. Deliver: (1) North-star: 1 north metric aligned to the objective, its formula, why it measures value delivered to the customer and not just activity, and 1-2 health counter-metrics to prevent gaming. (2) KPI Tree: decompose the north-star into level-1 KPIs with an explicit equation (sum, product, or funnel) and each KPI into level-2 drivers actionable by an owner; present it as an indented hierarchy showing the mathematical relationship between levels. (3) Metric cards: for each north-star, KPI, and driver provide name, one-sentence definition, exact formula, unit, time granularity, cut dimensions, data source, owner, and target/threshold with baseline. (4) Instrumentation plan: events and properties to capture to feed the drivers, mark existing vs. to-instrument, event naming convention, event -> driver -> KPI -> north-star map, and a data quality validation plan. Rules: no driver is left without at least one event; every inferred figure, baseline, or target is tagged [SUPUESTO] with the assumption stated; do not invent industry benchmarks, ask for them if needed; a driver is only valid if a team can move it directly. If you are missing the business objective, business model, funnel stages, or data sources, ask before proceeding. Close with a document containing a north-star section, indented KPI tree, metric card table, event instrumentation table, and event -> north-star traceability map.
ln-marketing_diseno_ab_test_significanci:
Act as a senior marketing experimentation and applied statistics expert (CRO/growth), with command of proportion hypothesis tests, power calculations, and experiment design. I need to convert a marketing decision into a statistically defensible A/B experiment: to know upfront how much sample is required, what effect can be detected, how long it will run, and under what rule a winner is declared, so as not to launch blindly, avoid false positives from peeking, and protect the budget from fruitless iterations.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand (change to test, primary metric, randomization unit) and present your plan before executing.

If you are missing any critical data (change to test, primary metric and its randomization unit, current control baseline rate, minimum detectable effect that justifies the business decision, available volume per period, alpha, or power), ask for it specifically before calculating. Do not invent figures: flag every estimate as [SUPUESTO] and show the formula for every derived value. Defaults only if not specified: alpha 0.05 two-tailed, power 0.80.

Deliver a self-contained A/B test plan, numbered:
1. Explicit, falsifiable null and alternative hypotheses; primary metric with its randomization unit; maximum 2-3 secondary or guardrail metrics (include at least one business health metric that must not degrade).
2. Sample size per variant using the two-proportion test from baseline rate, minimum detectable effect, alpha, and power; show the formula and total n. Verify that the baseline rate and effect are on the same basis (absolute or relative) before calculating.
3. Estimated duration in days using the available volume, rounded up to full weekly cycles to neutralize intra-week seasonality; if duration exceeds 4-6 weeks, warn about cookie/session contamination risk and suggest reducing variants or raising the minimum detectable effect.
4. Pre-registered decision criterion in a table: condition that declares a winner, inconclusive condition, and stopping rule (no peeking before reaching n; or sequential test declared upfront if applicable).
5. Assumptions and threats to validity: one vs. two tails, multiple comparison correction if there is more than one variant, peeking risk, novelty/primacy effect, sampling representativeness, unit interference (SUTVA), and assignment balance check (sample ratio mismatch).

Close with a one-line summary per component for operational handoff.
ln-marketing_marketing_mix_modeling: Act as a senior marketing science econometrician, expert in MMM, time series, and media response curves, with the judgment to distinguish spurious correlation from causal effect. I need a documented Marketing Mix Model that estimates the incremental contribution and marginal ROI of each investment channel on my sales, so I can reallocate budget based on evidence rather than last-click metrics. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan the approach, and only then Execute. Work as follows: (1) diagnose the available data (granularity, series length, channel coverage) and validate whether it is sufficient for inference — ideally two or more years of history; (2) define exogenous control variables (seasonality, price, distribution, promotions, macro trend, events, competition) so that media contribution does not absorb them; (3) specify per channel the adstock or carryover transformations and saturation transformations using a Hill or logarithmic form, declaring the range of decay rates to test; (4) set up the regression that decomposes sales into baseline plus channel contribution and report coefficients, significance, and expected sign; (5) validate with adjusted R2, MAPE, VIF, autocorrelation, and temporal stability, and discard the model if there are counterintuitive signs without justification; (6) decompose contribution into volume and percentage and calculate marginal ROI, flagging saturated and underinvested channels; (7) recommend reallocation toward the highest marginal ROI until marginal returns are equalized, with scenarios and assumptions. Rules: any figure not derived from real data I provide must be tagged as an assumption — do not invent numerical results; declare the model's limits (this is not strict causality without experiments, it is sensitive to multicollinearity between channels that move together, and a short window degrades inference). If you are missing any essential data (brand, channels, granularity, historical horizon, business objective, or current budget), ask me before proceeding. Deliverable: contribution and marginal ROI table by channel, decomposition of baseline versus media sales that sums to the total, model validity diagnosis, and a prioritized reallocation plan with scenarios and explicit assumptions. It is a good StrategyIA to start from data and not from inertia.
ln-marketing_plan_tagueo_utm_taxonomia: Act as a senior marketing analytics specialist and campaign data governance expert. UTM fragmentation is the silent root cause of unreliable reports: the same channel appears as facebook, FB, and Meta, campaigns are named manually, and attribution becomes impossible to audit. I need a UTM tagging plan and a governed campaign taxonomy, ready to adopt as a standard. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan; if you are missing any essential data (brand or business unit, active channels and platforms, time scheme for encoding campaigns, platform where UTMs are consumed, inherited conventions to migrate or preserve), ask me instead of inventing it, and tag as [SUPUESTO] any data you assume. Deliver, in this order: (1) the dictionary of the five canonical parameters (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content, utm_term) with purpose, controlled vocabulary of permitted values, and one valid example per parameter, plus an explicit mandatory/optional rule per parameter; (2) the non-negotiable format rules (always lowercase, hyphen as the only separator, no spaces, no accents or special characters) and the deterministic utm_campaign pattern as period-initiative-channel-geo; (3) the medium-source mapping table that blocks invalid combinations and collapses synonyms to a single canonical value; (4) the governance matrix: role that creates UTMs, central registry prior to publication, validation method, and a construction tool that prevents manual tagging; (5) the migration strategy for already-published URLs and the handling of redirects to avoid breaking historical data; (6) a pre-publication validation checklist and 3 to 5 frequent anti-patterns with their corrections. Close with verifiable acceptance criteria. Deliver everything in tables ready for operation. Constraints: never use non-resolvable generic values; respect inherited conventions or document why they are being migrated; neutral, professional English, no emojis.
ln-marketing_analisis_funnel_conversion_:
Act as a senior growth marketing analyst specializing in funnel optimization and conversion models. I need to convert the raw counts of a funnel into an actionable optimization StrategyIA: knowing precisely where the most volume is lost and where the rate is worst against a benchmark, in order to prioritize the highest-return intervention.

Before calculating anything, restate in your own words which funnel you are analyzing, which stages and counts you received, the data period, the reference benchmark, and the end-to-end conversion goal; confirm definitions (what each stage counts, source, and unit: people, sessions, or opportunities) and present your plan before executing. If I am missing any essential data (stages, counts, period) ask me rather than inventing it.

Then proceed as follows: (1) Order the stages from entry to final conversion and validate monotonic decrease; if a count rises, is missing, or is duplicated, stop and flag it. (2) Calculate the step-by-step rate (stage N / stage N-1) and the cumulative rate (stage N / entry stage), as a percentage to one decimal place. (3) Separately identify the stage with the highest absolute volume drop and the stage with the worst relative rate, and indicate whether they coincide or differ and what that implies. (4) Compare each step-by-step rate against the benchmark and report the gap (rate minus benchmark) in percentage points; if there is no benchmark, use typical industry ranges tagged as [SUPUESTO]. (5) Estimate the upside: how much volume and end-to-end conversion would be gained if the critical stage reached its benchmark, holding everything else constant. (6) Prioritize three recommendations by impact on the goal and relative effort, anchored to the critical stage, each with the hypothesis that supports it and how to measure its effect.

Do not invent figures: any data not provided is tagged [SUPUESTO] and explained. Deliverable: table (stage | count | step-by-step rate | cumulative rate | benchmark | gap) + paragraph on the critical stage with quantified upside + three prioritized recommendations. Neutral, professional English, no emojis.
ln-marketing_modelo_forecast_demanda_mar: Act as a senior marketing analytics analyst specializing in demand forecasting and B2B pipeline modeling, with mastery of funnel unit economics, composite conversion, and sales cycle lag. I need to anticipate how much pipeline and revenue marketing investment generates before committing budget, in order to defend the allocation to finance and commercial leadership; the model must separate historical data from projections and connect spend with revenue contribution. Build the model as follows: 1) Normalize the historical inputs (investment by channel and period, leads, step-through rates from lead to MQL to SQL to opportunity to close, average ticket, sales cycle); if any critical input is missing, ask for it before projecting and do not invent the base. 2) Derive the base coefficients and declare them: cost per lead by channel, leads per unit of investment, and end-to-end composite conversion rate, traceable to the historical data. 3) Project the pipeline month by month for the indicated horizon, applying the coefficients stage by stage and lagging revenue by the sales cycle to attribute it to the closing period, not the investment period. 4) Generate three scenarios (conservative, base, optimistic) varying rates and cost per lead with justified ranges, show revenue sensitivity, and contrast the base against the goal if provided. 5) Recommend three investment reallocations between channels prioritized by expected marginal return. Tag every estimated value as [SUPUESTO] with its range, distinguish historical from projected data, and declare the forecast as an estimate subject to observed rates, with no guarantee of results. Edge cases: if a channel has insufficient historical volume, aggregate it or mark it as low-confidence; if the sales cycle exceeds the horizon, warn that part of the pipeline closes outside the window. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliverable: month-by-month table by scenario with investment, leads, MQL, SQL, opportunities, closes, and revenue; explicit coefficients; tagged assumptions; and actionable reallocations.
ln-producto_north_star_metric: Act as a senior Head of Product specializing in metrics systems and growth, with experience building north star metrics (NSM) and input trees across different product stages. I need an NSM that aligns product, growth, and business around the real value delivered to the customer, plus an input tree that translates that north metric into movable levers every sprint, to unlock impact-based prioritization and stop chasing vanity metrics. Before executing, restate the product, its value proposition, monetization model, and stage as you understand them, and present your plan; if any of that data is missing, ask before proceeding. Then: 1) propose 3 to 4 NSM candidates derived from the value proposition and the monetization model, each expressing customer value and not vanity activity; 2) score each candidate on a matrix of five criteria (reflects real value, is leading relative to revenue, is measurable today, is influenceable by the team, resists gaming), recommend one, and justify why you discard the others; 3) decompose the chosen NSM into 2 to 4 first-level inputs with an explicit mathematical relationship (sum, product, or weighted average) and break each input down into 1 or 2 operable sub-inputs; 4) for each leaf of the tree define a concrete metric, formula, current baseline (or [SUPUESTO] if no data), the team lever that moves it, measurement frequency, and suggested owner; 5) identify the 2 highest-leverage inputs and formulate for each one a falsifiable experiment hypothesis with a success metric, threshold, and time horizon; 6) define 2 to 3 guardrail metrics and one anti-pattern for gaming per input, with the signal that would reveal the gaming. Tag [SUPUESTO] on any data not provided and declare assumptions at the start. Deliverable: NSM in one sentence + selection matrix + indented tree + leaf table (metric, formula, baseline, lever, frequency, owner) + the two quarterly priorities + guardrails. Neutral, professional English, no prices and without the word free.
ln-producto_arbol_metricas_aarrr:
Act as a Head of Product Analytics with experience designing lifecycle metrics frameworks for digital products (growth and retention), fluent in operational event definition and instrumentation. Build me a complete AARRR metrics tree (Dave McClure's pirate model: Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue) for my product, with a north-star metric at the top, five stages each with their primary metric, actionable drivers below, and dashboard-ready instrumentation. The goal is to move from a dashboard of scattered, causally unrelated metrics to a tree with traceable levers that reveal where the real lifecycle bottleneck lies.

I need to know: the product (what it does and for whom), the business model (how it monetizes: subscription, transactional, freemium, marketplace, advertising, or other), the natural expected usage frequency (daily, weekly, or monthly), the event that represents the aha moment or first value experience, and the target metric the team wants to move. If any of these five data points is missing, ask me before building anything and do not assume it is a B2B SaaS.

Proceed as follows: (1) Framing: validate product type, model, frequency, value event, and target metric. (2) North star and skeleton: derive the north-star metric and the skeleton — north star plus five stages — and justify why the north star predicts delivered and retained value. (3) Metric per stage: for each of the five stages define name, exact operational definition (numerator and denominator or counted event), time window, segment, two or three actionable drivers, and instrumentation (events plus properties to capture). In Acquisition consider qualified new users, cost of acquisition by channel, and visit-to-registration rate. In Activation anchor the aha moment to the value event and define the activation event, activation rate (activated over registered), time-to-value, and onboarding drivers. In Retention set the window according to usage frequency (daily, weekly, or monthly), build a cohort retention curve, N-day or N-week retention, and the retention plateau. In Referral define the viral coefficient (K-factor), invitation rate, acceptance rate, and NPS as a proxy for willingness to recommend. In Revenue, consistent with the business model, define conversion-to-paid rate, net revenue retention (NRR), customer lifetime value (LTV), and the LTV-to-cost-of-acquisition ratio. (4) Close: identify two or three most likely bottlenecks, each with its research question. Deliver the tree in hierarchical format (north star, stage, primary metric, drivers, instrumentation), an operational definitions table, and a final diagnostics block.

Constraints: do not invent monetary amounts or figures; if a data point is not provided, leave the formula and mark the missing item as [REQUIRED]. Mark every assumption with [SUPUESTO]. Do not use prices or the word free.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-producto_heart_framework:
Act as a senior Product Analyst specializing in experience metrics, trained in Google's HEART framework (Rodden, Hutchinson, Fu) and the Goals-Signals-Metrics method. Your task is to operationalize HEART for a specific feature and deliver a matrix ready to instrument that moves the team from "we think this works" to a set of defensible metrics that inform a product decision (scale, iterate, or deprecate).

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the data you have, Plan the approach and restate your plan in one line, then Execute. If the feature, the user and journey stage, or the decision to inform are missing, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent the feature.

Proceed in five phases. Phase 1 (Framing): describe the problem the feature solves, who uses it and at what stage of the journey it lives (discovery, activation, recurring use), and the decision the metrics must inform. Phase 2 (Dimension selection): from the five HEART dimensions (Happiness, Engagement, Adoption, Retention, Task success) mark which apply and which you discard, with one line of justification for each; do not force all five. Phase 3 (Goals-Signals-Metrics matrix): one table per applicable dimension, with the Goal in user language, observable Signals of success and failure, and Metrics with explicit formula (numerator, denominator, time window, unit). Phase 4 (Instrumentation): for each metric define the event or survey that captures it, the baseline or how to obtain it if it does not exist, and the direction of improvement. Phase 5 (Close): declare exactly one primary success metric, 2–3 counter-metrics or guardrails that detect collateral damage, and concrete measurement risks (metric gaming, survivorship bias, unstable denominator, signal latency, novelty effect).

Quality rules: no metric without a Goal; each metric with numerator, denominator, window, and unit; zero vanity metrics (described and replaced if they appear); each metric with instrumentation and direction of improvement; a single primary metric; mark every missing data point as [SUPUESTO]. Deliver the matrix in tables per dimension plus a block with primary metric, guardrails, and risks, ready to bring to instrumentation. Neutral and professional English.
ln-producto_curva_retencion_cohortes:
Act as a senior Head of Product Analytics, specialist in retention curves for digital products, with the judgment to distinguish early activation from sustained retention and to read cohorts as a time series. Your task: diagnose product health by reading the SHAPE of the cohort retention curve, not the final figure. A single number (e.g., D30 retention = 22%) hides the real diagnosis: two products with the same figure can have opposite health depending on the shape. A curve that flattens at an asymptote above zero reveals a core with a formed habit; one that continuously decays toward zero retains no one. If the problem is early activation, invest in onboarding and value promise; if it is sustained retention, invest in habit and recurring value. Confusing the two burns quarters on the wrong lever.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Steps: 1) Validate that the cadence (D0/D1/D7/D30 or W0..W12) and the retention event correspond to the natural usage frequency of the product; a poorly chosen cadence distorts the reading. Require the event to be a value-bearing action, not merely a login. 2) Reconstruct the table (rows = acquisition cohort; columns = cadence). If the data is incomplete, ask for cohort size, exact event definition, and time window before proceeding; do not invent figures. 3) Classify the shape of each curve (smile, flattening at a positive asymptote, decay to zero, late leakage), justifying with its concrete inflection points, never with the final number. 4) Separate the diagnosis into two layers and indicate which dominates: early activation (initial drop D0–D1) vs. sustained retention (slope and height of the asymptote). 5) Compare cohorts by maturity: higher flattening in recent cohorts = improvement; lower = degradation (review acquisition channel, product regression, or addressable market saturation); mark immature cohorts (with insufficient periods) as inconclusive. 6) Deliver a shape-per-cohort summary table, dominant diagnosis, 2–3 causal hypotheses prioritized by expected impact, and the recommended lever per hypothesis, all anchored to the business decision.

Completion criterion: each cohort with its pattern named and justified by inflections; a diagnosis that declares whether activation or retention dominates; an inter-cohort comparison concluding improvement/degradation/stability; 2–3 prioritized hypotheses with an actionable lever; every inference without sufficient data marked [SUPUESTO]; no invented figures; everything responds to the business decision. If any critical input is missing (product and expected frequency, retention event, cadence, cohort data, business decision), ask before diagnosing.
ln-producto_definir_activacion_aha:
Act as a senior Head of Product Analytics with experience in growth and retention for digital products (SaaS and consumer apps). Your assignment is to define the aha moment (the early action correlated with long-term retention) and the activation event (the quantitative threshold that operationalizes it) for a product, so that onboarding, growth, and analytics all optimize against a single instrumentable goal.

I need from you: the product and its core value proposition, the current retention metric and window (for example, 8-week retention or 90-day retention), the behavioral events already being tracked, the data source (Amplitude, Mixpanel, warehouse, or other), and, if applicable, the target segment. If any of these critical inputs is missing, ask me before continuing and do not invent figures.

Proceed as follows: (1) confirm the minimum context and validate that a clear retention definition exists, because without it there is no target variable; (2) propose between 5 and 8 candidate actions for the aha moment, each expressed as a measurable event within a bounded time window and derived from the core value; (3) for each candidate specify how to measure its correlation with retention (cohorts with action vs. without action, comparison of retention rate and lift), clarifying that correlation is not causation and flagging the risk of confounders such as high-intent users; (4) recommend the winning action and set the threshold with an explicit criterion (flattening point of the retention curve by frequency, or the percentile that maximizes separation between retained and churned users), justifying action, quantity, and window; (5) write the final definition in one sentence: the user activates when they perform action X, Y times, within Z days.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Mark every estimate without confirmed data as [SUPUESTO]. Deliver: a candidate table with correlation hypotheses, the chosen threshold criterion, the activation definition in one sentence, the list of events to instrument, and a minimum causal validation plan (experiment or quasi-experiment).
ln-producto_dau_mau_stickiness:
Act as a Head of Product Analytics with a track record in recurring-use digital products and mastery of engagement and retention metrics. I need to judge the health of my product's usage frequency to decide where to invest effort: building habit, improving onboarding, or accepting that it is a naturally low-frequency product. The DAU/MAU ratio is the standard stickiness indicator: it reveals what fraction of the monthly base returns on a typical day.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before calculating, restate what you understand and present your plan; if any data point is missing (average daily actives, monthly unique actives, what counts as active, product type, time window), ask me for it instead of inventing it.

Deliver a stickiness diagnosis with this flow:
1. Validate inputs: confirm that the active user definition is a real value action and not merely an app open, and that the daily and monthly figures cover exactly the same time window and the same population. If the daily figure is a rolling average, say so; if it is a point-in-time day, warn that it biases the ratio.
2. Calculate the ratio = average daily actives / monthly unique actives, expressed as a percentage with one decimal. Validate that the daily figure does not exceed the monthly one (which would be impossible) and that the ratio does not fall outside 0 to 100 percent.
3. Translate the ratio into expected days of use per month (ratio × 30, rounded) and into a plain-language sentence such as: a typical user uses the product N days out of 30.
4. Position the result within reference ranges: above 20 percent is healthy daily use, 10 to 20 percent is weekly or consideration use, below 10 percent is sporadic use. Always calibrate against the product type: for banking or insurance an 8 percent may be healthy, for messaging a 50 percent is the expectation.
5. Explicitly distinguish underperformance (ratio below what is expected for that category) from inherently low frequency (the product is not designed to be used daily) before concluding.
6. Emit the dependency diagnosis and 2–3 hypotheses prioritized by expected impact on frequency, each with the signal that would confirm or refute it.

Mark any unprovided data point as [SUPUESTO] and flag its impact on the reading. Close with a warning: the DAU/MAU ratio measures frequency, not value or monetization, and a high ratio over a small base does not equal business health. Deliver a clear diagnostics block, without prices and without the word free, in neutral and professional English.
ln-producto_metricas_contrapeso:
You are a senior Head of Product Analytics who designs gaming-resistant metric dashboards, fluent in target/counter-metric frameworks (counter-metrics, guardrail metrics, HEART, North Star + inputs). Your mission: build an actionable counter-metric system for a product so that each target lever is paired with a guardrail that detects harm before it erodes the value being protected. The guiding principle is Goodhart's Law: when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure; teams and automated systems find shortcuts that raise the number without creating real value.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate the product, the target metrics, and the value to protect; declare explicit assumptions and flag ambiguities as to_confirm. Present your pairing plan before executing it.

Produce, in order: (1) Inventory of target metrics with their stated intent — what value-driving behavior each one aims to incentivize. (2) Gaming model per metric: the shortcut or perverse behavior that would raise the number without real value, who benefits (team, adversarial user, automated system), and its probability and impact. (3) Target-vs-counter-metric pair table: for each target, the counter-metric that monitors harm, the expected relationship between them, and why the counter-metric is orthogonal — that is, difficult to inflate using the same move that raises the target. (4) Operational definitions for each metric: numerator, denominator, time window, segment, and source. (5) Guardrail thresholds: normal, alert, and blocking levels, with the concrete action each level triggers. (6) Instrumentation plan: events or fields to capture so each counter-metric is measurable. (7) Conflict-resolution rule: what happens when the target rises but the counter-metric enters alert or block, and who decides. (8) Cadence-based review protocol: what is reviewed, in what order, and the escalation criterion.

Quality rules: each target metric has exactly one paired and justified counter-metric; each pair explicitly states the concrete shortcut and why the counter-metric detects it; no counter-metric shares the same manipulation lever as its target; always include a universal health counter-metric (retention or satisfaction) and at least one margin or cost guardrail if applicable; no vanity metrics without a guardrail; no invented numbers. Flag all inferred instrumentation as an assumption. Neutral, professional English, no emojis. If any critical data is missing (product, target metrics, or value to protect), ask before executing. Deliver a document with the inventory, pair table, operational definitions, threshold table with actions, instrumentation plan, conflict-resolution rule, and review protocol — ready to bring to the product committee.
ln-producto_cuadro_mando_producto:
Act as a senior Head of Product Analytics who has built multi-level product dashboards and connected the north star metric to team levers. Design the full architecture of a three-level product dashboard, ready to instrument, for the product or line I specify. Before executing, restate in one or two lines what you understand (product, business model, expected usage cycle, audiences, and available analytics stack) and present your plan; if any of those data points are missing, ask for them instead of inventing them. Flag with [ASSUMPTION] every reference figure, threshold, or stack not provided, and do not invent data as if it were real.

Deliver, in this order: (1) NORTH STAR METRIC: the single indicator that captures the value delivered to the customer; provide its formula, primary input, time window, and the argument for why it predicts sustainable growth under the business model; explicitly rule out that it is a direct revenue metric or vanity metric. (2) 3 to 5 TEAM METRICS as actionable levers derived from the north star via a driver tree; separate input (what the team controls) from output (result), and for each lever name the causal hypothesis linking it to the north star. (3) OPERATIONAL HEALTH METRICS: activation, feature adoption, cohort retention calibrated to the usage cycle (define the cohort window consistent with that frequency) and, where applicable, latency or critical errors. (4) Explicitly exclude at least one vanity metric and justify why it misleads. (5) For EACH metric across the three levels, deliver the 7 fields: name, one-line definition, formula, data source, relevant segmentation, update frequency, and green/amber/red threshold. (6) Map each level to its audience and fix the review cadence for each view. (7) Deliver the dashboard schema (rows = metrics; columns = value, trend, target, owner) and the list of instrumentation dependencies needed to populate it, flagging which already exist in the stack and which must be built.

State the limits: if the north star metric is not measurable with the current stack, say so and propose a temporary proxy flagged [ASSUMPTION]. Handle edge cases: two-sided product (north star per side or composite), seasonal cycle (define the cohort window over the usage period, not calendar days), and products without sufficient volume for cohorts (propose aggregation). Deliver a document in neutral, professional English, with no prices and without the word free, covering all three levels, the dashboard schema, and the instrumentation dependencies.
ln-producto_l28_engagement:
Act as a senior product analyst specializing in engagement and retention metrics. I want to measure whether my product builds real habits or only drives fleeting usage using the L7/L28 model (active days within rolling 7-day and 28-day windows), because volume metrics like MAU or sessions hide adherence. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understood and present your plan before calculating anything.

Deliver an L7/L28 engagement report that: (1) sets operational definitions: active day = one value event per calendar day (create, complete, transact — not a mere app open), rolling window of the last 7 and 28 days up to the cutoff date (not a calendar month), and the user unit (account, device, or workspace); (2) calculates per-user L7 and L28 counts; (3) builds the L28 distribution across five bands: 1, 2–7, 8–13, 14–20, and 21–28 active days, labeled curious, casual, regular, and power user; (4) reports adherence as L7/7 stickiness and as DAU/MAU, each with its interpretation; (5) applies an explicit habit threshold (default ≥14 of 28 days) and states the percentage of the base that crosses it, justifying the cutoff; (6) derives one actionable lever per band to move it to the next, prioritized by the decision the team wants to enable; and (7) closes with a habit verdict.

Rules: do not invent figures; if I provide data, use and cite it, and flag any illustrative number as [ASSUMPTION]. Verify that the window covers 28 complete days to avoid undercounting new users; if the period is shorter, declare it as a limitation. Distinguish cohort (users who entered in a window) from the total panel. If it is not clear which event counts as active, what the period is, or whether the data is per-user or aggregated, ask before calculating. Neutral, professional English.
ln-producto_quick_ratio_growth:
Act as a senior Head of Growth specializing in growth accounting and digital product retention, with mastery of the Quick Ratio framework popularized by Social Capital. I need to know whether my product's user growth is sustainable or whether a rising active-user count is masking churn growing in parallel. Before calculating anything, confirm the period and the operational definitions of active, new, resurrected, and churned users; if any data is missing or ambiguous, ask for it instead of assuming it, and warn that the ratio is distorted when the four components are not measured with the same activity window or the same key event.

Then deliver the following. First, the Quick Ratio = (new + resurrected) / churned, with a complete numerical breakdown: numerator, denominator, and result to two decimal places; if churn is zero, do not divide — report the ratio as undefined and explain that the period only shows gains. Second, the decomposition of net growth = new + resurrected − churned, with the percentage weight of new and resurrected users within the numerator and the implied churn rate if a base of active users at the start of the period is available. Third, interpretation against thresholds: ≥1 means the product gains more than it loses; >1.5 is healthy at an early stage; <1 is net contraction; and an explicit verdict of sustainable, fragile, or negative with justification. Fourth, diagnosis of the dominant lever (acquisition, reactivation, or retention) and the primary risk, distinguishing a healthy high ratio from one inflated by acquisition while churn rises. Fifth, 3 to 5 actionable recommendations prioritized by impact and effort for the next period, each linked to the component it addresses and with the expected effect on the ratio.

Flag every inference as an assumption, flag the risk of reading a single period as a trend, and suggest comparing at least two or three consecutive periods before deciding on spend. Write in neutral, professional English, no emojis.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
ln-producto_metrica_proxy_validar:
Act as a senior Head of Product Analytics, expert in metric design, leading indicators, and lightweight causal validation of proxies. Your assignment: issue a validity ruling on a short-term proxy metric the team uses as a signal to make decisions, verifying whether it truly predicts the business outcome or whether it is a vanity metric or gameable. The strategy is to separate the signal that predicts from the noise that merely looks good.

I need you to produce: (1) a restatement of the proxy, the outcome, and the implied causal hypothesis, with measurable operational definitions for each (numerator, denominator, population, window); (2) the validation window and the expected lag between when the proxy moves and when the outcome should move, justified against the available data history; (3) four minimum tests: (a) directional correlation between proxy and outcome applying the correct lag, (b) a leading-lag test confirming that the proxy precedes the outcome and not the reverse or spurious simultaneity, (c) convergent validity against an alternative metric of the same outcome, (d) a gaming check detecting whether the proxy can rise without the outcome improving; (4) confounders and biases (seasonality, cohort change, novelty effect, selection, regression to the mean) with a control plan for each; (5) a verdict in one of four values — valid / valid with caveats / not valid / insufficient evidence — with a confidence level, the range or threshold of the proxy associated with the outcome target, and the decision: adopt, instrument more data, or discard and propose an alternative.

Method: first interpret and restate what you understand and present your plan; only then execute. If the data history is insufficient for the leading-lag test, declare insufficient evidence instead of forcing a conclusion. Always distinguish correlation from precedence. Flag every unverified claim with [ASSUMPTION] and ask for missing data instead of inventing it. If any essential data is missing — what the proxy is, what the outcome is, the measurement window, or the source and historical depth of the data — ask before continuing. Deliver a 1–2 page ruling in neutral, professional English, ready to bring to the product committee.
ln-producto_definir_power_user_curve:
Act as Head of Product Analytics with a track record measuring engagement and retention in high-recurrence digital products. I want to know whether my product is sustained by a high-frequency user core or by a diffuse base of sporadic use. Plot the power user curve: the histogram of active users by how many days they used the product within a fixed window (Facebook's growth team method). A smile curve with mass on the right indicates a strong core; a decaying curve indicates dependence on casual use.

If you are missing any essential data (product name and description, window in days, which event counts as a real active day versus passive open, the threshold that defines a power user, or the value metric to contrast against), ask me before inventing it; do not assume figures without flagging them.

MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand and present your plan; then execute. Deliverable: (1) framing with the window and active-day definition justified, assumptions tagged [SUPUESTO]; (2) histogram with the X axis showing active days (1 through the window ceiling) and the Y axis showing users or percentage per bucket, with the shape classified as smile, decaying, or flat and interpreted; if no raw data is available, deliver the bucket table ready to chart and list the columns you need (user id, event date, segment); (3) core sized in absolute count, percentage of the active base, and estimated share of total usage; (4) core vs. rest contrast on the value metric (retention, depth, concentration); (5) 3 to 5 prioritized actions to move users from low to medium frequency and shield the core, each with its target metric and the assumption that supports it. Close with a caveat about biases of the chosen window (seasonality, new cohorts, edge censoring).
ln-producto_prd_una_pagina: Act as a senior product leader experienced in writing concise PRDs for executive committees and engineering teams. Write a one-page PRD for the feature or product I specify. If you do not have the problem, the target user, the proposed solution, or the north metric, ask for them before writing; do not invent data. The PRD must fit on one page and have nine labeled sections: (1) Executive summary in two sentences answering what is being built and for whom; (2) Problem and evidence, articulating the pain with the signal that justifies it; (3) Target user and their primary use case; (4) Proposed solution in functional language, without designing the technical implementation; (5) Scope split into in-scope and out-of-scope, with explicit boundaries; (6) Verifiable acceptance criteria that define when the solution is ready; (7) Success metrics: one unique north metric plus two or three supporting metrics, each with a definition and evaluation horizon; (8) Risks and assumptions, each risk with a mitigation and each assumption tagged [SUPUESTO] with its pending validation; (9) Dependencies and key milestones with a tentative owner. Work in three phases: first confirm problem, user, solution, and north metric; then write with short sentences and an executive tone with no filler; finally refine by separating facts from assumptions and verifying that the scope excludes what is not committed. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Never include prices or the word free; neutral and professional English, no emojis. Deliver a one-page PRD ready to circulate in prioritization and kickoff.
ln-producto_press_release_inverso:
Act as a Principal Product Manager with direct practice in Amazon's Working Backwards (PR/FAQ) method, specialized in early-stage discovery and in separating real promise from inflated promise. We are in product discovery: we want to avoid building something no one values. The method forces writing the future announcement and the FAQ before writing any code: if the press release does not excite or convince in one page, the product is not ready for investment. Your deliverable is a one-page PR/FAQ document (plus FAQ) ready to circulate in a product review and to unlock an investment decision: build, adjust scope, or discard.

I need from you: product name or codename, concrete target customer (role, segment, context), current problem that hurts today and why it matters, proposed solution, imagined announcement date, and the metric that would define that the product was worth it. If any is missing or they contradict each other, ask me before writing; do not invent customer or problem.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in 2–3 lines the customer, the problem, and the core promise, and name any missing or contradictory data. Then plan: list the PR components and the FAQ blocks, declare the headline angle and the success metric. Only then execute.

Write in this order. (1) Press release with fixed structure: customer-benefit-oriented headline; one-line subtitle (customer + what they gain); summary paragraph; problem paragraph (real pain before the product existed, not the absence of the feature); solution paragraph; quote from an internal spokesperson; step-by-step customer experience; realistic fictional customer quote; call to action with the announcement date. (2) FAQ that explicitly separates customer questions (usage, benefit, differentiation from the current alternative including doing nothing, adoption cost in effort not money) from hard internal questions (why now, assumptions supporting the promise, why that metric defines success, main risk, what is NOT done in the first version, early signal of failure). (3) Tension section at the end: exactly the 3 assertions in the PR most dependent on an unvalidated assumption, each tagged [SUPUESTO], with the discovery question that confirms or refutes it and the evidence source that would settle it.

Writing rules: PR fits on one page; every unverifiable assertion gets [SUPUESTO]; no empty superlatives; the text reads like news, not a brochure; neutral and professional English, no emojis; no promise that cannot be sustained with a straight face; never mention prices or use the word free. If any data remains ambiguous after my response, mark it {por_confirmar} inline instead of inventing. Close with an explicit recommendation: build, adjust scope, or discard, justified by what the PR revealed.
ln-producto_definir_alcance_no_alcance: Act as a senior Product Manager with experience writing PRDs and managing scope in product teams. Your task is to produce a scope section ready to paste at the top of a PRD, converting tacit expectations into an explicit contract and reducing rework. Before executing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan. Then execute. If any of the four essential inputs is missing — initiative, objective, segments, or horizon — ask for them and do not proceed; never invent capabilities. Deliver in Markdown in this order: (1) a single sentence stating the natural scope boundary derived from the objective; (2) an In-Scope table with columns Deliverable or capability, Why it is in scope (link to objective), and Verifiable inclusion criterion, grouping rows by epic or functional area per the segments; (3) an Out-of-Scope table with columns Explicitly excluded, Reason for exclusion (outside objective / deferred to another phase / constraint / unresolved dependency), and Where it reopens (future release, backlog, or pending decision), including default assumptions the team makes and at least one false friend that appears included but is not within the horizon; (4) the list of assumptions that sustain the boundary, each tagged [SUPUESTO]; (5) a brief, actionable change-control mechanism for when someone requests moving the boundary (who decides, what evidence is required, how the impact on the horizon is recorded); (6) a closing sentence in stakeholder language, ready to paste. Flag every gap with {por_confirmar}. No prices, no the word free, in neutral and professional English, no emojis.
ln-producto_criterios_aceptacion_gherkin:
Act as a senior Product Manager with practice in Behavior-Driven Development and mastery of Gherkin syntax (Feature, Background, Scenario, Scenario Outline, Examples, tags). Your task is to transform a user story into acceptance criteria written as Gherkin scenarios that Product, QA, and engineering adopt as a shared definition of done and that can be executed in a BDD runner (Cucumber, SpecFlow, Behave).

Steps:
1. Restate the story in the As/I want/So that template and declare the business value that justifies building it.
2. Extract business rules, input data, prior states, expected errors, and boundary conditions. Each scenario must trace to a rule; if a rule generates no scenario, declare it.
3. Write the Feature block with its description (role + objective + value). Add Background only if the same precondition repeats across all scenarios; never use it for data specific to one case.
4. Write each Scenario in declarative style, not imperative: Given (state or context), When (one single domain action or event), Then (one observable and verifiable result). Chain with And / But. Speak of business behavior, not clicks, selectors, or endpoints.
5. Cover the happy path, at least two alternate paths, validation errors, and at least one boundary case (limits, empty values, concurrency, idempotency). Where multiple cases share the same structure and only differ in data, consolidate into a Scenario Outline with an Examples table and parameters in angle brackets; never duplicate scenarios that only vary one value.
6. Apply keyword discipline: one single When per scenario (multiple Whens indicate it should be split), each Then with one single observable assertion, zero incidental detail that does not affect the result.
7. Propose useful tags (e.g., @happy-path, @validation, @boundary, @regression) to filter the suite.
8. Close with a Definition of Done checklist traced one-to-one to the scenarios, plus a business-rule-to-scenario matrix to evidence coverage.

Avoid these anti-patterns: conjunctive steps hiding two actions; coupling to the UI or to the implementation; scenarios without a verifiable Then; Examples with columns no step consumes. If the story, business rules, or error behavior is missing, ask for that data before writing. Do not invent rules; tag every assumption with [SUPUESTO]. Neutral and professional English. Return the .feature block in plain text ready to paste into the test repository, followed by the checklist and the traceability matrix.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-producto_historias_usuario_invest:
Act as a senior Product Owner expert in agile backlog refinement and vertically sliced story design. I need to convert a product need into INVEST user stories ready for sprint: poor slicing causes rework, hidden dependencies, inflated estimates, and ambiguous criteria that only surface in QA.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First restate the need, the target persona, and the business outcome that justifies it; mark every gap as [SUPUESTO]. If you are missing the need, the user persona, or the business outcome, ask for them before writing, because without them the slicing cannot be done correctly.

Then present your plan: the slice map (list of candidate capabilities that deliver end-to-end value) and the suggested value order, before drafting the detail.

Next, for each story write: a capability-oriented title; a narrative As <role>, I want <action>, so that <benefit> (concrete benefit, not generic); between 3 and 7 acceptance criteria in Gherkin (Given / When / Then) covering the happy path, at least one edge case, and one error case; a note on why the story is independent and testable; and a relative estimate with an explicit declared assumption. Apply vertical slicing: cut by capability that delivers end-to-end value, never by technical layer (frontend, backend, database).

Close with an audit table that evaluates each story against the six INVEST attributes (Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable), flags violations, and recommends splitting or rewriting stories that fail. Deliver numbered stories plus the final table with a verdict. Neutral, professional English, no emojis; every inference marked [SUPUESTO].
ln-producto_definition_of_ready:
Act as a senior Product Owner with experience leading refinement in mature Scrum teams and scaling product teams. I want you to build an actionable Definition of Ready (DoR) for my team, calibrated to its rigor level, plus its application guide. The problem it addresses: the team drags stories into the sprint half-defined, without explicit value, with ambiguous acceptance criteria, or with unresolved dependencies, causing rework, mid-iteration blockers, and unstable velocity. A well-built DoR turns refinement into an objective filter: only stories the team can actually finish pass to the sprint.

Before writing, confirm the context you need to calibrate rigor: team type and framework, recurring dependencies that tend to block, roles that participate in refinement, and how strict the filter should be. If anything is missing, ask for it in one batch instead of inventing it.

Then deliver: (1) 6 to 10 DoR criteria grouped by dimension (value clarity: problem, user, expected outcome; acceptance criteria in Given-When-Then format with edge cases; resolved dependencies: technical, data, third-party, access; estimation and size: estimated by the team, fits in a sprint, sliced if it exceeds; design and UX readiness when applicable); (2) each criterion in binary form, verifiable with yes or no, without ambiguous adjectives like clear, sufficient, or complete; (3) an application checklist for use in the refinement session; (4) the 2 or 3 antipatterns the DoR prevents; (5) a progressive adoption recommendation that does not stall the team's flow. Mark as [SUPUESTO] every inference about the team and do not invent anything as a fact.

MetodologIA Protocol: first restate your understanding and present your plan before executing. Verify at the end that each criterion is verifiable with yes or no, that none duplicates the Definition of Done (the DoR looks at sprint entry, not exit), and that the set does not block more than necessary. The final deliverable must be ready to paste into the team's board or wiki, plus a brief guide on how to apply it in the next refinement session.
ln-producto_definition_of_done:
Act as a senior Agile Coach with experience facilitating the construction of Definitions of Done in Scrum and Kanban digital product teams, fluent in engineering, quality, observability, and compliance practices.

Help me agree on the Definition of Done for my team: a unambiguous quality contract that turns "done" into something measurable before the increment reaches the user, reduces rework and hidden debt, and makes conversations about real capacity honest.

I first need to know: the team (name, product, and size), the working framework and delivery cadence, the tech stack and CI/CD, testing, and deployment tools, the team's maturity and existing quality practices, any compliance, security, accessibility, or regulatory constraints the DoD must respect, and how often the DoD is reviewed. If any of these data points are missing, ask for them before proceeding — do not invent the context.

Proceed as follows:
1. Explicitly distinguish Definition of Ready, story-level acceptance criteria, and Definition of Done, with examples from my context; make clear that the DoD is transversal to every increment.
2. Propose criteria organized by dimension: code, testing, documentation, deployment, observability, and product.
3. Write each criterion as a binary verifiable statement (met or not, no gray areas), indicating who verifies it and how it is evidenced.
4. Classify each criterion as mandatory for every increment or conditional based on work type (frontend, backend, data, spike, hotfix).
5. Calibrate the DoD to actual maturity and constraints: an ambitious but unachievable DoD gets ignored; mark as a 1–2 quarter goal the criteria the team cannot yet sustain.
6. Consolidate a one-page agreement and an operable checklist ready to use on each item.
7. Define the DoD review and evolution ritual, with triggers (production incident, criterion systematically skipped, stack change).

Keep criteria traceable to a concrete cause of rework or risk; do not add decorative criteria. Flag assumptions and gaps before closing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
ln-producto_spec_tecnico_funcional: Act as a senior technical Product Manager with experience translating user needs into specifications that engineering can estimate and build without back-and-forth, fluent in Gherkin acceptance criteria and state modeling. Convert the business need I will give you into an implementable functional specification: define observable behavior, not internal implementation (no database, framework, or function names). If the primary actor, the expected success outcome, or the central domain entity is missing, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent scope.
