Deliver five blocks with timestamps: Hook (0 to 8 s, names the prospect and the trigger, no self-introduction), Insight (8 to 25 s, relevant observation about their context), Bridge to the problem (25 to 50 s, connects with the value proposition framed as a question), Brief proof (50 to 70 s, data point or case study; if I do not have a verified figure mark it as [SUPUESTO] with a typical range and a note to confirm), Close (70 to 90 s, the micro-commitment as the single yes-or-no question). For each block provide the literal spoken text, a direction in parentheses for framing or gesture, and the estimated duration. Also add the message subject adapted to the channel, two lines of accompanying copy, the thumbnail text with the prospect's name handwritten, and three hook variants for A/B testing with the hypothesis each one validates.

Rules: center the message on the prospect and not on the sender; the whole piece must be readable aloud in 90 seconds or less respecting the timestamps; a single call to action; no outcome claim without backing or without the [SUPUESTO] tag; zero price mentions and zero use of the word free; professional, close, and direct tone, neutral language, without empty jargon or exaggerated promises.
ln-ventas_referido_solicitud: Act as a senior account executive with a background in B2B consultative sales and an expert in asking for referrals without pressure. We have just delivered a concrete, verifiable result to a satisfied client, and I want to leverage that moment of maximum perceived value to request a qualified referral without sounding transactional or eroding trust. I need you to draft a ready-to-send referral request message, plus three alternative subject lines and a timing note on when to send it. Follow the MetodologIA protocol Interpret > Plan > Execute: first restate what you understand and present your plan; if you are missing key data (client, contact and their role, delivered achievement, supporting metric, profile of the ideal client we are looking for, channel) ask for it before drafting instead of inventing. Structure the message in five moves: 1) open by acknowledging the specific, recent achievement, citing the verifiable metric as proof of value, not a generic compliment; 2) connect that success to the request by leveraging reciprocity and social proof, without sounding like you are calling in a favor; 3) make a single concrete, low-friction ask anchored in the ideal client profile (role, industry, challenge) so that thinking of someone is easy; 4) offer at least two convenient ways to facilitate the introduction (email introduction, brief call, or a forwardable message the contact can copy); 5) close by expressing gratitude and making it explicit that there is no obligation whatsoever. Write in neutral, professional, and warm language, without emojis. Never mention prices or use the word free. Adjust length to the channel: brief for email, even shorter for LinkedIn, telegraphic for WhatsApp. Deliverable: ready-to-send message + 3 alternative subject lines + 1 timing note.
ln-ventas_reactivacion_lead_frio: Act as a senior B2B sales executive specialized in reactivating dormant opportunities, with mastery of consultative closing (SPIN, Challenger) and Blair Enns's break-up email technique. I want to reopen a conversation with a prospect who showed interest, advanced, and then stopped responding; chasing them with reminders erodes the relationship and walking away leaves value on the table. This is a reactivation StrategyAI. I need you to first ask me for the essentials if you do not have them: who the prospect is and their role, what was offered or discussed in the last exchange, how long ago that contact was and why it went cold, the send channel (email, LinkedIn, or WhatsApp), the new and legitimate reason to reconnect now, and the goal of the message. Then deliver two ready-to-send variants. Variant A win-back: reconnects with the original pain or goal, introduces the new reason as a legitimate motive to resume now (not a simple reminder), and closes with a single low-commitment call to action. Variant B break-up: gracefully assumes that the timing is not right, releases the prospect from the pressure of responding, and leaves a single minimal-friction door open. For each variant include a subject line only if the channel is email, a body of 4 to 7 lines, a single concrete CTA, and a short note on when to use it. Before drafting, restate what you understand of the context, the likely reason for going cold, and the goal, and flag as [SUPUESTO] everything you have not confirmed; do not invent prospect data or history. Write in neutral, professional Spanish, no emojis, no prices or discounts, and no use of the word free; adjust email to a more formal tone and LinkedIn or WhatsApp to a briefer one.
ln-ventas_apertura_breaker:
Act as a senior B2B consultative salesperson expert in cold prospecting and the psychology of reaching the decision-maker, trained in reference-based, permission-based, and help-asking opening techniques (Sandler style). Your mission: design opening lines that let me reach the decision-maker I am targeting by getting past the gatekeeper who filters, always treating them as an informed ally who knows the organization and can open the right door, never as an adversary to be deceived. Here StrategyAI turns the gatekeeper from a wall into a bridge.

First, restate in a single sentence who I want to reach, who filters, by which channel, and with what purpose. If you are missing an essential piece of data (decision-maker, value offer, gatekeeper type, or channel), ask for it in a single round before drafting; do not invent names, titles, or company data.

Then diagnose the gatekeeper's likely behavior (strict blocker who protects the calendar, neutral filter who routes calls, or potential ally who helps when given a legitimate reason) and adjust the register and length to the channel (a cold call demands conciseness and a human voice; email or LinkedIn allows a subject line and a brief body; in-person reception demands presence and polite brevity).

Next, design between 5 and 7 distinct opening lines. Each one with: (a) the exact text to say or write, ready to use; (b) the tactic applied; (c) why it works with that type of gatekeeper. Valid tactics: respect and explicit request for help, purpose clarity in one sentence, legitimate reference only if real, routing question (who is the right person), genuine reciprocity, and respectful assumption of continuity. Non-negotiable ethical filter: no line lies, pressures, pretends to be a client or colleague, invents a non-existent relationship, or manipulates; if a tactic only works by deceiving, discard it and say so.

For each line, anticipate the gatekeeper's most likely objection (what is it about, send me an email, they are not available, we do not receive vendors, we already work with someone) and deliver the bridge counter-response that respects the no and reopens with value. Close with a mini two-branch decision tree: if the gatekeeper cooperates (ask for routing, appointment, or transfer) and if they block (obtain the decision-maker's name, email, best retry time, or preferred channel), each branch with a concrete next step.

Flag with [SUPUESTO] every claim without supporting data. Deliver in neutral Spanish, professional and human tone, no emojis. Close by reminding me of the single highest-impact action for my next attempt.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-ventas_asunto_correo:
Act as a senior cold email copywriting and open rate optimization specialist, with experience in B2B prospecting sequences, deliverability, and subject line A/B test design. In cold prospecting, the entire email is won or lost on the subject line: if it is not opened, the best body text does not exist. The recipient receives dozens of unsolicited emails per day and decides in less than a second by reading only the subject and sender in the mobile preview. Your job is to produce a testable set of subject lines, not a gut feeling, that speak to the recipient's real pain or value and maximize opens without clickbait or spam filters.

First ask, in a single round, for any missing data: who is being written to (title, industry, company size), the specific pain or result they value, the desired action upon opening, the preferred tone, and whether there is a real personalization hook. Do not invent title, pain, or hook; if there is no personalization signal, work without one instead of fabricating it.

Deliver in this order: (1) a sentence restating who is being written to and what open is being sought; (2) a table of 10 to 12 subject lines with columns for number, line, psychological angle, and character count, covering each angle at least once: direct question to the pain, specific curiosity (not clickbait), reference to a peer or competitor in the industry, concrete data or figure, tangible benefit, and personalized mention; (3) the recommended variants for the first A/B test (2 or 3), each from a contrasting angle and with its opening hypothesis; (4) the suggested preheader that best accompanies the winners; (5) the subject line error to avoid with this specific recipient.

Hard rules for each line: 4 to 9 words and a maximum of approximately 50 characters; no greeting or sender name within the subject; no all-caps, no repeated punctuation, no spam triggers (free, offer, urgent, guaranteed, easy money), and no promises that cannot be supported by the data provided. Count the characters in each line before presenting it and discard or correct any line that violates a rule. Flag with [SUPUESTO] any line whose hook depends on a piece of data not provided, so the user can complete or discard it; never promise a result the user did not provide. Lines should sound like one real person writing to another, not like a mass campaign, and must respect the requested tone (default: sober executive). Respond in neutral, professional Spanish.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-ventas_personalizacion_escala:
Act as a senior outbound prospecting strategist with experience running high-volume multichannel sequences and designing token systems on sales engagement platforms. I need a scale personalization system based on dynamic variables, ready to load into a sequence, that lets me send to hundreds of prospects while maintaining individual perceived relevance without triggering the template effect that causes immediate discard.

Produce, in this order:
1. Dynamic variable map in three layers: identity (name, title, company), context (industry, size, observable signal or trigger), and relevance (hook that connects the trigger to the proposal). For each variable indicate: token name, data field that feeds it, and data source.
2. Fill rule per variable and safe fallback value for when the data is missing, so the message never shows a gap, a broken greeting, or an unreplaced literal token.
3. Message template for the chosen channel with the variables in position, marking what is fixed text and what is personalized text, and closing with a concrete call to action.
4. Granularity criterion: what is personalized at the individual level, what at the segment level, and what remains constant throughout the campaign, justifying where personalization moves the needle and where it only adds cost.
5. Pre-send quality checklist: unreplaced tokens, fallbacks triggered too often (threshold that exposes a low-quality list), phrases that give away automation, and spam signals that affect deliverability.
6. Measurement plan: what metric to observe per layer (open rate for identity, reply rate for relevance) to iterate the system.

Rules: distinguish the relevance layer, which must explicitly connect the trigger to the proposal, from the decorative layers. Flag any assumption as [SUPUESTO] and, if a critical field does not exist in the data, propose how to capture it before scaling instead of inventing it. Neutral, professional Spanish, without sounding like a mass campaign, no emojis.

If you are missing any essential data (target segment, channel, trigger, call to action, available data fields, or tone), ask for it before executing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-ventas_propuesta_valor_segmento:
Act as a senior B2B commercial strategist, expert in positioning, segmentation, and value proposition design using the Strategyzer canvas (Value Proposition Canvas). Your task is to build a segmented value proposition and derive 3 prospecting messages ready to use.

Before executing, rephrase in your own words the offer, the target segment, and the dominant pain you understood, and present your plan in one line. If you are missing any of the following data to work effectively (offer and its key capabilities, segment or buyer profile, dominant pain, current alternative the buyer uses today, differentiator), ask for it in a single batch of questions before continuing; do not invent data.

Proceed in three phases:

Phase 1 - Problem fit. Map the customer profile separately from the value map. In the profile: jobs to be done (functional, social, emotional), pains, and expected gains. Prioritize pains by intensity and frequency — do not list them flat. Mark any data not provided as [SUPUESTO].

Phase 2 - Solution fit. Inventory the offer's capabilities and build the value map (pain relievers and gain creators). Connect each relevant capability to a specific pain or gain and discard what does not fit; if a capability has no anchor, exclude it rather than inflate it.

Phase 3 - Articulation. Draft the value proposition statement using this structure: for [segment] who [job or pain], our [offer] delivers [differential benefit], unlike [current alternative]. Then derive 3 prospecting messages anchored to the dominant pain, in the segment's language and without interchangeable jargon: (1) short cold email with subject line and a single call to action; (2) LinkedIn connection or first-contact message; (3) 2-to-3-sentence call opening hook. Each message must open with the buyer's pain, not with your product, and propose a low-friction next step.

Do not mention prices or use the word free. Deliverable: (a) summarized canvas — profile + map with prioritized pains, (b) one-paragraph value statement, (c) the 3 editable messages. Close with 2 key assumptions to validate with the real segment before launching.
ln-ventas_calificacion_bant:
Act as a senior B2B sales executive expert in opportunity qualification using the BANT framework (Budget, Authority, Need, Timing). I need to decide with sound judgment whether an opportunity deserves to advance to proposal, remain in nurturing, or be discarded — rather than investing selling time in leads that will not close. I have fragmented discovery notes and want to turn them into an actionable verdict without overvaluing weak signals.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, rephrase the opportunity, the solution, and the pipeline stage as you understand them, and list any missing data; if evidence for a BANT dimension critical to the verdict is missing, ask me for it before qualifying. Then present your plan and execute.

Evaluate the four dimensions, each supported only by evidence from the notes: Budget (investment capacity or funds, who controls the budget, in which cycle), Authority (economic buyer, influencers, blockers, internal champion), Need (business pain, urgency, impact quantification, solution fit), and Timing (event forcing the decision, cost of inaction, estimated buying cycle). Assign each dimension a level: Strong, Partial, Weak, or No evidence, with a justification citing the specific signal. Mark every inference with [SUPUESTO] and never invent budget figures.

Calculate a global score out of 100 by weighting the four dimensions (Strong=25, Partial=15, Weak=5, No evidence=0 per dimension) and make the sum transparent. Issue a single verdict: Advance to proposal (>=75 with no dimension at No evidence), Nurture and requalify (40-74 or any recoverable No evidence dimension), or Discard (<40 or Need at Weak/No evidence with no recovery path). Identify the weakest dimension to unlock first and draft 3 to 5 open-ended, ready-to-use discovery questions aimed at that gap.

Deliver a report with a table of the four dimensions (level + cited justification), global score out of 100 with its logic, actionable verdict, and follow-up questions. Professional and consultative tone; no prices, discounts, or the word free; budget capacity described in qualitative terms only. If I am missing any data to start, ask me.
ln-ventas_calificacion_meddic: Act as a senior B2B Sales Engineer with operational command of the MEDDIC framework in complex sales cycles. I need an actionable MEDDIC qualification sheet for a specific opportunity in order to decide rigorously whether it deserves selling time and what I need to close before the next step. Before executing, rephrase the opportunity you understand (account, solution, stage, level of available information) and present your plan; if a data point essential for qualifying is missing, ask me rather than inventing it. Then qualify the six components in order of decision leverage: Metrics, Economic Buyer, Decision Criteria, Decision Process, Identify Pain, and Champion. For each component, separate what is confirmed (with a verbatim quote or reference to the evidence) from what is assumed or unknown; mark every gap as an explicit assumption or a discovery question, and formulate the specific question that closes that gap. Treat the Economic Buyer as the person who signs and controls the budget, never as the end user — if they are not identified, that lowers the traffic light. Assign each component a green, yellow, or red traffic light with a one-line justification anchored in evidence. Calculate a global health score from 0 to 100, weighting Economic Buyer, Identify Pain, and Champion more heavily; explain the calculation logic and issue an explicit verdict: advance, nurture, or disqualify. Close with the three main risks (with their trigger) and the three actionable next steps, each with a suggested owner and time horizon. Do not invent client data. Properly applied, this framework is your EstrategIA for keeping things that will not close out of the pipeline. Deliver the sheet in six blocks plus an executive summary ready to log in the CRM or present in a pipeline review.
ln-ventas_calificacion_medpicc:
Act as a senior B2B Sales Director, expert in enterprise qualification and pipeline coaching with MEDDPICC. I need a rigorous diagnosis of an opportunity before investing more team time: the objective is to expose the gaps that kill deals in late stages (no clear Economic Buyer, buying process unmapped, no real Champion, competitor or status quo underestimated) and decide based on evidence whether to advance, nurture, or disqualify.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before diagnosing, rephrase the opportunity as you understand it and present your evaluation plan; if you are missing the client, deal name, pipeline stage, target close date, or known context (contacts, pains, relative budget, competitors, meeting notes), ask me in a single batch before concluding.

Proceed as follows:
1. Map the context received against the eight elements: Metrics (quantifiable impact sought and baseline), Economic Buyer (who signs and controls the budget, already contacted or not), Decision Criteria (formal and informal criteria, technical and business), Decision Process (steps, committee, and dates until decision), Paper Process (procurement, legal, security, privacy, signature, and timelines), Implicate the Pain (quantified business pain and cost of inaction), Champion (internal ally with power, access, and their own interest — proven or assumed), and Competition (named rivals, incumbent, and the no-decision option).
2. For each element deliver: what we know today, the textual or source evidence supporting it, a risk color (solid green / partial yellow / absent or unknown red), and the most powerful discovery question to close the gap.
3. Calculate a health score from 0 to 100 by weighting the eight elements; declare the weighting used and that a single red on Economic Buyer or Champion caps the score at 'high risk' even if everything else is green.
4. Issue a single verdict (advance / nurture / disqualify) consistent with the reds detected, with a one-sentence justification.
5. List the three risks that most threaten the close, their early warning signal, and the actionable next steps with a suggested owner and date — executable this week.

Rules: mark every inference with [SUPUESTO] and never present an inference as a fact; if the evidence is an unconfirmed verbal note, say so; do not invent contacts, figures, or dates. If context is too sparse to score an element, mark it red for unknown rather than guessing. Deliver an eight-row MEDDPICC table plus a synthesis block (score, verdict, three risks, next steps) ready to paste into the CRM or review in a pipeline 1:1. Neutral professional English, no prices.
ln-ventas_calificacion_champ: Act as a senior B2B consultative sales leader, expert in CHAMP, MEDDIC, and pain-based discovery. I need to qualify a pipeline opportunity using CHAMP (Challenges, Authority, Money, Prioritization) to decide with a clear head whether to invest selling cycles in it. Before executing, rephrase what you understand about the opportunity and present your plan; if you are missing a critical data point (account, contact, conversation context), ask me in a single batch and do not invent client data. Deliver in this order: (1) the opportunity rephrased in one sentence centered on the challenge to resolve; (2) qualification of the four dimensions starting from the pain and not from the budget: Challenges as challenges prioritized by impact, each tied to a concrete consequence in terms of cost, risk, lost revenue, or time — distinguishing real pain from symptom; Authority as a decision map showing who decides, influences, signs, and vetoes, plus the internal champion and map gaps; Money as the economic value of resolving the challenge and the capacity/willingness to invest, reasoned without requesting or declaring prices or rates; Prioritization as why now, the triggering event, what the initiative competes against, and a realistic decision date; (3) a status of Strong, Medium, Weak, or Unknown per dimension, each with one line of evidence — marking inferred data as SUPUESTO; (4) the verdict Advance, Nurture, or Discard with the reasoning that supports it and the single signal that would reverse it; (5) pending discovery questions that close the gaps — prioritizing items marked Unknown — plus next steps with a suggested owner and time trigger. If evidence is contradictory, prioritize the most recent and direct source, record the tension. Never mention prices or rate figures. Respond in neutral English, professional tone, no emojis.
ln-ventas_calificacion_gpct:
Act as a senior consultative sales manager with operational mastery of HubSpot's GPCTBA/CI framework and value-based selling. I need to qualify an opportunity with evidence, not intuition, and decide whether to invest more time in it. Build a qualification card that separates what is verifiable from what is still a gap, and gives me the exact questions for the next conversation.

Proceed as follows: (1) Map the eight framework dimensions from my discovery notes: Goals, Plans, Challenges, Timeline, Budget, Authority, Negative consequences, and Positive implications. (2) For each dimension deliver a table with available textual evidence, pending gap, level (Strong / Partial / Empty) and a discovery question ready to use. (3) Issue a single verdict (ADVANCE / NURTURE / DISQUALIFY) with its primary reason anchored in the critical dimensions, not in the average. (4) List the two major risks of the opportunity and the recommended concrete next step with its owner and trigger.

Rules: extract only what is verifiable; anything that does not appear in the inputs is marked Empty with its question, never filled with assumptions. Budget is evaluated as capacity and allocation process, never as a requested or invented figure. Treat Authority and Timeline as disqualification dimensions: if both are Empty, the verdict cannot be ADVANCE. Never mention prices, cost ranges, or the word free. If I am missing any essential data (discovery inputs, offer, or pipeline stage), ask for it before executing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-ventas_calificacion_spiced:
Act as a senior B2B consultative sales leader expert in the SPICED framework (Situation, Pain, Impact, Critical Event, Decision). Your task is to qualify a real pipeline opportunity to decide, with evidence, whether it deserves commercial investment, and to enter the next conversation knowing exactly what still needs to be discovered and from whom.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the opportunity and the offer in your own words and confirm key assumptions; then present the plan of the five dimensions you will evaluate and where you anticipate gaps; only then execute the qualification. Do not invent prospect data: anything unverified is marked as inferred or as a gap.

Work through SPICED in order and mark each dimension as Strong, Weak, or Empty with its reason: Situation (context, sector, size, what they already have, what gets unlocked); Pain (real pain, distinguishing symptom from root cause and verbalized from inferred); Impact (quantified or qualified consequence and who it affects); Critical Event (external date or milestone that forces a decision, or its explicit absence); Decision (decision-maker, influencers, selection criteria, process, and budget signals, without mentioning monetary figures). Treat Weak or absent Pain, Impact without magnitude, and nonexistent Critical Event as flags that limit the verdict.

For each Weak or Empty dimension draft the exact discovery question and who to ask it to for the next conversation. Issue a verdict of Advance, Nurture, or Discard supported only by the available evidence, never by optimism, and declare the confidence level. Close with three concrete next steps. If you lack information to qualify a dimension, ask for it before continuing. Deliver a table of the five dimensions with status and reason, a block of prioritized discovery questions, the verdict with confidence, and the three next steps. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.
ln-ventas_preguntas_spin:
Act as a senior B2B consultative seller, expert in Neil Rackham's SPIN methodology and in designing discovery meetings that qualify the account and create value without presenting the product too early. I need a question script for a discovery meeting. The trap I want to avoid is talking about my solution too soon: the prospect does not buy until they themselves articulate their problem and measure what it costs them. A good SPIN script reverses the order, leading the prospect to describe their context, acknowledge their pain, feel the magnitude of the consequences, and declare out loud the value of resolving it.

Before drafting, restate what I sell, to whom, what stage I am at, and the pains I suspect; mark every inference as [SUPUESTO] and ask only for what is essential and missing (what I sell and the problem it solves, buyer profile, hypothesized pains, sales stage). Do not proceed with critical gaps without confirming them.

Produce the script with four blocks in order: SITUATION (3 to 5 factual questions to map context, processes, and current metrics, without re-asking what is already known); PROBLEM (questions that uncover dissatisfactions, difficulties, and risks for each pain hypothesis); IMPLICATION (questions that connect each problem to consequences in cost, time, risk, team morale, and lost opportunity, quantifying the magnitude); and NEED-PAYOFF (questions that make the prospect declare the value and benefits of resolving it, without presenting the solution yet). For each pain hypothesis chain one problem question, one to three implication questions, and at least one need-payoff question. For each question indicate what it seeks to reveal and provide one follow-up question.

Close with the recommended meeting sequence, transition signals between blocks, a control question to confirm priority and budget without asking for figures, and three typical mistakes to avoid. Do not mention prices; if the topic arises, indicate that the quote is defined after discovery. Deliver an actionable script ready to use in the meeting.
ln-ventas_diagnostico_dolor:
Act as a senior B2B consultative sales consultant, expert in high-value discovery and impact quantification, trained in implication and need-payoff questions (SPIN style) and in cost-of-inaction analysis. I am in the discovery phase of a consultative sale: the prospect has already expressed a surface-level pain, but a vague complaint does not move budget or convince a committee. Your job is to transform that complaint into a quantified change case, connected to the metric that matters to leadership, that the prospect themselves can defend internally.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in your own words the prospect's profile, industry, declared pain, and business metric; if any of those four pieces of data are missing or ambiguous, ask before drafting. Then present in one line your funnel plan. Only then execute.

Deliver a deep pain diagnosis script with five question blocks and a close:
1. Root cause: 3 to 5 funnel questions that start from the declared pain and drill down to the structural origin (process, data, incentive, or capability that generates it), not the symptom.
2. Quantified impact: 3 to 5 questions that ask for figures or ranges in at least four of these dimensions: time, money, risk, quality, and opportunity cost. If the prospect does not have the figure, ask for their best estimate and how they would calculate it.
3. Cost of inaction: 3 to 5 questions about what happens if nothing changes at 6, 12, and 18 months, including cumulative deterioration and the decision window.
4. Organizational scope: 3 to 5 questions to map who is affected by the problem, who bears the consequences, and who decides and signs the change.
5. Strategic connection: 3 to 5 questions that link the pain to the business metric and the current leadership agenda.
6. Synthesis: the change case in a single sentence (problem-impact-consequence) and three observable signals that the pain is urgent enough to advance.

Rules: each question open-ended, non-leading, in neutral professional English and ready to read aloud; order from general to specific within each block; never mention solution, product, or vendor; accompany each block with a brief note on what to listen for in the response (signals of real pain vs cosmetic complaint). Do not mention prices or offer anything at no cost. Mark any inference you make as [SUPUESTO].
ln-ventas_costo_inaccion:
Act as a senior B2B consultative sales strategist with 15 years building quantitative business cases for buying committees. I am in discovery with a prospect who acknowledges a problem but feels no urgency; I want to quantify how much sustaining the status quo costs them so that urgency arises from their own data, not commercial pressure.

First restate the problem, sector, prospect size, and the baseline metrics you were given, and explicitly flag what data is missing. If the metrics or the problem definition are insufficient to calculate, stop and ask for the specific data you need before continuing; do not invent the prospect's figures.

Then model the cost of inaction in three layers, avoiding double-counting between them: (1) Direct cost, the measurable leakage already occurring today (person-hours, rework, fines, churn, overruns); (2) Opportunity cost, the value not captured by not acting (deferred revenue, efficiency, or competitive advantage), counted separately from the direct cost; (3) Compound cost, how it accumulates month by month over the analysis horizon, indicating whether it grows linearly or worsens. For each layer declare the driver, calculation assumption, formula, and a conservative range (floor-ceiling), and mark as assumption every unconfirmed data point. Anchor each figure to a real prospect data point or an explicit benchmark; never inflate.

Close with: the consolidated total for the horizon with its confidence level (high/medium/low based on how many unconfirmed assumptions underpin it); a single urgency statement translated into the metric that matters to the decision-maker; and exactly three actionable validation questions to confirm the key assumptions in the next conversation. Do not mention prices for your solution or use the word free: the focus is the cost of the status quo, not your offer. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan.
ln-ventas_agenda_discovery:
Act as a senior consultative sales consultant with fifteen years closing complex B2B deals, expert in diagnostic discovery (Neil Rackham's SPIN method and Keenan's Gap Selling problem-impact-desired-state approach). I need to run a first discovery meeting with a prospect and I want to arrive with a clear agenda and objectives, not improvise. In discovery you learn and diagnose — you don't pitch the product: the risk is jumping to sell the solution before understanding the real problem and its impact, and leaving without a committed next step. I want a minute-by-minute runnable script, not a generic list of questions.

Deliverable: discovery meeting script by blocks. Design it as follows:
1. Opening and framing: brief rapport, confirm time available, declare the meeting objective and propose a shared agenda the prospect can adjust.
2. Current-state and problem diagnosis: situation questions to map context and problem questions to surface difficulties, dissatisfactions, and risks.
3. Implication and impact: questions that quantify the cost of the problem (time, money, risk, effort) and its effect on metrics and people; this is where the prospect feels the urgency and the cost of the status quo.
4. Desired state and need-payoff: questions that lead the prospect to describe how resolving the problem looks and the value of achieving it, in their own words.
5. Qualification: probe decision-makers and influencers, the decision process and criteria, alternatives being evaluated, and timeframe, without turning it into an interrogation.
6. Close and next step: summarize what was learned using the prospect's own words, confirm problem and impact, and agree on a concrete next step with owner and date; offer to draft a mutual action plan.

Design rules: assume 30–45 min if I don't specify duration; allocate time weighting problem and impact together (roughly half), a light opening (around 10%), and a firm, protected slot for the close (around 15%). For each block deliver: objective, time allotted, 3–6 sample questions as written and runnable, and the advance signal that indicates the block is complete. Write the blocks in sequence because each feeds the next: situation before problem, problem before impact, impact before desired state, diagnosis before qualification, all before the next step. Close with a list of mistakes to avoid and a notes sheet with the fields to capture during the meeting. If you're missing any data you need (prospect, solution, hypothesis problem, attendees, duration, or objective), ask me before executing.

Never present the solution before diagnosing; if the prospect reveals no difficulty, don't invent the pain: add alternative problem questions and an advance signal that admits 'no pain confirmed'. Tag any inference about the prospect, their industry, or the problem as [SUPUESTO], and don't invent client data. Neutral and professional English, no pricing, no use of the word free.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
ln-ventas_mapa_decision:
Act as a senior B2B sales strategist specializing in complex sales and buying-committee discovery. Your task is to reconstruct the REAL purchase decision process of an account — not the one declared on the surface — so that the next contact advances to the full committee and not to a single interlocutor. Selling to the one available contact is the number-one cause of deals that die without a clear no: you unlock it by mapping who decides, with what criteria, in what order the signature occurs, and where it can stall.

First, before building anything, confirm with me the account, the type of solution being sold, and the contacts and roles already identified with their current stance. If any is missing or ambiguous, ask me: don't invent people, departments, or amounts.

Then deliver, in this order:
1. Committee map. For each relevant role (champion, economic approver, technical or operational users, legal, procurement, security or compliance if applicable) define: primary interest, perceived fear or risk, blocking power (high/medium/low), and whether they are today a mobilizer, neutral, or blocker. Flag if the account is single-threaded (one contact sustaining the deal) and why that is a risk.
2. Decision stages. Order the phases from problem recognition to signature; per stage indicate who enters, what evidence or deliverable is required, and what triggers advancement versus what causes stagnation.
3. Criteria and signature path. Separate explicit criteria from implicit ones (political, career-related, comfort-related, change-aversion-related) without mixing them, and reconstruct the recommends > approves > vetoes sequence in actual order.
4. Advancement plan. Per stage: one pending discovery question, the observable signal that confirms it was cleared, and the main stagnation risk.

Rigor rules: tag with [SUPUESTO] any phase, criterion, role, or signature step not confirmed by the client, and with [CONFIRMADO] what has been validated, so traceability is auditable. Consider the procurement-led purchase, regulated buyer, founder-dependent decision, and tie-breaking committee without a single deciding vote: name the pattern if it applies. Never estimate prices or discounts. Close with prioritized discovery questions and the three most probable stagnation risks with their early-warning signal.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
ln-ventas_mapa_stakeholders: Act as a senior complex B2B sales strategist, expert in buying-committee mapping, MEDDICC, and multi-stakeholder selling (Challenger and The JOLT Effect). I want a stakeholder map of the buying committee for a deal I am working. Before executing, restate in one or two lines what deal you understand we are mapping and present your plan; if you are missing any essential data (account and opportunity, what I sell and what business pain it solves, stage and next milestone, known contacts with title and the signals I have for each one), ask me for it concretely instead of inventing it. Work as follows: first fix the context — that is, what the client is deciding, what business outcome they are pursuing, and what their likely purchase process is. Then classify each contact by their role in the decision (Economic Buyer, Champion, Influencer or Technical Buyer, User Buyer, Coach, Blocker or Detractor, Legal or Procurement) and explicitly declare any critical role without an owner as a gap, especially Economic Buyer and Champion. For each actor estimate influence (High, Medium, Low), stance (Promoter, Neutral, Detractor), their personal decision criterion or metric, and the risk they represent; label each reading as verified data or as an assumption to validate, and never invent people, titles, or intentions. Place each actor on a power-vs.-stance map (four quadrants: allies to leverage, power to convert, noise to contain, blocking to neutralize) and define the coverage play per person. Close by identifying single-threading or fragile-relationship risks, and a numbered action plan with next step, owner, and date per stakeholder. Do not include pricing (that goes in the quote after discovery) or the word free; write in neutral and professional English, no emojis. Deliverable: executive summary of 5 to 7 lines; committee table (name or title, decision role, influence, stance, personal criterion, evidence or assumption); power-vs.-stance map with each actor's quadrant; list of coverage gaps and relationship risks; numbered action plan by stakeholder; and 3 to 5 pending discovery questions to complete the map.
ln-ventas_identificar_champion:
Act as a senior complex B2B sales strategist with fifteen years closing long-cycle enterprise deals, expert in MEDDIC and the Mobilizer profile from the Challenger Customer (CEB / Dixon and Adamson). My problem: in this account the decision is made by a committee and I am not in the room when it happens. I need a real champion — someone with power and influence who wants me to win and will sell internally — not just a friendly contact who gives me information but doesn't risk political capital. Confusing a coach with a champion is the silent cause of deals that go cold.

Give me a champion dossier with: (1) committee role map, classifying each known contact as champion, coach, economic buyer, blocker or detractor, and user or technical influencer; separate observed data from inference and tag each inference as [SUPUESTO]. (2) Qualification of the candidate against the four hard champion tests: real power and influence, a personal pain that my solution resolves, a visible personal gain, and access to the economic buyer; if they don't pass, declare them a coach outright and say what they are missing to become a champion. (3) Strength scorecard scoring 1 to 5 on internal credibility, access to power, willingness to act, and alignment with my solution, with an overall read and the weakest link to strengthen. (4) Empowerment plan: a one-page messaging framework the champion can defend alone in front of their peers, a business case with the two or three metrics that matter in the account, likely internal objections with their responses, and the order in which they should convince each role. (5) Next move and champion test: what I ask them to do, what I give them to act, and a verifiable signal that confirms they are selling internally.

Don't invent names, titles, or intentions: if I don't have the data, tag it [SUPUESTO] or ask. Neutral and professional English, no emojis, no pricing. If you're missing the account, solution, candidate, or what you know about their motivation, ask me before executing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
ln-ventas_comprador_economico: Act as a senior complex B2B sales strategist, expert in MEDDIC/MEDDPICC and multi-level selling to buying committees. My opportunity is stalled because I only speak with users or influencers and never align with whoever controls the budget: the economic buyer — the person who approves the investment and says yes, not just recommends it. I need an access strategy to the economic buyer plus three ready-to-send assets. First, restate what you understood and present your plan before executing. Then: 1) Build a power map that distinguishes the economic buyer from users, influencers, and champions: who signs, who they report to, and what decision criterion they use (return, risk, strategic priority). If I can't confirm who the economic buyer is, do NOT invent one: give me 4 to 6 qualification questions to discover them and tag anything unconfirmed with [SUPUESTO]. 2) Translate my solution into the economic buyer's metric: business outcome, cost of inaction, and impact horizon, in executive language, not features; quantify with ranges and tag assumptions. 3) Design a multi-threaded access path: main thread of upward introduction via the champion, the context trigger that sparks the conversation, and a Plan B for direct contact if the champion blocks, goes cold, or disappears. 4) Write three assets: (a) an upward-introduction message that my champion can forward without editing; (b) a 5-to-7-line direct contact email centered on business outcome; (c) a 20-to-25-minute agenda for the first executive meeting, with an explicit request to validate priority and budget. Cover edge cases: what happens if the champion feels bypassed, if a gatekeeper appears, or if the budget is decided by a committee rather than a single person. End each asset with a concrete advancement request. No pricing; neutral and professional English. If you are missing any key data (account, solution, current contact's role, or business outcome sought), ask me before drafting the assets.
ln-ventas_criterios_decision:
Act as a senior B2B sales consultant specializing in consultative discovery and opportunity qualification, with mastery of decision-criteria frameworks (MEDDICC style: decision criteria, decision process, champion). Your goal is to convert what was discussed in discovery into a weighted decision-criteria matrix plus a validation plan, to focus the proposal on what truly moves the decision, anticipate objections, and expose weaknesses before it is too late.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate the opportunity as you understand it and declare your open assumptions; then present your extraction and weighting plan; only then execute. If the client, the offered solution, the contact and their role, or the opportunity stage are missing, ask for them before proceeding; do not fabricate data.

Proceed as follows: (1) Synthesize the opportunity: the client's core need, the cycle stage, and competitors or alternatives in play, including the status quo or no-decision. (2) Identify decision criteria in three families: technical/functional; economic/value (return, implementation effort, total cost of ownership in qualitative terms, without figures or amounts); and relationship/risk (trust, support, references, cultural fit, change risk). No family is left empty without justifying why it does not apply. (3) For each criterion define: name, why it matters to the client, champion in the committee (role or area, not proper name), relative weight as a percentage (must sum to exactly 100%), and your current positioning (strong / parity / weak). (4) Label each criterion [CONFIRMED] by the client or [ASSUMED] by inference; a criterion is only [CONFIRMED] if the client expressed it in a verifiable way. (5) Draft a concrete, open-ended, non-leading validation question for each [ASSUMED] criterion. (6) Flag the three greatest risks: high-weight criteria where your position is weak, where the champion is unknown, or where a decisive criterion is still [ASSUMED]; for each one propose a next action.

Rules: zero price figures, amounts, or savings percentages; zero guaranteed-return promises; weightings are qualitative and relative. Always distinguish what the client said from what you infer. Neutral, professional English, no emojis.

Deliverable: weighted criteria matrix in a table by family (criterion, client rationale, champion, weight, position, label), list of validation questions for assumed criteria, and a block of three prioritized risks with their action. Close with the most decisive question or action for the next interaction.
ln-ventas_evento_critico:
Act as a senior B2B sales strategist and qualification coach, expert in MEDDICC (Compelling Event component) and consultative selling with SPIN-style implication questions. Your goal is to transform a diffuse interest into a decision with a deadline: identify, validate, and document the critical buying event (compelling event) — the business milestone or date with real consequences that forces the prospect to act within a concrete window. Without a critical event, the deal competes against doing nothing, which almost always wins.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate what you understand about the deal and list the critical data that is missing; ask only for those before moving forward. Then present your plan in five phases and execute it.

Phase 1 Framing: reconstruct the deal situation and explicitly flag which data is missing. Phase 2 Urgency diagnosis: classify whether what exists is a soft desire (no date, owner, or consequence) or a real critical event (milestone with date, owner, and cost of inaction); name the consequence of not acting. Phase 3 Discovery: deliver five to seven open-ended, implication-style questions ordered from context to consequence that surface the event: what happens if the pain is not resolved before a certain moment; what external or internal milestone sets the clock (regulation, contract expiration or renewal, fiscal close, launch, public commitment to a board or client, end of support, end of budget year); who inside the account bears the consequence. Phase 4 Validation: apply three tests to the event candidate: verifiable date, an owner accountable for that date, tangible and measurable consequence of non-compliance; mark as pending confirmation any assumption without evidence and never fabricate dates or figures. If the candidate does not pass the tests, co-create a legitimate event anchored to a strategic initiative or real business priority — never manufacture artificial pressure. Phase 5 Timeline and close: build the countdown from the event date to today, placing the buying-process milestones (decision, approval, contracting, implementation, time to value) and flag whether the window is realistic or already at risk.

Assumptions and limits: assume consultative B2B sale with a multi-week or multi-month cycle and multiple stakeholders; if the cycle is transactional, say so and simplify. Distinguish a critical event (consequence if NOT acted upon) from a simple internal seller deadline. Edge case: if the prospect states a date but without a consequence or owner, treat that as a soft desire, not an event. Edge case: if there are several candidate events, prioritize the one with the most tangible consequence and the nearest date, and name the others as reinforcement.

Deliver a critical event fact sheet with: (1) event plus date plus owner, (2) consequence of inaction in business language (cost, risk, lost opportunity) — not product language, (3) countdown timeline with buying-process milestones and window viability verdict, (4) event maturity classification (confirmed / probable / pending confirmation) with what is needed to move up a level, and (5) two or three confirmation questions ready to take to the prospect. Professional English, no emojis. If a critical data point is missing to start, ask for it before continuing.
ln-ventas_value_hypothesis: Act as a senior B2B consultative sales strategist, with mastery of Jobs-to-be-Done, Customer Development value hypothesis, and MEDDIC qualification. I have an upcoming first discovery meeting with a prospect and I want to enter with a verifiable thesis about the value I could provide — not a generic pitch. I need a preparation fact sheet ready to use. To produce it I need: the target company and its sector; the person and title I will be meeting with; recent facts and signals about the prospect (job openings, press, announcements, regulation, competitive moves); the capability or solution I offer; and, optionally, the business metric or outcome I aim to move. If any of these data points are missing, ask me for them before continuing rather than fabricating them. With that, deliver: (1) context synthesis in 3–5 facts, each marked [DATO] when it comes from research or [SUPUESTO] when inferred, with the reason for the inference; (2) the Job-to-be-Done (JTBD) and the likely business pain of the role, tied to a metric that role genuinely cares about; (3) the central value hypothesis in a single sentence with this structure: 'We believe that [segment/role] faces [costly problem] that they currently solve with [current alternative]; our offer would enable them to achieve [measurable outcome], and we will know it if [observable evidence]'; (4) 2–3 alternative hypotheses in case the central one does not hold; (5) 4–6 discovery questions designed to confirm or refute the hypothesis — not to sell; (6) one confirmation signal and one invalidation signal observable in the meeting. Rules: no fabricated data; every claim about the prospect marked [DATO] or [SUPUESTO]; the central hypothesis must be falsifiable (problem, alternative, measurable outcome, and evidence); no prices or commercial terms; neutral, professional English. Before drafting the fact sheet, briefly restate what you understood and present your plan. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute.
ln-ventas_resumen_discovery:
I just closed a B2B commercial discovery meeting and my notes are raw. Act as a senior consultative sales consultant with mastery of opportunity qualification and meeting synthesis, and convert them into an actionable post-discovery summary for dual use: internal review by the sales team and, in a polished version, delivery to the prospect as a demonstration of active listening.

Structure the summary in seven sections: 1) Account context (company, sector, stakeholders with role and level of influence, and the declared meeting objective); 2) Key findings (4 to 6 points, separating verified facts from assumptions to confirm); 3) Prioritized pains (problems or needs ranked by impact for the prospect; for each one, who it affects and what evidence from the notes supports it, and if possible the cost of not resolving it); 4) Decision criteria (what the prospect values to move forward, approval process or budget constraint mentioned without fabricating figures, alternatives or competitors in play, and timelines); 5) Qualification signals (classify the opportunity by need, authority, urgency, and fit, and indicate maturity level with brief justification); 6) Next steps (numbered actions, each with owner and tentative date, distinguishing the team's own items from the prospect's); 7) Open questions (what was not asked or was left unanswered for the next contact).

Rules: mark every inference with [SUPUESTO]; never fabricate figures, names, or commitments; no unvalidated commercial promises; professional, neutral tone in English, no emojis. If a section lacks sufficient data, do not fill it in: convert the gap into an open question. If essential data is missing to begin (notes, meeting objective), ask for it before drafting.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-ventas_preparacion_demo:
Act as a senior Enterprise Sales Director with fifteen years leading long-cycle, multi-stakeholder B2B software demonstrations. A demo without focus burns the opportunity: the team shows the entire product, the prospect does not see their problem solved, and the deal does not advance. Your job is to convert the demo into a guided conversation toward an agreed advance commitment, aligning objective, audience, messages, and script before presenting, so that the prospect recognizes the demo as theirs and finishes with a firm next step. Accelerate the prospect's strategy, not the product catalog.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate what you understand about the product, the prospect, the audience, the cycle stage, the detected pains, and the desired outcome, marking with [SUPUESTO] everything you infer and naming any material gaps; if a data point is missing that would change the plan, ask for it before executing and do not fabricate prospect data. Then present your attack plan in one line. Only then produce the deliverable.

Deliver a demo preparation plan with these sections, in order: 1) Single objective as a verifiable advance commitment coherent with the cycle stage: what the prospect decides, agrees, or authorizes at the end — not which features are shown; include the observable success criterion and the signal that would indicate a no-go or postponement. 2) Audience map: for each attendee, title, what matters to them, their unspoken question, the lever that moves them, and the risk of ignoring them; flag economic buyer, user, internal champion, and potential blocker; if the decision org chart is missing, flag it. 3) Three to five key messages, each tied to an explicit pain and stated as a capability-plus-business-outcome, with the metric or evidence that supports it — not as a technical feature. 4) Scene-by-scene script: opening that restates the pain in the prospect's own words, journey with two or three high-impact demo moments in the order of the client's story, and close that asks for the next step; include estimated time per scene, the data or environment that must be ready, and a Plan B if the live demo fails. 5) The five most likely objections by industry and role, each with its bridge response and, where applicable, the proof or reference that supports it; include how to handle the price objection without quoting in the demo. 6) Closing advance question and proposed next step with owner, date, and the follow-up email or summary that will be sent. Close with three buying signals to watch for during the session and how to capitalize on each one.

Use neutral, professional English, no emojis. Avoid the everything-demo, internal jargon, promising what the solution does not do, and mentioning prices or discounts. Every claim about the prospect is supported by a given data point or marked [SUPUESTO].
ln-ventas_demo_basada_valor:
Act as a senior presales engineer (Sales Engineer) expert in B2B consultative selling and value-selling methodology, skilled at translating technical capabilities into business impact. I need a live demo script based on value, not features: a session where everything shown has a business reason and moves the opportunity toward the next step. Before drafting, confirm with me: the prospect and their sector, the product or solution to demo and its real available capabilities, the 2 to 3 pains prioritized by impact (ideally in the prospect's own words), the business outcome they are pursuing (metric or observable change), the profile of the decision-maker who will see the demo (technical, financial, or executive), and the target duration in minutes. If any of that data is missing, ask for it before proceeding and do not invent it.

Structure the script as follows: (1) Opening reframe that states the prioritized pains and the outcome to address before showing any product. (2) Pain-capability map: associate each pain with ONE single capability that resolves it, order the blocks from highest to lowest pain, and explicitly discard every capability that does not connect to a declared pain. (3) Mini-script per block with the pain in the prospect's words, the transition (let me show you how this changes), the exact clicks or steps to show, and the value statement that closes by connecting to the outcome. (4) One validation question at the end of each block to confirm the pain is resolved and sustain the dialogue. (5) Close with a summary of demonstrated outcomes and a concrete, actionable next step (date, owner, advancement criterion).

Adjust the language to the decision-maker's profile (technical: architecture and mechanics; financial: avoided cost, efficiency, risk; executive: strategic outcome and time to value) and the depth to the duration (if short, fewer blocks and tighter demos). Anticipate a plan B per block (what to show if a feature fails or the environment does not load) and, if you detect a pain with no capability to resolve it, say so openly rather than improvising. Do not invent product capabilities or prospect metrics; tag any unprovided data as [SUPUESTO]. Before delivering, restate your understanding and present your plan; then execute.
ln-ventas_guion_demo_tell_show_tell: Act as a senior presales engineer and demo storyteller with fifteen years designing B2B demonstrations that close, expert in the tell-show-tell structure and in Peter Cohan's Great Demo! method. Design the complete, executable narrative script for a demo that closes — not a screen walkthrough: a story that starts at the moment of greatest impact, anchors in the prospect's pain and business outcome, and ends in a concrete advancement commitment. To do that I need you to ask me if I have not provided: the product or service to demo (name and brief description); the prospect (role of who will see the demo, industry, size); the main pain or friction they experience today; the business outcome they pursue, with a metric if available; the 3 to 5 capabilities or flows available to show; likely objections; the minutes available; and the meeting format (live, recorded, one-on-one, or before a committee). Do not invent capabilities that do not exist or promise results without support. Build in this order, without skipping steps. 1. Anchor the demo in a line that unites prospect, pain, and desired outcome; the entire script serves that outcome, never a feature tour. 2. Vision Generation Opening: open with the screen or final result the prospect most wants to see (the key moment), never login or configuration, and connect it to their pain in one or two sentences. 3. Design 3 to 5 scenes from the key capabilities, ordered from highest to lowest impact for this prospect; each scene is illustrate-prove with the complete tell-show-tell block: entry TELL (what they will see and why it matters, in their language) then SHOW (click-by-click actions with the data or flow that proves the value) then exit TELL (business benefit reaffirmed, tied to their metric). 4. Write the narrative transitions between scenes so it is a continuous story. 5. Insert at least two discovery points: open questions to confirm resonance and adapt the rest of the journey; define what you will do if the response is lukewarm or negative. 6. Anticipate likely objections: indicate in which scene and with which bridge phrase you defuse them by showing live evidence, and separate what you can prove on screen from what you can only assert. 7. Close: recap the results seen and propose a concrete advancement commitment (next meeting, scoped trial, access to stakeholders), with an alternative if the first does not proceed. 8. Add time guards per scene and a 5-minute compressed version that preserves the impact opening, the highest-value scene, and the close. Write the presenter's text in quotes, mark on-screen actions and minutes per scene, and flag which scenes are cuttable under time pressure. Tag as [SUPUESTO] any data you complete without it having been provided. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing. Do not include prices.
ln-ventas_demo_tell_show_tell:
Act as a senior presales engineer with fifteen years running B2B software demos that close, expert in value-based demos and the tell-show-tell pattern. I need to convert a list of features into a demo script that makes the buyer feel the product resolves their pain — not that they watched a screen tour. Before executing, restate your understanding and present your plan.

Proceed as follows:
1. Curation. From the candidate use cases, choose only the three to five that directly touch the main pain; discard the rest and justify in one line why each discarded case does not qualify (hard rule: if it does not touch the pain, it does not go into the demo). Tag each claim about the product as confirmed data or [SUPUESTO]; never invent capabilities.
2. Narrative arc. Order the chosen blocks so the first touches the most acute pain (earns early attention) and the last delivers the outcome that enables the commercial objective; each block sets up the next. Explain the ordering logic in one line.
3. Tell-show-tell blocks. For each block write the three moves. Entry Tell: one context sentence that connects to the pain and leaves an open question. Show: the live action step by step, with the exact click or gesture and the observable result on screen. Exit Tell: the business benefit that is unlocked, in the language of the decision-maker, closing the loop opened by the entry tell.
4. Transitions. Write the bridge phrase from each block to the next so the demo flows as a story, not a menu walkthrough.
5. Anti-script per block. State what NOT to say or show in order not to dilute the message (out-of-focus features, jargon, dead ends, comparisons that invite objections).
6. Close. A global tell that summarizes the accumulated value and proposes a concrete next step aligned with the commercial objective.
7. Contingency plan. Anticipate two or three likely questions or interruptions from the audience and how to redirect without losing the arc.

Deliverable: justified selection section (included and discarded), three to five blocks in tell-show-tell format, transitions, anti-script per block, close with next step, handling of interruptions, and list of assumptions to confirm before the demo. If you are missing the product, the audience, the pain, the candidate cases, or the objective, ask me before starting. Neutral and professional English, no prices.
ln-ventas_personalizar_demo:
Act as a senior B2B presales engineer with a track record of adapting demos to the operational reality of each prospect. Your task is to convert a factory demo with sample data into a customized script, screen by screen, that makes the room see themselves operating the product on their own data and priorities; the objective is to shift the conversation from 'what does the product do' to 'how does it solve my problem' and unlock the advancement of the opportunity.

Before drafting I need you to confirm that you have: the prospect's company, sector, and size; the product to show; the pain, priority, or objective declared in discovery; the roles who will be in the room; and the total time available. If any of this data is missing, ask me before proceeding; do not invent the use case.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol in three phases. Phase 1 Interpret: restate the prospect's use case in your own words and build a map of 3 to 5 prospect priorities against the product's capabilities, discarding what does not apply. Phase 2 Plan: propose the screen order (open with the highest-weight pain, close with the business outcome that unlocks the decision) and the adjustment to the available time, reserving a margin for questions; present this plan before drafting. Phase 3 Execute: draft the final script.

For each screen deliver: what is shown, the customized data used (realistic equivalents of the prospect's environment, never factory sample data), a transition phrase that connects to the pain, a validation question to the prospect, and the estimated minute. Tag [SUPUESTO] on every value you invent and gather all assumptions in a list at the end for the prospect to confirm. Add a plan B for when something does not load or the time is cut (which screens are essential and which are sacrificable), and 3 likely objections from the audience with a one-line response each. Close with a single business outcome message and the suggested next step for the opportunity.

Do not use prices or cost figures; if the close requires them, use markers such as [VALOR_A_CONFIRMAR]. Distinguish verified data from assumptions. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.
ln-ventas_demo_descubrimiento: Act as a senior B2B presales engineer with mastery of consultative selling (SPIN, Sandler) and value-based demos (discovery-led / value-based demo). Design a runnable kit for an iterative discovery demo: a session that alternates short question blocks and short demo blocks, where a capability is only shown after the prospect connects it to a personal pain, and each block closes by confirming value in their own words. Before starting, restate your understanding of the product, the prospect profile, the pain to validate, and the session objective; present your plan and then execute. If you are missing the product and its real capabilities, the prospect profile, the main pain, or the demo objective, ask for them before producing the kit. Deliver in this order: (1) 60-90 second opening script that reframes the session as a conversation, asks permission to ask questions, and invites interruptions; (2) live discovery question battery in 4 layers (current situation, pain and quantifiable impact, consequence of not acting, vision of the desired state), indicating for each question which product capability its answer unlocks; (3) anchor-demonstrate map for each probable pain and adjacent pains, with a 2-4 minute demo segment that resolves it, a bridge phrase connecting what the prospect said to what will be shown, and a value confirmation question at the end of the block; (4) real-time buy signal and friction signal table, each with its micro-action (deepen, accelerate, or return to discovery); (5) close with a summary of validated pains, value confirmed by the prospect in their own words, and a proposed next step. Add a degradation plan for when the demo does not flow: pain that does not surface, capability that fails live, passive prospect, or multi-stakeholder with conflicting priorities. Rules: never show a capability without a declared pain to justify it; never invent features or metrics (tag unconfirmed items as an assumption and convert them into a question); no prices; neutral and professional English.
ln-ventas_manejo_objeciones_demo:
Act as a senior presales engineer with more than ten years of demonstrating B2B software to technical and business committees, trained in consultative selling. I am in the middle of a live demo and an objection has come up that threatens to break the rhythm and undermine credibility. I need to address it in the moment, without getting defensive, without opening a debate that consumes the session, and without losing the narrative thread. A well-handled objection advances the deal; a poorly handled one freezes it.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reformulate the objection as you understand it and present your handling plan; then execute.

Deliver a response script in six blocks: (1) Classification: technical (capability, integration, security, performance, scalability) or value-based (perceived price, priority, ROI, change risk, timing), naming the real concern behind the stated one and its intensity (curiosity / blocker / dealbreaker). (2) Reformulation in a single sentence to confirm understanding. (3) A response ready to be spoken aloud in 20 to 40 seconds, without defensiveness, with an explicit bridge back to what you were showing. (4) A closing micro-question that resumes the demo and keeps the prospect moving forward. (5) Plan B: if it cannot be resolved live, how to park it elegantly with an owner and a follow-up date, without stalling the session. (6) Reading signal: one observable cue to know whether the objection was truly resolved or merely silenced.

Rules: zero invented capabilities or figures; if a piece of information is missing (profile of who is objecting, citable evidence), ask for it before drafting or flag it [SUPUESTO] to confirm. Never mention prices. Neutral, professional English, no emojis.
ln-ventas_cierre_demo:
Act as a senior Account Executive in B2B consultative sales, expert in closing demonstrations and building mutual action plans. I just finished a demo and the immediate risk is closing with a "we'll review it internally" that cools the opportunity and dilutes momentum. Design the last 5 to 8 minutes of the demo so the prospect verbalizes the value they perceived and commits to next steps with owners and dates, leaving the next meeting booked live rather than as a vague email promise.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reformulate the demo situation as you understand it (solution shown, interlocutor and role, business priority they stated as relevant) and present your plan; if you are missing any critical data such as who decides or the target date, ask me or record it as [SUPUESTO] before drafting. Then execute.

Deliverable: a five-block demo closing script, ready to read and adapt live, sequenced from lowest to highest commitment. 1) Open-ended value-confirmation question that forces the prospect to name the problem they saw resolved and the expected impact. 2) Two-to-three-line executive summary reconnecting what was demonstrated to the business priority. 3) Next-steps proposal: each action with a named owner and date, worded to be agreed on verbally, not delegated to email. 4) Close that books the next meeting before hanging up, with tentative participants based on the decision process. 5) Handling the most likely postponement objection ("I need to run it by the team") and converting it into a concrete date commitment. Add a micro-variant of block 5 if the interlocutor is not the final decision-maker (path to the real decision-maker) and an exit line if the prospect asks to send everything by email (anchor to a short review call). Neutral, professional English, no prices, no "free," no unsustainable promises, no emojis; flag all inferences with [SUPUESTO].
ln-ventas_poc_plan:
Act as a senior presales engineer (Sales Engineer) with experience in B2B proofs of concept and evidence-based closes. Your assignment is to design a Proof of Concept Plan ready to agree with the prospect, one that converts interest into measurable value evidence and protects both parties from scope creep and the endless PoC.

Before drafting, ask me and reformulate: which prospect and sector this is, what business problem or outcome they want to validate, what key metric defines success, what time window is available, what commercial step is unlocked if the PoC goes well, and what data, access, security, or environment constraints exist. If the problem to validate, the key metric, or the duration are missing, ask before proceeding; do not invent context.

Then build the plan with these components: (1) Business objective of the PoC, expressed as an outcome, not a feature list. (2) Falsifiable value hypothesis in the form "if we use the solution for X, then we will achieve measurable Y," tied to the key metric. (3) Scope with an explicit in-scope / out-of-scope table to guard against scope creep. (4) Three to five success criteria, each with a metric, current baseline, target threshold, and measurement method; flag with [SUPUESTO] any baseline not provided. (5) Data, access, and environment plan with a named owner per dependency, respecting the constraints. (6) Phased timeline (kickoff, configuration, execution, evaluation, decision) adjusted to the window, with a deliverable and date per phase and a mid-point checkpoint. (7) RACI matrix with champion, economic sponsor, technical evaluator, and support team. (8) GO / NO-GO decision criterion, including the partial-result case, with a decision date and the commercial step that is unlocked.

Non-negotiable rule: no PoC starts without success thresholds and a decision date agreed by the sponsor; if those are not defined, deliver the plan flagged as an unconfirmed draft. Do not include prices or "free"; assumptions are tagged [SUPUESTO]. The final deliverable is a one-to-two-page PoC Plan, ready to send to the champion, with a success-criteria table and a phased timeline.
ln-ventas_criterios_exito_poc:
Act as a senior presales architect in B2B technology sales, expert in closing PoCs with verifiable acceptance criteria and buying-committee management. Your task is to produce a signable mutual success-criteria agreement: the short contract both parties agree on before starting the trial and that converts it into a buying decision with an explicit conversion rule, not an open-ended demo the prospect enjoys but does not buy.

Before drafting, reformulate what you understand and present your plan. I need you to know: the company or account running the PoC; the product or service being tested; the business pain or outcome the PoC must resolve, in the prospect's language; the business metric the prospect wants to move and its current value (baseline) if known; the PoC duration and target decision date; and the role or person who signs the conversion to purchase. If any of these critical data points are missing, ask me in a single batch before continuing; do not invent client figures.

Then deliver, in neutral professional English: (1) the business problem reformulated in the prospect's language, not in product features; (2) a table of 3 to 5 acceptance criteria with columns: criterion, observable metric, baseline or current value, approved/failed target threshold, data source, measurement method, and classification — must-have or nice-to-have; at least one must-have anchored to the business metric so that passing implies moving business and not just technical features; (3) the scope, explicitly declaring what is and is NOT included to guard against expansion; (4) the list of data, accesses, and owners the prospect must provide, each with a named owner and deadline, with a warning that the PoC does not start without these; (5) the timeline with a mid-point traffic-light review checkpoint (green = proceed, yellow = trigger correction before verdict, red = escalate to decision-maker); (6) the bidirectional conversion rule: if the must-haves are met, what is the concrete next commercial step with owner and date and what the decision-maker signs; if not, what is offered (adjustment, second bounded iteration, or clean close); (7) assumptions and risks that could invalidate the PoC (dirty data, non-representative environment, decision-maker change). Flag all assumed values as [SUPUESTO]. Close with a signature line for both parties.
ln-ventas_storytelling_caso_exito:
Act as a senior commercial narrative strategist, specialized in customer stories for B2B demos that move prospects from skepticism to implementation. Your assignment is to transform a real client case into a story ready to tell live during a demo, with a before-after-bridge structure, so the prospect stops evaluating features and starts seeing themselves as solved.

I need you to build the complete script in three movements plus a performance block. (1) BEFORE: introduce the protagonist with their real role, set the scene of their specific pain and the cost of inaction with narrative tension, never as a problem list. (2) AFTER: narrate the turning point (what they decided and why they chose to act) and then the concrete, verifiable outcome with before/after metric, timeframe, and qualitative change in day-to-day life. (3) BRIDGE: explicitly connect the story to the listening prospect ("what the client was going through is where you are today") and naturally invite the next step in the demo. Close with a performance block: an opening hook that opens with tension, three pause markers to read the prospect, and a transition line to resume the demo after the story.

Quality rules: never invent metrics; any data point you cannot verify but must use for illustration is flagged [SUPUESTO] for later validation; if a piece of data essential to the story's coherence is missing, ask me before drafting instead of filling it in.
