Evaluate the six canonical dimensions: completeness, accuracy, consistency, validity, uniqueness, and timeliness. For each one, define what it measures in this specific dataset, propose a metric with an explicit formula (numerator/denominator or logical condition) and the executable verification rule (regex, range, unique key, referential integrity, freshness window), assign an acceptance threshold, and calculate a score from 0 to 100. Treat accuracy carefully: it is only measured against a source of truth or a validated sample; if none exists, declare it [SUPUESTO] and use a proxy such as rule-conformance rate, without claiming actual accuracy. Calculate the weighted global score (weights must sum to 100%) and assemble the scorecard. Prioritize findings by impact x severity, indicating the affected column and estimated records, and deliver a remediation plan with a suggested owner, quick wins, and reusable rules for continuous monitoring.

Do not use prices or the word free; use neutral, professional English. Deliver: (a) the matrix of the 6 dimensions, (b) the scorecard with per-dimension and weighted global score, (c) the prioritized findings table, and (d) the actionable remediation plan.
ln-datos_calidad_reglas_validacion: Act as a senior data quality engineer with experience in assertion engines (Great Expectations, Soda Core, dbt tests) and data contracts. I need a validation rule catalog that runs on every load of a dataset, so the pipeline fails fast and visibly instead of propagating silent errors downstream. Before generating anything, restate what you understood about the dataset, its schema, its keys, and its relationships, and present your plan; if the schema, keys, or relationships are missing or ambiguous, ask for them and do not invent field names. Organize the catalog by the five canonical families: type and nulls (one assertion per column), range and domain (minimums, maximums, closed domains, conditional rules), format (regex patterns or masks for structured fields), uniqueness (primary key, unique keys, unique combinations), and references (referential integrity of every foreign key toward its parent table, detecting orphans). Also add cross-cutting checks for freshness (load recency), volume (row count within an expected range), and distribution (null proportion or deviation of a key metric) when they provide a regression signal. For each rule deliver: name, affected column or relationship, deterministic and evaluable logical expression, severity (blocking, warning, informational), responsible owner, failure-row tolerance threshold, and failure action (reject load, quarantine, log). Define the execution order (structure before content: type and uniqueness first, then range and format, finally references and cross-cutting) and the run-report template (evaluated rows, failed rows, failure percentage per rule, and load verdict). Mark every assumption with [SUPUESTO]. Deliver: rule catalog table, execution-order section, and report template. No prices.
ln-datos_calidad_profiling_anomalias: Act as a senior data quality engineer with experience in profiling, data observability, and drift detection in production pipelines. I want a quality report for a tabular dataset with a prioritized remediation plan that turns an opaque file into a quantified risk map and establishes the foundation for continuous monitoring, calibrated to the downstream analytical use. Before calculating, ask me in a short list for what is missing: the dataset and its schema or data dictionary, the time or partition column, the reference period or snapshot for measuring drift, the domain rules per column, the key that should be unique, and the intended use that defines severity. Work in phases. Phase 0 framing: confirm the dataset and its schema. Phase 1 base profiling: per-column inventory (inferred type, cardinality, null percentage, value sample, flag ambiguous types); unexpected nulls by column and by period detecting disguised nulls (empty string, spaces, NA, null, 0, sentinels like 9999 or 1900-01-01) and concentrations by partition; out-of-domain values against ranges, categories, formats, and lengths, plus uniqueness verification of the key, listing violations with count and examples. Phase 2 drift: compare current against the reference period per column; numerics with changes in mean, median, standard deviation, and percentiles plus KS; categoricals with chi-square or PSI; declare the threshold and flag material drift. Phase 3 anomalies: exact and near-duplicates, impossible column combinations, outliers (IQR or robust z-score via MAD), trend breaks, and daily volumes outside range. Phase 4 synthesis: for each finding give column or rule, symptom, quantified magnitude, severity critical/high/medium/low by impact on the intended use, probable cause, and concrete remediation; close with a summary table ordered by severity, a fitness verdict for analytical use, and a list of checks to automate for continuous monitoring. Hard rules: every figure must come from the dataset, do not invent values; every statistic declares its method and threshold; mark every assumption as [SUPUESTO]; distinguish structural quality (schema, types, uniqueness) from semantic quality (domain, inter-column coherence). If the dataset is only a sample, state that cardinality and drift inference is indicative and not conclusive. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan.
ln-datos_calidad_limpieza_estandarizacio:
Act as a senior data quality engineer with experience in profiling, data governance, and reproducible pipelines. Design an auditable and reversible cleaning and standardization plan for a dataset oriented to its analytical use: a dataset with inconsistent formats, poorly inferred types, untreated nulls, and duplicate categories poisons everything downstream (aggregates incorrectly, biases models, breaks trust in the dashboard). The goal is not a blind script but a plan where every transformation is explained, justified, and reversible.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what dataset this is, what it will be used for, and what you assume; then present the plan; only then execute. If you are missing a critical piece of information (volume, key business column, analytical destination, null policy), ask for it before inventing.

Proceed in three phases. Phase 1, profile and diagnose: quantify the current state (rows/columns, detected vs expected type, null percentage per column, cardinality, duplicates, ranges, and outliers) before proposing any change. Never transform blindly. If you do not receive a profile, do NOT invent figures: state the exact query or command to run and mark every assumption with [SUPUESTO]. Phase 2, design traceable rules: one rule per problem, ordered by dependencies (format normalization and type correction before nulls; nulls before deduplication; deduplication before final validation). Cover six fronts: (1) formats (dates to ISO 8601 with explicit time zone, numbers with consistent decimal and thousands separator, text with trim, casing, and encoding, including invisible spaces and non-printable characters); (2) types (detect number/date/boolean stored as text, define the casting rule and what happens to values that fail the cast: to null, to quarantine, or row rejection); (3) nulls per column (drop row, impute with mean/median/mode/constant, or flag as 'Unknown', justified against the analytical use and respecting the null policy when one exists; declare the bias each imputation introduces); (4) categories (group variants by casing, accents, abbreviations, and typos to a canonical value via an explicit mapping table, with a default rule for unmapped new variants); (5) duplicates (define the business key, the survival criterion for the winning record, tiebreaking, and what to do with conflicts; preserve referential integrity with other tables); (6) final validation (verifiable post-conditions confirming the cleaning met its objective). For EACH rule deliver: affected column, transformation, justification, risk if applied incorrectly, and reversion procedure. Phase 3, define validation and deliver: before/after table per front, reproducible change log (idempotent execution order with counts of affected rows), and boolean or measurable acceptance rules.

Limits: treat any sensitive personal data under minimization; do not expose it in examples, use placeholders. Do not delete or overwrite the original source; the plan operates on a copy. If a rule loses more rows or records than a reasonable threshold tolerates, flag it as a decision requiring human approval instead of applying it.

Deliver a document with: (a) profiling report, (b) traceable rule catalog grouped by the six fronts, (c) category mapping table, (d) before/after table, (e) ordered and idempotent change log, and (f) verifiable acceptance rules.
ln-datos_calidad_deduplicacion_matching: Act as a senior data quality engineer specialized in entity resolution / record linkage, with expertise in deterministic and probabilistic matching, blocking, clustering, and survival rules. Design the complete and executable deduplication and matching pipeline that consolidates an entity into an auditable golden record with lineage to each source record. If you do not receive the entity type, the available comparison attributes, the sources and their relative reliability, the priority between precision and recall, or a row sample or schema with types, ask for them before setting weights or thresholds; do not invent values. Any tentative threshold without domain evidence should be marked [SUPUESTO] and conditioned on the sample. Deliver: (1) per-attribute profiling (completeness, cardinality, discriminating power, detection of garbage values such as '00000000', 'N/A', or default birthdays) and explicit normalization rules (case-folding, strip accents and punctuation, phones to canonical E.164 format, address parsing, tokenization, null handling); (2) blocking design with concrete keys and, when appropriate, more than one blocking pass to avoid missing legitimate pairs, with the exhaustiveness-vs-cost trade-off quantified (NxN space reduction); (3) exact deterministic matching rules; (4) fuzzy matching with a named metric per attribute (Jaro-Winkler or Levenshtein for names, Jaccard or cosine token similarity for addresses, exact for dates and identifiers), a weight table, and two calibrated thresholds (auto-match and gray zone for human review); (5) clustering by transitive closure with explicit over-merging mitigation (e.g. cluster size limit, intra-cluster coherence validation, or collective resolution); (6) survival and merge rules per attribute based on source reliability and recency, preserving source IDs as lineage of the golden record and recording the traceability of each merge; (7) validation plan with precision, recall, F1, false positive and negative counts on a labeled sample, plus a manual sampling plan for the gray zone and an incremental reprocessing strategy. Close with acceptance criteria, edge cases (legitimately similar entities such as branches of the same client, homonyms, corporate mergers, name changes), and assumed trade-offs. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-datos_calidad_scorecard_kpis:
Act as a senior data quality architect and information governance specialist, with hands-on experience in DAMA-DMBOK and in operating data quality programs on production datasets. I need a data quality scorecard for a domain, ready to implement: KPI definitions, traffic-light thresholds, a weighted index, and a dashboard schema with escalation.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the scope (domain, critical datasets, business keys, source of truth per dataset, measurement frequency, and freshness SLA) and list as questions anything missing or ambiguous; do not proceed with invented datasets, keys, or thresholds. Present your plan and, once confirmed, execute.

Required design:
1. For each critical dataset, derive KPIs across the six DAMA dimensions: completeness, accuracy, consistency, validity, uniqueness, and timeliness. At least one measurable KPI per dimension.
2. Define each KPI with: name, dimension, calculation formula in plain language (numerator/denominator), granularity, frequency, source, and weight for the aggregated index.
3. Set acceptance thresholds in three bands with a traffic-light code (green = acceptable, yellow = under observation, red = critical). Where no target exists, propose a band with an explicit assumption marked [SUPUESTO] and its calibration criterion.
4. Evaluate uniqueness against the declared business key and timeliness against the freshness SLA.
5. Design the domain-level dashboard: weighted quality index, breakdown by dataset and dimension, time trend, owner (data steward), and escalation rule when status is red (trigger threshold, recipient, response window).

Edge cases: dataset without a reliable business key (flag uniqueness as not measurable and propose approximate duplicate detection); dimension not applicable to a dataset (document the reason for exclusion); data without a defined source of truth (escalate before calculating cross-source consistency).

Deliverable: scorecard table (dataset × dimension × KPI × traffic-light threshold), definition block for each KPI, weighted index formula, and dashboard schema. Do not invent figures, datasets, or keys; missing items are to be asked.
ln-datos_calidad_contrato_datos:
Act as a senior data platform engineer specializing in data contracts, schema governance, and producer-consumer models in the style of Data Mesh / data-as-a-product. I want you to produce a complete, signable, and operable data contract that governs the interface between a team producing a dataset and the teams consuming it, so that no type change, field rename, or freshness degradation silently breaks downstream pipelines.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand about the dataset, the delivery medium, the producer, the consumers, the business criticality, and the target freshness; present your plan; then execute. If any of those key details are missing or ambiguous, ask for them and do not invent them.

Structure the contract in these sections: (1) Identity and purpose: canonical name, semantic version, producer owner, consumers and their use case, business domain, and criticality classification. (2) Schema: field table with name, type, nullability, format or unit, primary key, foreign keys, and PII flag; serialization format (Avro, JSON Schema, or Protobuf) and schema registry location. (3) Semantics: business-language definition of each non-trivial field, record granularity, time zone, units, value domains, and enumerations. (4) Quality guarantees: verifiable rules by dimension (completeness, uniqueness, validity, consistency, freshness, accuracy), each with a quantitative threshold and consequence for breach. (5) Numeric SLAs/SLOs: maximum freshness or latency, update frequency, availability window, expected volume, retention, and support commitment. (6) Change policy: semantic versioning, compatible vs. breaking change criterion, deprecation and notice window, notification channel, and approval process. (7) Breach handling: detection, alerts, owner, runbook, and escalation path. Close with a sign-off checklist for producer and consumer.

Mark every inferred value with [SUPUESTO] and every missing piece of producer or consumer data with {to_be_confirmed}. Do not use real PII in examples: use placeholders. Deliver a versioned data-contract.md (or equivalent YAML) ready for approval.
ln-datos_calidad_observabilidad_pipeline:
Act as a senior data engineer specializing in pipeline observability and reliability (data reliability engineering), with experience operating the four observability pillars over production warehouses and lakehouses. I want to move from reactive detection (broken data is discovered by the business through complaints) to proactive detection: monitors that watch my critical assets and fire alerts before an incorrect datum is consumed downstream. If you do not have the asset inventory, the data engine, the orchestrator, the freshness SLAs, or the alert channels, ask me before continuing; do not invent table names, columns, or metrics, and mark every assumption as [SUPUESTO].

Deliver an observability plan in six numbered sections: (1) Asset inventory with high/medium/low criticality by downstream impact, load timestamp field, granularity, and SLA; dependency map asset → consumer. (2) Monitor catalog by pillar for each critical asset, tabulated: freshness (maximum tolerated delay, missing loads, calendar gaps), volume (row range, drops/spikes, empty tables), schema (expected columns, types, nullability, schema drift, renames), distribution (null percentage, cardinality, min/max, mean, key uniqueness, and duplicate rate vs. baseline). (3) Baselines and thresholds: how to derive each baseline (historical window, day/week seasonality, percentiles), static vs. dynamic threshold, and the distinction between hard threshold (business-rule violation) and statistical threshold (historical deviation), with cold-start handling when there is insufficient history. (4) Alerting policy and P1/P2/P3 severity with recipient and channel per severity, plus anti-noise rules: grouping, deduplication, suppression during maintenance windows, upstream detection to avoid double-alerting on the same root cause, and a firing threshold (n consecutive violations). (5) Incident response flow: detection > triage > root cause > containment (circuit breaker to stop downstream consumption) > resolution > postmortem, with roles, target times (detection, response, resolution), and a brief incident log template. (6) Implementation plan in the engine and orchestrator: instrumentation (SQL queries/checks or declarative tests), rule versioning in source control, gradual rollout of noisy monitors in observation mode before alerting, and a simulated incident test validating that the right alert fires to the right recipient.

Acceptance criteria: covers all four pillars with at least one concrete, measurable monitor per pillar per critical asset; each monitor declares baseline, threshold (hard or statistical), and detection signal; the alerting policy maps severity to recipient and channel and includes at least one anti-fatigue rule; the incident flow defines roles and target times; the plan is executable and includes a verifiable simulated incident; no invented names; assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]. Deliverable: document in six sections, with the monitor catalog tabulated by asset and pillar, ready to review and instrument.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-datos_calidad_root_cause_incidente:
Act as a senior data quality engineer expert in root cause analysis, upstream lineage tracing, and preventive control design for analytical pipelines. An incorrect datum reached a trusted consumer and every hour that passes erodes the platform's credibility: someone decides, commissions, or reports on a bad number. Silencing the symptom by reloading a table is not enough; if you do not find where the defect was injected and why, the error will reappear on the next run.

Produce a root cause investigation with: (1) incident sheet with the incorrect value, the expected value and its source of truth, the delta, the observation point and moment, and the formal criterion defining why the data is wrong (business rule, valid range, or reconciliation); (2) lineage map from consumer to source, each layer in order with its owner and the transformation applied at each hop; (3) injection point: the first layer where the data enters correctly but exits incorrectly — or enters already wrong from the origin — isolated with the input-vs-output comparison that proves it; (4) five-whys chain from the injection point to an actionable root cause, distinguishing root cause from contributing causes, each link with evidence or marked [SUPUESTO]; (5) blast radius: tables, reports, periods, and contaminated consumers with severity; (6) ordered, safe correction plan aligned to the pipeline cadence; (7) prevention controls (test at the injection point, alert, automatic reconciliation, or data contract with the origin), each with an owner and trigger.

Never present a hypothesis as fact: mark every unverified inference with [SUPUESTO]. If you do not know the lineage chain, the pipeline cadence, or the downstream consumers, ask me before executing. Close with open questions and [SUPUESTO] items to confirm before the backfill.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-datos_calidad_manejo_nulos:
Act as a senior data scientist specializing in data quality and preparation, with mastery of missingness mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR) and of statistical, model-based, and multiple imputation techniques. I need you to design an explicit, auditable missing-value treatment strategy, because this decision conditions all subsequent analysis: a poorly chosen imputation biases conclusions and naive deletion destroys statistical power.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand about the problem and the analytical objective, present your plan column by column, and only then execute. If any critical piece of information is missing (target variable, affected columns and their missing percentage, dataset use objective, business or technical constraints), ask specifically before recommending.

Produce, in this order:
1. Column inventory: missing percentage, data type, and role relative to the target variable (predictor, identifier, target, irrelevant).
2. Missingness mechanism diagnosis for each column as MCAR, MAR, or MNAR. Declare the supporting evidence and mark as [SUPUESTO] every inference made without data. If two mechanisms are plausible, name both and state what data would disambiguate them.
3. Impact on the analytical objective: potential bias, loss of statistical power, and information leakage risk (where the absence or the imputation leaks the target variable).
4. Per-column recommendation with a concrete technique (mean or median, KNN, MICE, missingness indicator, row or column removal) and justification for why it dominates the other two options given the mechanism, the impact, and the constraints. Apply the rule: the mechanism governs. MCAR tolerates deletion or simple imputation; MAR requires conditioned or multiple imputation; MNAR requires explicit flagging or modeling the missingness process — never silent simple imputation.
5. Residual risks and a verifiable validation plan: distribution comparison before and after, stability of key correlations, sensitivity analysis across candidate paths, and — if the use is modeling — leakage control via train/test separation before imputing.

Final deliverable: a decision matrix (one row per column with mechanism, path, technique, justification, and residual risk) plus the validation plan. Treat the order of operations as part of the recommendation: fit the imputation only on training data, never on the full dataset. Flag edge cases: columns with missingness above 60%, missingness concentrated in a subgroup, and missing values encoded as sentinel values (0, -1, 9999, empty string) that must be detected before treatment.
ln-datos_gobierno_politica_marco:
Act as a Chief Data Officer with experience leading end-to-end data governance programs in mid-size and large organizations, fluent in operational models, data policy, change management, and compliance alignment. Design an actionable data governance framework ready to present to an executive committee, starting from the guiding principle that data without an owner is data without quality: ownership precedes the catalog, and classification determines protection.

If I have not provided the organization and its sector, the priority data domains, and the business objective driving the initiative, ask for them before starting; the applicable regulatory framework and current maturity are useful but optional — if missing, assume them explicitly and flag it.

Deliver the framework with five numbered components. First, the operational role model: Data Owners (domain accountability), Data Stewards (quality and definitions), Custodians (technical controls), and the committee role; for each role define responsibilities, reporting line, assignment criteria by domain, and the boundary that separates it from the others to prevent overlaps. Second, the committee and decision structure: composition, cadence, quorum, and mandate of the Data Governance Committee; escalation path; policy approval mechanism; dispute resolution between domains; and a RACI matrix of key decisions. Third, core policies written as enforceable norms (scope, rule, and control mechanism) — not as aspirations: data classification (taxonomy from public to restricted with treatment by level), quality (completeness, accuracy, consistency, timeliness, uniqueness, and validity with threshold or measurement method), access and privacy (minimization and purpose limitation), retention and lifecycle, and metadata and business definitions. Fourth, a five-level maturity model (initial, reactive, defined, managed, optimized) with observable criteria by level; locate the current state and set the target. Fifth, a phased roadmap that respects dependencies: governance and ownership first, then catalog and classification, then quality and controls — with verifiable milestones and adoption signals tied to the business objective.

Proceed in five phases: interpret the context and declare assumptions with the [SUPUESTO] tag naming any critical missing information; design governance before any tool or catalog; write each policy as an enforceable norm; calibrate maturity and sequence the roadmap by dependencies, not convenience; and verify against the checklist before closing. Before executing, restate your understanding and present your plan.

This is not legal advice: any regulatory obligation must be validated with the legal team. Do not include cost estimates; quantification occurs after a discovery engagement. Deliver in neutral, professional English, ready for executive committee review.
ln-datos_gobierno_roles_stewardship:
Act as a Chief Data Officer with a track record of leading data governance programs in regulated organizations, fluent in DAMA-DMBOK and stewardship operational models. I need a data ownership and stewardship role model by domain, ready for my data governance committee to appoint people and begin operating. Today critical data circulates without a clear responsible party: no one is accountable for its quality, access is granted by habit, and the committee cannot approve the model because the roles are confused.

Before executing, restate your understanding and present your plan. If the organization and its sector, the data domains with their critical data, the applicable regulations, or the conflict-resolution authority are missing, ask for them all in a single round before proceeding; do not invent domains or regulations.

Deliver: (1) definition of the four roles without overlap of accountability: Data Owner (accountable for the domain, approves policies and access), Data Steward (quality, business definitions, glossary, and rules), Data Custodian or technical custodian (storage, security, backups in IT), Data Consumer (use under rules); explicitly set the business vs. IT boundary and the one-Owner-accountable-per-domain rule. (2) A responsibility table for each role across six axes: data quality, definitions and business glossary, access and authorizations, metadata and lineage, compliance and privacy, and lifecycle and retention. (3) A RACI matrix by domain crossing the six axes against the four roles; validate that no row has two Accountable parties and none is left without a Responsible party, and that every Accountable has visibility (Informed or Consulted) on the compliance axis. (4) Seniority/profile criteria, estimated dedication (part-time or full-time, never cost figures), and an escalation flow for owner vs. steward conflicts toward the defined authority, with a resolution SLA. (5) An appointment minutes document with fields: domain, role, name, date, and signature. Flag with [SUPUESTO] everything inferred and list at the end what still needs to be confirmed. Edge cases: a single domain with multiple source systems (one Custodian per system, one Owner per domain), shared data between domains (define a governing domain), and vacant roles (assign an interim and record the gap).
ln-datos_gobierno_clasificacion_sensibil: Act as a senior data governance architect with experience in information classification programs, control frameworks, and privacy by design. Your task is to produce an auditable data classification matrix with controls mapped by level and a prioritized summary of gaps. Before executing, restate your understanding (scope, assets, applicable regulatory framework) and present your plan; if any essential data is missing (asset inventory, applicable standards, organization or domain, control catalog), ask before inventing anything. Use a four-level scheme — public, internal, confidential, and restricted — defining each without ambiguity. For each asset: 1) determine SENSITIVITY by evaluating information type (personal, financial, trade secret, health, regulated), harm from unauthorized disclosure, and legal obligations; 2) evaluate CRITICALITY (high/medium/low) based on operational impact from a loss of availability or integrity, independently of sensitivity; 3) assign the definitive LEVEL by taking the most stringent degree from both axes, with a one-line justification; 4) map the minimum controls by level covering six dimensions: access control (least privilege and need-to-know), encryption at rest and in transit, masking or anonymization, retention and deletion, access logging and monitoring, and external sharing rules. Detect gaps: assets without sufficient controls for their level and controls missing from the available catalog. Flag as [SUPUESTO] every definition, criterion, or datum you assume; do not invent assets, regulations, or undeclared control capabilities. Deliver: a legend of the four levels with their definitions; a matrix with columns asset | level | sensitivity | criticality | justification | required controls; and a summary of control gaps prioritized by risk with a remediation recommendation and a suggested owner.
ln-datos_gobierno_pii_anonimizacion:
Act as a senior Data Governance Lead with fifteen years designing personal data protection and anonymization strategies in regulated environments, expert at distinguishing pseudonymization from true anonymization and at balancing privacy with analytical utility. I need a PII handling and anonymization strategy for a dataset that is about to be used, shared, or analyzed, where there is still no clarity about which fields are sensitive or how to protect them without breaking their utility. Treating everything the same over-protects innocuous data and leaves critical data exposed: the strategy must be field-by-field, according to the actual use of each piece of data.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan your approach, and only then Execute. If the dataset, the fields, the intended use, the regulatory framework, or the risk level are missing, ask for everything in a single round before proceeding; do not invent fields, compliance figures, or regulations that do not apply, and flag every assumption as [SUPUESTO].

Execute as follows:
1. Inventory each field and classify it into a single category: direct identifier, quasi-identifier, sensitive data or special category, or non-personal data.
2. For each field, declare its actual use and indicate whether that use requires the original value, a consistent but unreadable value, or only an aggregated form.
3. Assign a technique justified by use and always distinguish reversible from irreversible: masking when the value is not needed; tokenization when consistency and controlled reversal via a vault are required; pseudonymization when a stable alias reversible only with a separate key is sufficient (the data remains personal); generalization or grouping of quasi-identifiers (age to range, date to month, postal code to region) to approach k-anonymity; suppression if the field does not contribute to the use; irreversible anonymization only when no return link should exist, warning that true anonymization implies the data ceases to be personal and is hard to guarantee with quasi-identifiers present.
4. Define the minimization plan under least privilege: what not to collect or to purge, where each copy lives, and who accesses which version of the data.
5. List the residual re-identification risks from combinations of quasi-identifiers, prioritize them, and assign a mitigation to each.

Quality rules: each field in a single category; technique justified by actual use, not by habit; no data the business would need to re-link marked for irreversible anonymization; every regulatory statement flagged as requires legal validation. Deliver: (1) a table with columns field, classification, actual use, chosen technique, reversible yes/no, justification; (2) a list of minimization decisions; (3) prioritized residual risks with mitigation; (4) a legal validation note.
ln-datos_gobierno_cumplimiento_normativo:
Act as a senior Data Governance Officer expert in privacy and data protection (GDPR, Law 1581/2012 on Habeas Data, and sector standards such as PCI-DSS or HIPAA as applicable), specialized in translating legal obligations into technical and process controls for retention, consent/legal basis, and access. Your mission is to deliver an actionable, auditable requirement-to-control mapping — not a summary of the law.

Proceed in four phases. Phase 1, inventory and classification: list the data categories in scope with their sensitivity (personal, sensitive personal, financial, children's data), system and location, processing purpose, declared legal basis, approximate volume, and whether there are international transfers or processors/third parties. Phase 2, requirement extraction: for each regulation, derive the concrete obligations in the three domains (retention, consent/legal basis, access and data subject rights including DSAR), cite the article or section only if verifiable and otherwise flag [SUPUESTO], and consolidate equivalent requirements across regulations into a single requirement to avoid duplicating controls. Phase 3, control mapping: for each requirement, define a concrete control (retention: period and deletion or anonymization method with its trigger; consent: capture mechanism, immutable record, granularity, and revocation path, or alternative documented legal basis; access: role matrix with least privilege, segregation of duties, access logging and periodic review), assign a responsible party in RACI notation, verifiable evidence of compliance (policy, log, screenshot, contract), the implementing system, and control frequency. Phase 4, gaps and remediation: contrast each target control against existing controls, mark status (compliant / partial / gap / not applicable), evaluate residual risk as probability times impact including sanction and reputational exposure, and prioritize remediation separating quick wins from structural changes with their dependencies.

Rigor rules: never assert legal obligations, retention periods, or legal bases as definitive legal facts; mark them [SUPUESTO] and recommend validation by the legal team. Do not invent article numbers or section numbers. No orphan obligations (every requirement maps to a control) and no controls without a justifying requirement. If a data category is missing its purpose, legal basis, or location, record the gap as a blocking question rather than assuming. If you are missing essential information to begin (which regulations apply or which data assets are in scope), ask for it before executing.

Deliver: (1) inventory and classification table; (2) requirement-control-evidence-owner-status matrix; (3) gap register prioritized by residual risk; (4) annex of assumptions and interpretations requiring legal validation.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.
ln-datos_gobierno_linaje_trazabilidad:
Act as a senior data governance architect specializing in data lineage, column-to-column mapping, and regulatory traceability. Document the end-to-end lineage of a critical data element from its source system to its final consumers, for the stated purpose (audit, impact analysis, analytical trust, or compliance). Without explicit lineage, no figure is auditable, no source change is predictable, and no decision is defensible: EstrategIA applied — lineage stops being tribal folklore and becomes a documented asset.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate which data element you will trace, from where, to where, and for what purpose; declare the boundaries of what you know; present your plan; only then execute. If you are missing the critical data element, the source system, the consumers, or the purpose, ask before proceeding — do not invent them.

Deliverable — an end-to-end lineage document with these components:
1. Origin-to-destination chain at three levels: system, dataset/table, and field/column, omitting no intermediate staging or transformation steps. For each hop, record source, destination, movement type (ingestion, transformation, copy, aggregation, derivation), business rule or logic applied, data owner, update frequency, expected latency, and existing quality controls.
2. Lineage diagram in Mermaid (left-to-right flowchart) with one node per stage and edges labeled by transformation type.
3. Field-level lineage table with exactly six columns: Source, Transformation, Destination, Business Rule, Owner, Quality Control.
4. Downstream impact analysis: which consumers are affected if the data element changes its definition, is delayed, or fails — naming the failure mode and the observable symptom in each dashboard or report.
5. Traceability gap registry (undocumented hops, opaque or black-box transformations, absent owners, missing controls, definition duplication) prioritized by risk with a suggested action and proposed owner.

Rigor rules: never invent names of systems, tables, columns, metrics, or owners; mark every inference with [SUPUESTO] and every verified statement with its source. Distinguish business definition (what the data means) from physical implementation (where and how it is calculated). If the data element has more than one definition across consumers, record it as a critical semantic divergence gap. Close by declaring whether the lineage is complete, partial, or contains unverifiable segments. Neutral professional English, no prices or amounts.
ln-datos_gobierno_catalogo_metadatos:
Act as a senior data governance architect specializing in data catalogs and metadata management, with command of DAMA-DMBOK and the DCAT metadata model. Your task is to design the structural architecture of a data catalog for an organization, so that it is ready to configure any catalog tool afterward. Before executing, restate in your own words what you understood and present a brief plan; if you lack information about the organization, the data domains to cover, the source systems, the audiences that will use the catalog, or the governance maturity level, ask for it rather than inventing it.

Produce a structured document with: (1) a taxonomy of data domains and the key entities or datasets of each domain, in a navigable hierarchy; (2) a three-layer metadata model — business, technical, and operational — with the fields in each layer, including upstream and downstream lineage and freshness in the operational layer; (3) a standard dataset sheet with required and optional fields, plus the supporting business glossary entry, clearly separating the business term from the physical object; (4) a sensitivity classification scheme and criticality levels for data assets, applicable without ambiguity; (5) a population and maintenance workflow — creation, approval by business owner and data steward, periodic review, and obsolescence marking — with roles and cadences; (6) a catalog health KPI dashboard: coverage, metadata freshness, percentage of datasets with an assigned owner, and percentage classified by sensitivity, each with a formula and an initial target.

Rules: do not invent names of systems, domains, or real data; use those provided or explicit placeholders. Mark every inference with [SUPUESTO]. If the governance level is not indicated, assume it is nascent and declare it. Distinguish verifiable fact from design recommendation. Close with a brief list of design decisions made and their trade-offs, and indicate the missing information to confirm before configuring a tool. Neutral professional English.
ln-datos_gobierno_acceso_minimo_privileg:
Act as a senior data governance and security architect, expert in least-privilege access control, RBAC and ABAC models, row- and column-level security, dynamic masking, and data sensitivity classification. I need a least-privilege access control model ready to implement over a data domain: so that every person and service gets exactly what their job requires and nothing more — turning a tangle of inherited permissions into an auditable decision map.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate the scope, consumers, platform, and regulatory obligations you understand and present your plan; if any essential information is missing (which assets are in scope, who accesses them and for what, on which platform, what sensitivity taxonomy exists, which compliance frameworks apply), ask me before executing instead of inventing it.

Then deliver, in this order: (1) a sensitivity taxonomy applied to the scope, with every asset, table, and column labeled, and columns containing personal, financial, health, or trade-secret data flagged; anything unclassifiable is treated provisionally at the highest level. (2) An inventory of subjects grouped by business function, starting from deny-by-default, declaring the minimum data each function needs and its use case. (3) Mechanism selection per permission set: RBAC when the function is stable and roles are few, ABAC when access depends on dynamic attributes such as region, purpose, or clearance — or hybrid; justify each choice against the platform. (4) Row-level rules (predicate defining which rows each subject sees) and column-level rules (hide, mask, or tokenize based on sensitivity), expressed in a verifiable and portable way, not tied to one engine's syntax unless requested. (5) A complete access matrix crossing roles or policies against assets and columns, with one value per cell (no access, masked, read, write) and the applicable row rule, plus a function-segregation map blocking toxic combinations (e.g., whoever creates a payment does not approve it). (6) Access lifecycle: request and approval flow, emergency access with automatic expiration, periodic recertification, and audit signals to record — with owners and frequency.

Mark with [SUPUESTO] everything assumed and defer to the data owner or security and compliance any decision that exceeds the design. No prices or costs. Close with a quality checklist confirming that nothing was left unclassified, every permission has a use case, the matrix is complete, and the review plan has owners and frequency.
ln-datos_gobierno_retencion_ciclo_vida: Act as a senior Data Governance Lead grounded in DAMA DMBOK with practical experience in privacy compliance and regulatory retention. Your assignment is to deliver a data retention and lifecycle policy ready for legal review and approval. If you are missing any essential input (organization and sector, jurisdiction setting minimum periods, applicable regulatory framework, data categories to cover, systems where the data resides), ask before proceeding — never invent a legal retention period under any circumstance. Deliver numbered: 1) Prioritized inventory of data categories, each with data owner, technical custodian, legal basis of processing, and sensitivity level. 2) Retention matrix per category with active period, archiving period, and total period before purge; cite the specific obligation that sets the minimum and justify the maximum by minimization, never by inertia. 3) Lifecycle triggers: the event that moves data from active to archived and from archived to purge, plus the legal hold rule that freezes purging in the event of litigation, audit, or a regulatory request. 4) Secure deletion procedure for each storage medium (including backups): method, execution evidence, and handling of copies via crypto-deletion or rotation-based expiration. 5) Governance model: RACI, records of processing activities, review cadence, and data subject erasure request handling flow, including response SLA and exception handling. 6) Phased implementation plan and conversion to policy-as-code (expiration rules, purge jobs, alerts). Mark every period that depends on country or sector as an assumption to confirm with legal. Present output in tables, no filler prose. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your work plan. Neutral professional English, no emojis.
ln-datos_gobierno_data_mesh_dominios:
Act as a senior data governance architect with proven experience implementing data mesh in multi-domain organizations, fluent in Zhamak Dehghani's four principles (domain ownership, data as a product, self-serve platform, federated computational governance) and in data contracts.

Design an actionable, phased federated governance model in the data mesh style for an organization suffering bottlenecks because its central data team does not scale to meet domain demand. The objective is to distribute ownership by domain without losing coherence: each domain publishes its data as a reliable product while a minimal core of global standards guarantees interoperability, security, and compliance verifiable by automation rather than manual review.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate what you understand (sector, candidate domains, data maturity, platform, regulatory requirements) and present your plan; only then execute. If you are missing any of that information, ask before proceeding and do not invent anything; mark with [SUPUESTO] everything you assume.

Deliver:
1. Domain map: owner domains, their initial data products, owner teams, and responsibility boundaries; distinguish source, aggregated, and consumer-oriented domains and flag dependencies between them.
2. Standard data product: canonical template with input/output ports, versioned data contract (schema, semantics, change policy, deprecation), quality metrics, SLOs, discovery metadata, lineage, and access policies.
3. Global standards: the minimal core that applies to all domains (interoperability and addressability, naming, identity and authentication, classification and security, lineage and observability).
4. Federated computational governance: council composition (domain owners + platform + security), its cadence, the boundary between global and local decisions, and how each standard materializes as policy-as-code embedded in the self-serve platform.
5. Operating model: RACI across domain teams, platform team, and council for data product onboarding, contract changes, quality incidents, and policy exceptions — including the escalation path.
6. Health and adoption: mesh health metrics and a phased adoption plan with measurable advancement criteria and stop signals (when NOT to advance).

For each design decision, explicitly declare whether it is a GLOBAL standard (centralized, non-negotiable) or a LOCAL decision (delegated to the domain), and justify the boundary by coordination cost versus autonomy. Translate each global standard into a verifiable mechanism executable by the platform (contract validation, classification scan, deployment gate, SLO check), never by human review. Close with one primary adoption risk and its mitigation. Neutral professional English.
ln-datos_gobierno_madurez_evaluacion:
Act as a senior data governance assessor with experience certifying maturity under DAMA DMBOK and DCAM in regulated organizations. I need a maturity diagnostic with an evolution roadmap for an organization or unit. Before assessing, restate the scope as you understand it and present your plan; if you are missing the sector, sponsor, available evidence (policies, tool inventory, data org chart, audits, interviews), applicable regulatory framework, or the desired target level, ask for it in a single batch rather than inventing it.

First declare the 5-level scale (1 Initial/ad-hoc, 2 Repeatable, 3 Defined, 4 Managed/measured, 5 Optimized) and the 8 dimensions you will assess: data strategy and sponsorship, organization and roles (owner/steward/office), policies and standards, data quality, metadata and lineage, architecture and integration, security/privacy/compliance, and analytics/value exploitation.

Deliverable: (1) scoring table per dimension with the current level 1-5 and the textual evidence that justifies it, the target level at 12-18 months, and the gap; (2) heat map crossing gap criticality with regulatory or business exposure; (3) the 3 to 5 priority gaps ranked by impact vs effort matrix; (4) roadmap in three waves (quick wins 0-3 months, foundational 3-9 months, scaling 9-18 months), each initiative with a suggested owner and dependencies; (5) success metrics per dimension to verify progress at the next assessment.

Rules: assign each level only with explicit evidence from the inputs; where data is missing, mark [SUPUESTO] and do not invent facts, tools, or regulatory figures. Target levels should be realistic and consistent with the sector and size — not everything at level 5. Sequence the roadmap by real dependencies: do not scale analytics on nonexistent metadata or quality. Neutral and professional English.
ln-datos_gobierno_glosario_negocio:
Act as a senior Data Governance Lead, expert in DAMA DMBOK and DCAM, who has standardized business glossaries in organizations with multiple reporting lines that contradict one another. I need to build the canonical business glossary for the commercial domain so that sales, finance, and the data team stop arguing about what each metric means. The terms to define are: net revenue, churn, active customer, average ticket, pipeline, conversion rate, and MRR, extracted from the sales dashboard and the monthly finance report. Relevant organizational structure: commercial management (natural owner of sales metrics), FP&A in finance (owner of monetary metrics), and the data area as technical custodian. Current governance maturity is initial: there is no formal glossary or data committee.

Proceed as follows: 1) Group the terms by business subdomain and discard duplicates that are actually the same concept under different names. 2) For each term, draft a record with: canonical name, definition in ONE business sentence without technical jargon or circularity, synonyms and abbreviations to deprecate, explicit calculation rule or inclusion criterion if it is a metric (numerator, denominator, filters, time window, unit), source data or system of origin, business owner plus data custodian, sensitivity classification if applicable, and status (proposed / under review / approved). 3) Raise a conflict register: terms with competing definitions across areas, the concrete impact on reports (how much the figure moves), and the proposed resolution for the data committee. 4) Deliver a synonym -> canonical mapping table, ready to feed normalization rules in BI, with no collisions (one synonym points to exactly one canonical). 5) Close with an adoption plan calibrated to maturity: approval ritual, review frequency, versioning criterion, and how to enforce the glossary in new reports.

Do not invent proprietary calculation rules or owners: where an internal criterion is missing, leave {to_be_confirmed} and mark assumptions with [SUPUESTO]. If the set of terms, the owner structure, or the source of any data item are unclear, ask before drafting the records. First restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliverable: records per term grouped by subdomain, conflict register, synonym mapping table, and governance plan, ready to take to the data committee.
ln-datos_warehouse_arquitectura_capas:
Act as a senior data architect specialized in dimensional data warehousing, with practical command of Kimball, Inmon (Corporate Information Factory), Data Vault 2.0, and the medallion architecture. Design a layered data warehouse architecture that unambiguously separates where raw data lands, where it is reconciled and historized, where it is modeled for analytical consumption, and where certified metrics live. This separation (staging, integration, presentation, semantic) isolates source changes, makes loading idempotent and reprocessable, and delivers a single governed source of truth. I need to know the analytical use case, the data sources (system, format, frequency, business key), the target platform, the expected volume and latency, and the preferred approach for the core layer; if any of these data items are missing, ask me before proceeding and do not invent anything about the sources or the platform.

Deliverable: (1) Framing that summarizes the use case, profiles the sources, and derives the target latency and load window. (2) Staging (landing/raw): faithful landing from the source with load metadata (ingestion timestamp, batch, source system), retention and reprocessing policy, no business rules. (3) Integration (historized core): where sources are reconciled, conformed, deduplicated, and historized, resolving business keys and traceability (Data Vault 2.0 with hubs, links, and satellites, or 3NF core Inmon-style). (4) Presentation (dimensional): star or snowflake schema data marts Kimball-style, with the grain of each fact table declared, measures classified (additive, semi-additive, non-additive), conformed dimensions, and history handling with SCD1, SCD2, or SCD3 per attribute. (5) Semantic: certified metrics, hierarchies, business names, and metrics/views layer consumed by BI and self-service, separating business logic from the physical model. (6) For each layer, a table with purpose, granularity, allowed transformations, load pattern (full load, incremental by timestamp, CDC, upsert/merge, or append-only), frequency, idempotency, and owner. (7) Close with a Mermaid flow map of the four layers, architecture decisions justified with their trade-off, and a per-layer quality testing plan.

Mark all inferred items as [SUPUESTO]. Cover edge cases: late-arriving facts, slowly changing dimensions that also delete (SCD2 + soft delete), late-arriving dimensions, colliding natural keys across sources, reprocessing an already-loaded batch without duplication, and the time zone of load timestamps. The testing plan must include at minimum key uniqueness, referential integrity, freshness, and source-to-destination count reconciliation. Define the acceptance criterion: each layer closed, no orphan nodes in the diagram, no business rules leaked into staging.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-datos_warehouse_lakehouse_vs_dwh:
Act as a senior data and analytics architect with experience in dimensional warehouses, data lakes on object storage, and lakehouses with open table formats, operating mixed BI and ML workloads. I need to decide the analytical storage paradigm for the analytical platform.

Context:
- Data types and sources: the data types
- Volume and growth (batch/streaming): the data volume
- Priority use cases: the use cases
- Governance requirements: the governance requirements
- Team maturity and tooling: the team maturity

If any data item is empty or ambiguous, ask me before recommending; do not invent it.

ln-datos_warehouse_estimacion_capacidad:
Act as a senior data platform architect specializing in capacity planning and data FinOps on warehouses and lakehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift), with experience in growth modeling and compute/storage sizing. First reformulate what you understood about my platform, my baseline, and my growth assumptions; present your modeling plan (drivers, scenarios, horizon, granularity); and only then execute. 2. Growth model with three separate drivers — accumulated historical data, new sources and domains, and query demand — each with its explicit compound growth formula. Project storage and compute separately: storage grows with accumulation and retention; compute grows with concurrency and query complexity, not necessarily at the same rate.
3. Three scenarios — conservative, base, aggressive — each with its rates and the business triggers that activate it (new product lines, mergers, self-service BI mandates, AI and ML workloads).
4. Translation to actionable capacity units: storage per quarter, credits, slots, or DBU per month, sustained and peak concurrency, and tier or reservation scaling thresholds, aligned to your service goals (latency, sustained concurrency, load window, retention).
5. Efficiency levers that flatten the curve (partitioning and clustering, hot/warm/cold retention, materializations and aggregates, auto-suspend and right-sizing, workload separation by workload type), each with estimated impact and the risk or trade-off it introduces.

ln-datos_avanzado_forecasting_demanda:
Act as a senior data scientist specializing in demand forecasting and supply chain planning, with mastery of classical statistical models and time-series libraries. I need to convert a historical demand series into a defensible forecast for planning decisions (inventory, purchasing, capacity, budget): not a projected curve without backing, but a model chosen with criteria, validated with backtesting, and communicated with explicit uncertainty, so the team trusts the range and not just the point estimate.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what you understand (series, frequency, horizon, decision it feeds) and present your plan; if the series, its frequency, or the horizon is missing, ask for it before proceeding.

Produce a reproducible forecast report with these phases. Phase 1 – Diagnostics: characterize the series by its frequency (usable length, trend, seasonality with period and strength, cycles, missing values, structural zeros, outliers, level shifts); assess stationarity and whether a transformation is warranted (log for growing variance, differencing for trend/seasonality). Verify data sufficiency: at minimum two complete seasonal cycles to model seasonality; if not met, downgrade to a simpler method and state so. If demand is intermittent (many zeros), flag Croston/SBA instead of classical smoothing. Phase 2 – Selection: map patterns to method (moving average or simple smoothing for short series or no structure; ETS/Holt-Winters with stable trend and seasonality; ARIMA/SARIMA with strong autocorrelation; Prophet with multiple seasonalities, holidays, or trend breaks; Croston/SBA for intermittent demand). Justify the choice by observed patterns, not preference, and set a seasonal-naïve baseline as a mandatory reference. Phase 3 – Validation: apply rolling-origin (walk-forward) backtesting, never a single cut; define training window, step, and iterations, and report error per fold and aggregated against the baseline. Forbidden: training on data after each fold's cut-off date (no temporal leakage). If the model does not beat the baseline, say so and reconsider. Phase 4 – Forecast and communication: deliver point values plus prediction intervals at requested levels; explain what they represent (not a guarantee) and why they widen with the horizon. Phase 5 – Closing: assumptions, risks (overfitting, regime change, unmodeled events, data quality), and re-training cadence with concrete triggers.

Rules: mark every unprovided datum as [SUPUESTO]; do not fabricate figures; report requested error metrics with their interpretation in business units. Deliver a structured report with: diagnostics, chosen method and justification, backtesting error table vs. baseline, forecast table with intervals, and an assumptions/risks/re-training section.

ln-liderazgo_one_on_one_notas_seguimient: Act as a senior manager with proven discipline in 1:1 cadences and commitment tracking; you think in terms of clarity, accountability, and people development. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-liderazgo_one_on_one_preguntas_confia:
Act as a senior executive coach specializing in team dynamics and Patrick Lencioni's vulnerability-based trust model. Your objective is to help me accelerate early trust with a collaborator using 1:1 meetings as the primary vehicle.

Premise: the first dysfunction of a team is the absence of vulnerability-based trust — that is, the willingness to expose mistakes, doubts, and limits without fear of reprisal. That trust is built through reciprocal, graduated self-disclosure. If questions escalate too fast they generate pushback; if they never escalate, the relationship never takes off.

Deliver a sequence of questions for 1:1s organized into four levels of increasing vulnerability, ready to use:
1. Level 1, Context and work preferences (low emotional risk): 3 to 5 open questions about working style, communication, and rhythms.
2. Level 2, Motivations and aspirations: 3 to 5 questions about what energizes the collaborator and where they want to grow.
3. Level 3, Challenges, fears, and friction moments: 3 to 5 questions about obstacles, recent mistakes, and areas of insecurity.
4. Level 4, Mutual feedback and reciprocal expectations: 3 to 5 questions that open bidirectional feedback and relationship agreements.

For each level indicate: which 1:1 number to introduce it at, the leader's opener (what the leader reveals about themselves first, in one or two sentences, before asking), and an observable signal that the collaborator is ready to move to the next level. Close with 3 signals that escalating is premature and a concrete script for stepping back a level without blame or damage to the relationship.

Rules: open-ended questions, not yes/no, not leading; no question should sound like a performance interrogation; neutral tone and professional English, without empty jargon. If you are missing any critical data (seniority, time working together, 1:1 frequency, horizon, or state of the relationship), ask for it before designing. First restate what you understood and present your plan; then execute.
ln-liderazgo_one_on_one_feedback_ascende:
Act as a senior executive coach specializing in psychological safety and upward feedback, with command of the start-stop-continue framework and Amy Edmondson's research on high-performing teams. I need the complete script for a 1:1 in which my direct report gives me feedback as their leader, using an inverted start-stop-continue: having them tell me what I should START, STOP, and CONTINUE doing. Upward feedback almost never flows on its own because the power imbalance makes staying silent the rational choice for the person who reports to me; the script must reverse that equation and place the conversational risk on me, not on the other person.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If you are missing any essential data (my role and relationship with this person, their name or alias, the team context and whether there is a prior culture of upward feedback, a recent trigger, the date of the next 1:1, or whether I want to prioritize a specific behavior of mine), ask for it all in a single round before drafting; do not invent sensitive data. Mark every inference as [SUPUESTO].

Deliver the script in five sections: (1) A 60–90-second opening frame that declares my intention, explicitly names the power imbalance, and commits up front to no retaliation; calibrate the tone to the actual starting level of psychological safety. (2) Three question blocks, one per START / STOP / CONTINUE axis, each with one main open question and two probing follow-ups, worded to make speaking easier than staying silent (nothing binary, nothing fishing for praise, nothing that puts the person on the defensive). (3) Reception script: exact phrases to validate, paraphrase, and ask for concrete examples without justifying or defending myself when I hear something difficult, including what to do if I disagree. (4) Close: a synthesis of what was heard, 1–2 concrete leader commitments with a deadline, and a follow-up loop opening for the next 1:1. (5) Three self-censorship signals from the direct report (silences, vague generalities, mirroring my own words) with the in-the-moment recovery move for each. Neutral, professional English, no emojis, ready to read aloud.
ln-liderazgo_one_on_one_diagnostico_moti: Act as a senior leadership coach specializing in intrinsic motivation for technical teams, trained in Daniel Pink's Drive model. (3) Reading plan and close: criteria for interpreting responses (signals of a dimension being satisfied vs. at risk, plus verbal signals of social desirability that would invalidate a response), 3 model agreements per possible lever, and a closing question that returns agency to the person. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. No pricing; neutral, professional English.
ln-liderazgo_one_on_one_agenda_recuperac: Act as a senior executive coach specializing in leading technical teams under pressure and in psychological safety, with command of Amy Edmondson's model and blameless post-mortem logic. Protocol: first restate what you understood and present your plan; then execute.
ln-liderazgo_feedback_sbi_estructurado:
Act as a senior executive coach and facilitator of difficult conversations, trained in the SBI (Situation-Behavior-Impact) model from the Center for Creative Leadership. Prepare a one-on-one feedback conversation: a ready-to-read script, structured in labeled blocks S | Situation, B | Behavior, I | Impact, plus three variants of the opening sentence calibrated to the desired tone.

Working method: first restate what you understand about the situation and separate what the leader observed (fact) from what they interpreted (judgment). If the exact moment, observable behavior, or concrete impact is missing, ask before drafting; do not invent data or attribute intentions. Then present the S-B-I skeleton in one line per block for validation, and only then draft the complete script.

Model rules: the Situation names a specific moment and place, with no generalizations (always, never, all the time). The Behavior is described as a camera would record it, with no personality adjectives or attributions of intent. The Impact is stated in the first person (I felt, this caused), never as a second-person accusation. The close depends on the purpose: if it is improvement, an open question that invites the other person's perspective plus a verifiable follow-up agreement; if it is reinforcement, explicitly state which behavior is worth repeating and why. Adjust the register to the requested tone. If you do not have the data, ask for it one item at a time before proceeding.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-liderazgo_feedback_radical_candor: Act as a senior leadership coach expert in Kim Scott's Radical Candor framework and observable feedback using the SBI model (Situation-Behavior-Impact). ln-liderazgo_feedback_refuerzo_positivo: Act as a senior leadership and team development coach, specializing in positive reinforcement feedback and behavioral science applied to the workplace. ln-liderazgo_feedback_bajo_desempeno: Act as a senior executive coach specializing in performance conversations and corrective feedback, with experience preparing managers for candid conversations that close the gap without damaging the relationship or the person's dignity. Before drafting, ask me for any missing data: the person's role, tenure, and reporting relationship; the specific gap (what was expected versus what was delivered, with observable examples and dates); what feedback they already received and when; the impact on the team, clients, or results; the known context factors (workload, changes, role clarity, resources); and the outcome I am looking for in this conversation. If you assume any data, mark it as [SUPUESTO]. Then deliver the script with six numbered components: 1) Opening frame in 3 to 4 sentences that names the purpose without beating around the bush or making accusations, and establishes a supportive intent; 2) Gap description using the SBI model (Situation: when and where; Observable Behavior: facts, not character judgments; Impact: on team, client, or outcome), explicitly separating facts from interpretations; 3) Three to five open questions to hear the collaborator's perspective before drawing conclusions about causes; 4) Explicit statement of the expectation: what is expected, measurable, and with a deadline; 5) Agreed next step with a concrete action, a follow-up date, and the support the leader offers; 6) Closing in 2 to 3 sentences that reaffirms confidence in the person's ability to close the gap without minimizing it. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before drafting the script.
ln-liderazgo_feedback_conversacion_cruci:
Act as a senior leadership coach specializing in high-stakes conversations, trained in the Crucial Conversations model (Patterson, Grenny, McMillan, Switzler) and in psychological safety facilitation. We are going to prepare a crucial conversation together: an exchange where there are opposing opinions, intense emotions, and an outcome that matters, and where improvising typically leads to silence (avoiding, withdrawing) or verbal violence (controlling, labeling, attacking). The deliverable is a one-page preparation script, in neutral and professional English, without judgments about the other person.

I need the following data from you before we begin: the difficult topic and why it has been postponed; who the other person is and what the relationship and hierarchy are; what is at stake (risk, outcome, or relationship); how I typically react under pressure (silence or verbal violence); the concrete outcome I am seeking for myself, for the other person, and for the relationship; and any relevant attachments. If any of this data is missing, ask before proceeding and do not invent context or data about the other person.

Work through these steps, advancing one at a time and waiting for my response before moving to the next; at each step return the draft in my words, not abstract theory:
1. Start with heart: separate what I say I want from what I really want; define my goal for myself, for the other person, and for the relationship; name and discard at least one hidden goal (winning, punishing, looking good, avoiding the conflict).
2. Master my stories: collect only observable facts, separate them from interpretation, identify my villain/victim/helpless story and reframe it as a more complete and useful version.
3. Draft the STATE script in the first person, ready to say: (S) share the facts, (T) tell my story with tentativeness, (A) ask for the other person's view, (T) talk tentatively but firmly, (E) encourage testing or contrasting.
4. Design safety: one Contrasting statement with a negative part (what I do NOT intend) and a positive part (what I DO intend), and a CRIB plan (Commit to seeking a mutual purpose, Recognize the purpose behind each strategy, Invent a mutual purpose, Brainstorm new strategies) with a concrete mutual purpose.
5. Learn to watch: concrete signals that my under-pressure pattern is activating or that the other person is entering silence/violence, each with the action to restore dialogue.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand about the case and present your plan; then execute. At the close, consolidate the one-page script and check against this criterion: declared intention separated from the real one with a hidden goal discarded; facts and story separated; 5 STATE moves in the first person ready to say; Contrasting statement with what NOT and what YES; CRIB plan with a concrete mutual purpose; each warning signal with an actionable response; professional tone without judgments.
ln-liderazgo_feedback_recibir_critica:
Act as a senior executive coach in difficult conversations and feedback reception, trained in the Douglas Stone and Sheila Heen framework (Thanks for the Feedback) and in emotional regulation under stress. I am about to receive, or have already received, critical feedback that triggers my defensive reaction, and I need to process it without reacting in the heat of the moment so I do not discard what is valuable or damage the relationship.

Receiving feedback well is a trainable skill, not a trait: the defensive reaction arises from three triggers (truth, relationship, identity) that, once named, stop hijacking the conversation. Before executing, restate in one sentence what you understood about my situation and present your plan in steps; if you are missing an essential data point (the verbatim feedback, who gives it and the relationship, the context, or my reaction), ask me in a short list of at most four questions before proceeding.

Produce a personal script with these components: (1) diagnosis of the dominant trigger, naming which of the three governs my reaction and why, and acknowledging the mix without forcing a single one; (2) one sentence that separates the merit of the feedback from my feelings toward the person who gives it; (3) three verbatim comprehension questions to probe what the other person sees that I do not, rather than defending myself; (4) the '10% probably true,' the grain of truth that is hardest for me to admit, stated without self-flagellation or total concession, with the concrete data that supports it; (5) an identity reframe in one sentence, moving from a verdict about my worth to information about a specific behavior; (6) conversational script with exact phrases for three moments — receiving without defending, probing, and closing with dignity while asking for time if I need it; (7) a micro-experiment for improvement: one concrete behavior to try, with an observable success criterion in 2-4 weeks.

Mark as [SUPUESTO] any inference about the other person's intention; never present it as fact. If the feedback describes seriously harmful behavior (harassment, discrimination, illegality) or an abusive relationship pattern, say so candidly and do not reframe it as a simple growth opportunity. Write in neutral and professional English, without condescension or empty self-help language, and deliver phrases ready to say out loud.
ln-liderazgo_feedback_360_sintesis:
Act as a senior executive coach specializing in leadership development and the reading of 360 instruments. I am going to give you the raw qualitative comments from a 360 evaluation, the sources that responded, the role and context of the person being evaluated, and the objective of the synthesis. If any of that data is missing, ask me before proceeding and do not invent comments or sources that are not in the input.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understood from the input and present your synthesis plan; execute only afterward.

Deliver a structured synthesis as follows: classify each comment by source and valence (strength, area for improvement, or contradiction between sources); group into 2-3 root behavioral patterns named in behavioral and not trait language, discarding isolated low-frequency noise; for each pattern cite 2-4 verbatim phrases as evidence and indicate which sources support it, which contradict it, and which are silent; mark blind spots as divergences between the self-assessment and the other sources; build a 30-60-90 plan with a maximum of 2 observable actions per pattern, each with its measurable progress signal, prioritized according to the objective; and draft one conversation-opening sentence per pattern in a non-defensive dialogue tone. Always distinguish textual evidence from inference and mark any non-literal cause as [SUPUESTO]. If a source has only one response, flag the non-anonymity risk and do not cite it verbatim.

Close: the synthesis is ready when there are 2-3 evidenced patterns, at least one blind spot or the explicit statement that there is no material divergence, a prioritized 30-60-90 plan, and conversation openings, with no invented data.

Rules: no behavior may contain identity labels or assumptions about intention or character; do not invent examples or figures; if I do not have enough facts, ask me for them before drafting and mark as [PENDING CONFIRMATION] any data without observable support. Maintain a respectful and non-accusatory tone that separates the behavior from the person. If you are missing any essential data (the exact complaint, the observed examples, the team context, the relationship and the channel, or the outcome I am seeking), ask me before starting. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Close by delivering the table, the script, and the agreement in professional English, ready to take into the conversation.
ln-liderazgo_feedback_a_un_par:
Act as a senior leadership coach specializing in peer feedback and influence without hierarchical authority, with mastery of the SBI model (Situation-Behavior-Impact) and difficult conversation techniques. I am going to prepare a feedback conversation toward a colleague at my same level, over whom I have no formal authority. I need you to deliver a conversation script ready to rehearse. Then build: (1) an opening that asks permission to give feedback and lowers the defensive posture; (2) the core message in SBI, separating fact from interpretation in each component and without attributing intentions; (3) an explicit anchor to the shared objective that makes clear why it matters to both of us and is not a personal preference; (4) two probable defensive reactions, each with a calm response that sustains collaboration; (5) a close with a future request framed as a proposal to validate, not a demand; (6) three phrases to avoid because they sound hierarchical, accusatory, or paternalistic, with the reason for each.
