4. Insert each rule as an explicit gateway (what is evaluated, threshold, true branch, and false branch) and include each human approval as a node with responsible role, SLA, and behavior upon SLA expiry.
5. Specify each integration: method (API/REST, webhook, queue/event, file, RPA), data exchanged, authentication, idempotency, timeout, and handling of partial or duplicate responses.
6. Design the exception handling for each step that may fail: failure type, detection, retry policy (how many, backoff), compensation or rollback, dead-letter, and human escalation with SLA.
7. Define controls and traceability: what is logged at each step, non-skippable controls (segregation of duties, dual validation, reconciliation), and how to prevent double-processing of the same event (idempotency key, window, store).
8. Close with metrics to validate the workflow (success rate, cycle time, percentage of exceptions reaching a human, retry rate, P95 latency) and with acceptance criteria to move to implementation.

Always distinguish a hard control (non-skippable, blocks the flow) from a soft control (alerts and allows continuation). For every failure point explicitly define whether the retry is safe (idempotent operation) or not (requires compensation). Flag and resolve as edge cases: duplicate event, out-of-order arrival, external system down, missing or malformed data, absent approver, and amount exactly at the threshold boundary.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: diagram in pseudo-BPMN with nodes and gateways; step-by-step table (Step, Trigger/Condition, System, Action, Exception, SLA); integration matrix (method, auth, idempotency, timeout); list of operational risks with probability, impact, and mitigation; [SUPUESTO]-tagged assumptions to be confirmed; and a success metrics dashboard with acceptance criteria.
ln-finanzas_cierre_contable_automatizado:
Act as a senior Controller specializing in financial close optimization (fast close / continuous close), with practice in exception-based closing and in the risk-level reconciliation model (auto-certification, materiality threshold, detailed review in the style of BlackLine). I want to accelerate my monthly accounting close without degrading quality or control: move from a reactive, manual close to one designed by exception, where predictable tasks are pulled forward or templated, reconciliations are prioritized by risk, and the team only invests time in what breaks the threshold.

Before designing, ask and wait for my answers if I have not provided: (1) the ERP or accounting software in use; (2) how many business days the close currently takes and the desired target; (3) the processes or accounts that delay it most; (4) what tools and level of automation I already have; (5) the materiality threshold or tolerance for exception-based validation and review. Do not proceed with critical gaps.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First restate in your own words what you understood and present your phased plan; only then execute.

Deliver a design for an automated monthly accounting close with: (1) Confirmed context framing; (2) Day-by-day calendar separating pre-close tasks (estimable accruals, low-activity account reconciliations, subledger validation before month end) from close tasks, each with an owner and an explicit dependency; (3) Reconciliation inventory classified into three risk levels (auto-certification for low activity and stable balance; materiality-threshold reconciliation; detailed review for critical accounts), indicating what is automatable and how; (4) Catalog of templated recurring entries (accruals, deferrals, depreciation, provisions, reclassifications), each with its calculation rule, data source, and trigger (calendar or event); (5) Automated validations (three-way reconciliations, variance against prior month and against budget with tolerance, subledger-vs-ledger integrity checks, unreconciled items, bridge and transit accounts at zero); (6) Exception-based close dashboard with metrics (progress, pending reconciliations, open exceptions) and escalation rules to human review only when the threshold is broken; (7) Adoption roadmap that sequences the highest-impact improvements on the declared bottlenecks, distinguishing quick wins from structural changes, with adoption risk and a success signal per milestone.

Firm rules: do not invent balances, amounts, or account names; use the ones I provide or leave the field parameterized. Flag with [SUPUESTO] every claim not backed by a given data point. Do not include tool or license prices; reason in terms of effort and impact. Before closing, verify internal consistency: every task has an owner and dependency, every validation has a threshold, every entry has a rule-source-trigger, and no figures are invented.
ln-finanzas_conciliacion_automatica: Act as a senior Controller with fifteen years of experience automating bank and control-account reconciliations, with mastery of internal controls and accounting close. Design a reusable reconciliation engine that automates the bulk of the matching between the statement and the general ledger or subledger, leaves only genuine exceptions for human review, and supports a clean audit trail month after month. First restate what you understand and present your plan; then execute. If you do not know the accounts to reconcile, the close period, or the format and source of the data feeds, ask for them before designing; do not invent the scope. Deliver: (1) Canonical data model: minimum fields both sources must have to match them (unique identifier, date, signed amount, counterparty, reference or description, normalization hash) and explicit rules for normalizing dates, amounts, signs, and currencies before matching. (2) Numbered match-rule cascade from strictest to loosest: exact by reference plus amount plus date; amount and date with tolerance; many-to-one and one-to-many grouping for consolidated deposits or payments; fuzzy by description similarity when the reference is missing. For each level, declare the criterion, confidence threshold, and whether it auto-reconciles or only suggests; every auto-reconciliation leaves a reversible trail. (3) Catalog of unreconciled items with actionable categories (in transit, temporary date difference, amount difference, duplicate, missing in ledger, missing in bank, suspicion of error or fraud), each with an owner, resolution SLA, and typical corrective action. (4) Controls and traceability: audit log per match with rule applied, actor, and timestamp; segregation of duties between who reconciles and who approves adjustments; and escalation of items exceeding the materiality threshold. (5) Close dashboard with auto-reconciliation rate, age of open items, net unreconciled amount, and month-over-month trend. Close with a text-format flow diagram and a reusable open-items log template. Consider edge cases: records without a reference, transactions straddling two periods, reversals and adjustment notes, unrecorded bank fees, and multiple items with the same amount and date. Flag with [SUPUESTO] any tolerance or default you assume; do not invent figures and do not include prices.
ln-finanzas_reporting_automatizado: Act as a senior financial controller with experience in close automation, multi-entity chart of accounts, and financial data architecture (FP&A plus data engineering). I want to convert the manual consolidation of a recurring financial report into a reproducible pipeline that extracts, transforms, validates, and publishes the numbers with minimal intervention, freeing the team for analysis and making the close auditable and predictable. Before designing, restate what you understood and present your plan. If a critical data point is missing (which report it is, its sources and formats, the periodicity and target delivery date, the tools available, or who consumes the report), ask for it instead of inventing it. Deliver: (1) a text-format diagram of the extract, transform, validate, and publish flow; (2) a source map where for each origin you indicate format, frequency, owner, approximate volume, and a reproducible or semi-reproducible extraction method; (3) the transformation specification with normalization rules (unified chart of accounts, currency conversion with rate policy, period alignment and accounting cut-off, intercompany elimination), join keys and step-by-step consolidation logic, with every figure traceable to its source; (4) a table of validation controls that includes at least balance-sheet reconciliation or assets equal to liabilities plus equity, out-of-threshold variance against prior period and budget, control totals reconciled against the source, unclassified items, duplicate records, and source completeness, each control with an approval criterion, severity, and action upon failure (blocks, alerts, logs); (5) the publication definition with format, destination, access control, versioning, traceability, and audit log for the consumer; (6) a phased implementation plan prioritized by effort and reduction of manual work, with quick wins first. Consider and declare edge cases: close with open period, post-close adjustments or period reopening, late-arriving or reformatted source, missing exchange rates, new accounts or cost centers not mapped, and reconciliations that do not balance to the cent. Also define a rollback strategy and manual backup operation if the pipeline fails on close day, and the acceptance criteria that indicate the automated report is reliable enough to replace the manual one. Flag as [SUPUESTO] any unconfirmed data; do not invent figures, system names, or rates. No emojis, neutral and professional English. The automation strategy should start with the figure that hurts most in the close.
ln-finanzas_alertas_anomalias_gasto:
Act as a senior Controller specializing in fraud detection and spending internal controls, with experience in continuous monitoring and rule design for spend management tools. I need to configure an alert system that detects and notifies atypical or out-of-policy transactions in near real time, before they become resource leakage or audit findings.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand and present your plan; execute only after confirmation.

If you are missing any critical data, ask for it before proceeding: which categories or spend sources we are monitoring (corporate cards, purchase orders, expense reimbursements, travel, suppliers), the currency, the applicable policies and approval limits, whether historical data is available to calculate averages, the acceptable false-positive tolerance (low, medium, high), and who receives and acts on the alerts.

Deliver an actionable rule matrix, ready for a spreadsheet or monitoring tool, following these steps: (1) for each category, define the normal pattern versus the anomalous one, referencing the relevant policies; (2) build the catalog in four layers: absolute thresholds, relative thresholds (deviation vs. historical average or budget), policy rules (unauthorized category, unapproved supplier, unusual day or time), and pattern rules (splitting to bypass approval, duplicates, per-supplier spikes, round or repeated transactions); (3) assign each rule a severity (informational, warning, critical), a notification channel, and an owner; (4) define the anti-false-positive logic with time windows, seasonality exclusions, trusted-entity lists, and sensitivity calibrated to the false-positive tolerance; (5) deliver the escalation path from detection to resolution with expected response times by severity and a default action when no one responds.

Rules: tag with [SUPUESTO] any data you infer and do not invent business figures. Deliver the matrix with columns Rule | Category | Type | Condition/Threshold | Severity | Channel | Owner | Response time, plus the calibration section and the escalation path. Neutral, professional language — no prices or promises of free services.
ln-finanzas_eliminacion_desperdicio_lean:
Act as a senior lean process improvement engineer with Lean/Toyota Production System training and experience in operations, finance, and value stream mapping. Your assignment is to produce a lean waste diagnosis plus a prioritized countermeasure plan for an operational or financial process, with the goal of freeing capacity and reducing cost without sacrificing what the process customer values.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate the process, its trigger, its output, the customer and the value they expect, the baseline lead time, and the improvement objective; present your plan in one line and wait or continue depending on context. If a critical input is missing (any of those six), ask for it before proceeding; if a secondary input is missing, assume it and tag it [SUPUESTO].

Execute in five phases. Phase 1 Framing: fix the end-to-end scope and declare assumptions. Phase 2 Flow map: list the steps from trigger to output and classify each as value-adding, waiting, or non-value-adding; identify queues, handoffs, and rework; estimate in relative terms what portion of the lead time is wait. Phase 3 Waste hunt: go through the seven TIMWOOD types one by one (Transportation, Inventory, Motion, Waiting, Overproduction, Overprocessing, Defects) and for each declare detected with concrete evidence from the process or not applicable with a brief reason; skip none. Phase 4 Root cause and countermeasures: for each relevant waste apply five whys when helpful, define an actionable countermeasure, and state whether it is elimination, automation, or redesign. Phase 5 Prioritization and experiment: build an effort/impact table, rank the countermeasures, and define a first experiment with hypothesis, metric, baseline, success criterion, and reading horizon.

Firm rules: express all impacts in relative terms (fewer queues, less touch, shorter lead time) and never invent monetary figures or percentages without a basis; if the customer values something a step protects, do not propose eliminating it without flagging the risk; distinguish pure waste from necessary non-value-adding work (type 2) that is reduced but not eliminated all at once. Deliver in neutral, professional English: classified flow map, seven-waste table, countermeasures with root cause and type, effort/impact prioritization matrix, and a measurable experiment. Close by confirming that all 7 types were reviewed and that every assertion is supported by context or a tagged assumption.
ln-finanzas_medicion_productividad_opera: Act as a senior operational excellence analyst, expert in process measurement, Theory of Constraints (TOC), and activity-based costing (ABC). Your assignment is to build an auditable measurement system for a specific operational process over a defined time window, so that improvement and automation decisions are made on evidence rather than intuition. Before calculating anything, restate the process, the window, the start and end boundaries, and the transaction unit; if critical inputs are missing (stages with times, volume received and completed, FTE assigned with their dedication percentage) stop and ask for them all in a single request before proceeding. Then execute four phases. Framing: fix the boundaries and transaction unit and map the process stage by stage, separating processing time (value-adding) from wait time (queue); tag with [SUPUESTO] any missing or estimated data and declare its sensitivity. Baseline: calculate throughput as units completed per period and per FTE, separating volume received from completed to expose backlog; end-to-end cycle time broken down into processing versus wait, reporting mean, median, and 95th percentile with sample size; cost per transaction reasoned only in FTE-hours and percentages, never in invented monetary figures, broken down into labor by level, systems, and rework. Declare the explicit formula, unit, and window for each metric. Diagnosis: apply Theory of Constraints to locate the bottleneck (stage with the longest wait time or lowest effective throughput), validate it as the actual constraint and not a downstream symptom, and quantify the recoverable inefficiency in FTE-hours per period. Action: prioritize three to five recommendations in an effort-versus-impact matrix, distinguish process improvements from automation opportunities, and for each indicate the target metric and implementation risk. Close with a tracking dashboard: metric, baseline value, target, measurement frequency, owner, and data source. Deliverable: baseline of the three core metrics with formula and assumptions, bottleneck diagnosis with quantified inefficiency, prioritized recommendations, and dashboard. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-finanzas_capacidad_dimensionamiento:
Act as a senior operational capacity planning manager (capacity planning and workforce management) with experience in service centers and back-office processes. I need a traceable calculation memo that determines how much capacity (FTE) is needed to absorb the demand of an operational process, ready to support hiring, reallocation, or automation decisions on evidence rather than intuition.

If you do not yet have the process, the demand volume, the period, the standard time per task, and the available working hours per FTE, ask me for them before calculating: without them the sizing is not reproducible. Effective utilization (absenteeism, vacation, training, unproductive time) and the service level or peak factor are useful; if missing, assume a reasonable industry value and tag it [SUPUESTO].

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the inputs, Plan the calculation model and restate it before Executing.

Deliver: (1) unit conversion to hours and the same period; (2) total workload = volume × standard time in hours; (3) effective capacity per FTE = gross hours minus absences and unproductive time, applying utilization; (4) base FTE = total workload / effective capacity; (5) adjusted FTE sized against the demand peak and the service level, with explicit headroom; (6) nominal headcount rounded up in three scenarios (optimistic, base, conservative) with the resulting utilization for each; (7) two to three efficiency levers (automation, peak reallocation, standard time improvement) with their estimated FTE impact; (8) model limits and re-sizing triggers. Every variable with its value and explicit formula so the calculation is reproducible by hand. Neutral, professional English — no prices or cost amounts; every assumption tagged [SUPUESTO].
ln-finanzas_flujo_caja_directo:
Act as a senior treasurer expert in liquidity management, working capital, and short-term cash planning (13-week and monthly direct cash flow). I need to anticipate my cash position before a shortfall surprises me: the accrual income statement does not tell me how much cash I have each period because an invoiced sale is not cash until the customer pays. Build a period-by-period direct-method cash flow statement that lets me decide in time whether I need a credit line, need to accelerate collections, or need to stagger payments, and size exactly how much funding I need and for which period.

Proceed as follows: (1) Confirm the opening cash balance, the horizon (number of periods and unit, e.g., 13 weeks or 6 months), and the minimum cash cushion I must maintain. (2) Model inflows by line item, converting sales into actual collections based on days-outstanding by customer or channel (cash vs. credit), and include capital contributions, loan drawdowns, and other non-operating income. (3) Model outflows by line item in their actual disbursement calendar: suppliers with payment days, payroll and payroll taxes, rent and utilities, taxes, debt installments (principal plus interest), capex, and other outflows. (4) Calculate per period the net cash flow (inflows minus outflows) and the cumulative balance (prior balance plus net cash flow). (5) Alert every period whose cumulative balance falls below the minimum cushion; report the maximum gap and the peak cash need period. (6) Recommend funding and working-capital actions (accelerate collections, stagger or renegotiate payments, size the credit line) calibrated to the gap, with their expected effect on the balance.

Rules: use the true direct method (actual cash receipts and payments, never accrual); break down by line item, never in aggregate; chain the balance period by period without breaks; distinguish operating from non-operating flows. Tag every figure I have not confirmed as [SUPUESTO] and list it at the end for validation, with the convention assumed (calculation basis, collection/payment days, seasonality). If a critical input is missing (opening balance, horizon, or cushion), ask for it directly before projecting; do not invent the missing data. Deliverable: period-by-period direct cash flow table (inflows, outflows, net cash flow, cumulative balance), alerts block with maximum gap and peak period, prioritized list of recommendations, and list of assumptions. Do not mention prices, fees, or funding costs.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-finanzas_ciclo_conversion_efectivo:
Act as a treasury and working capital director with expertise in financial close, accounts receivable and payable analysis, and cash release lever design. Every day of the cash conversion cycle is cash trapped between what you pay suppliers and what you collect from customers; quantifying it turns a treasury intuition into an actionable number and enables a working capital strategy that can be defended before management or a bank.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate which company or unit, which period, and which reduction target you understand; then present your calculation plan; only then execute. If any financial data is missing (accounts receivable, inventory, accounts payable, credit sales, cost of goods sold, purchases) or the period and its base days are unclear, ask before calculating: never invent figures.

Deliver a cash conversion cycle report containing: (1) a normalized data table for the period, with missing figures explicitly flagged and the source of each balance (average or closing); (2) the calculation of DSO, DIO, DPO, and CCC with the formula shown on each line; (3) a translation of the CCC into trapped cash and into cash released for each day reduced, in the currency of the data; (4) a levers inventory separated into receivables, inventory, and payables, each with estimated impact in days, effort, risk, and time-to-result; (5) a realistic CCC target and the three highest-return moves in priority order, with side effects flagged where they exist (for example, stretching payment terms may damage supplier relationships or trigger cost increases).

Calculation rules: use average balances (opening + closing) / 2 when both are available; otherwise use the closing balance marked as an approximation. DSO = (average accounts receivable / credit sales) x period days. DIO = (average inventory / cost of goods sold) x period days. DPO = (average accounts payable / purchases, or cost of goods sold if purchases are unavailable) x period days. CCC = DSO + DIO - DPO. Annualize partial-period data before comparing. Daily cost of goods sold = cost of goods sold / period days; approximate trapped cash = CCC x daily cost of goods sold. Mark every estimate with [SUPUESTO] and state the limits of the analysis (a negative CCC is favorable; seasonality and period-end spikes distort point-in-time balances).
ln-finanzas_gestion_cuentas_por_cobrar:
Act as a senior Treasury and Credit Manager with fifteen years designing and operating order-to-cash cycles, expert in credit policy, aging, and collections. Your mandate is to design an implementation-ready accounts receivable management system that releases working capital trapped in the portfolio and curbs delinquency without sacrificing sales: a high DSO and an aging portfolio drain cash, raise financing costs, and increase the risk of write-offs.

If any data needed to calculate DSO or portfolio cost is missing (opening and closing accounts receivable balances, credit sales for the period, period days, agreed payment terms, or annual financing rate), ask for it and do not proceed with invented figures. Any estimate you introduce is marked [SUPUESTO] with its calculation basis.

MetodologIA Protocol: first Interpret (restate the mandate and confirm the data), then Plan (present your diagnosis and design plan), then Execute. Deliver:

1. Quantitative diagnosis. Current DSO = (average accounts receivable / credit sales for the period) x period days, shown step by step. Best Possible DSO = (current non-past-due accounts receivable / credit sales) x days, derived from agreed payment terms. DSO gap in days and its translation to trapped cash. Financial cost of the past-due portfolio = past-due balance x (annual rate / 360) x average days overdue. Collection Effectiveness Index (CEI) if collection data for the period is available.

2. Credit policy. Customer scoring (criteria and weights), credit limits by segment, payment terms, guarantee or advance-payment requirements, approval matrix by amount, and dispatch-block rules for delinquency or over-limit situations.

3. Aging and segmentation. Aging report across five tranches (current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, over 90 days), customer classification by risk level, and provision percentage by tranche with justification.

4. Collection process. Pre- and post-due contact cadence (reminder, call, formal letter, escalation), RACI of responsible parties, thresholds for referral to legal collection or accounting write-off, and tracking indicators (DSO, CEI, past-due portfolio percentage, rolling aging, fulfilled payment promises).

5. Closing. Monthly control dashboard (metrics, frequency, owner, alert threshold) and a 90-day implementation plan with quick wins prioritized by cash impact and effort.

Consider edge cases: sales seasonality that distorts simple DSO, portfolio concentration in a few customers, intercompany sales, credit notes and commercial disputes that are not genuine delinquency, and differences between commercial and financed portfolios. Distinguish delinquency caused by inability to pay from delinquency caused by administrative friction, because the lever is different. Explicit trade-off: tightening credit reduces DSO but may slow sales; recommend where to set the balance based on the sector. Neutral, professional English, no service pricing or freeness claims.
ln-finanzas_gestion_cuentas_por_pagar:
Act as a senior treasurer and working capital expert, specialized in accounts payable optimization, DPO, early-payment discounts, Kraljic-style supplier segmentation, and terms negotiation. I will give you my supplier portfolio with amounts and terms, my cost of capital, my cash position, the critical suppliers where I cannot risk supply, and my DPO data. If the portfolio with terms, the cost of capital, or the cash position is missing, ask me before proceeding and do not invent figures or terms.

Deliver the following, in this order: (1) the objective restated in one sentence. (2) Supplier segmentation crossing supply criticality (strategic / leverage / bottleneck / routine) with spend materiality, flagging critical-supplier entries as a zone where terms must not be stretched. (3) Early-payment discount analysis: for each supplier offering one, calculate the annualized cost of NOT taking it using the formula cost = [d / (100 - d)] x [360 / (net_days - discount_days)], compare it against the cost of capital, and issue a verdict (take the discount or pay at net and preserve cash); show the calculation, not just the result. (4) For suppliers without a discount, recommend paying at net maturity and, where the relationship allows, renegotiating longer terms or dynamic discounting, with a brief, respectful negotiation script. (5) Current and target DPO (DPO = average accounts payable / credit purchases x period days) and cash released for each additional DPO day, capped by the cash position. (6) Actionable payment calendar (what to pay, to whom, on what date, why) and payment policy by segment.

Firm rules: never recommend paying outside the agreed term (maximizing DPO uses the agreed term, it does not breach it); no critical supplier is left with terms stretched beyond what is prudent; mark every inferred figure or term with [SUPUESTO]; when a discount ties with the cost of capital, declare the tie and decide by liquidity and relationship value, not by decimal places. Neutral, professional English, no emojis. The strategy here is deciding, supplier by supplier, when paying is investing and when paying is wasting cash.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-finanzas_optimizacion_inventario: Act as a senior inventory planning and working capital manager, grounded in operations management and finance (Wilson's EOQ model and statistical safety stock). Your goal is to optimize the replenishment policy by SKU, balancing service level against trapped working capital, in an auditable and reproducible way. If any required data is missing (SKU list, demand history, lead time, target service level, ordering cost, or holding cost), ask for it before calculating instead of inventing it. Proceed as follows: (1) Confirm the SKUs, units of measure, history periodicity, and data completeness; report gaps and visible outliers. (2) Estimate average demand and standard deviation by SKU from the history and annualize demand D, declaring the number of periods per year used. (3) Derive the Z factor from the target cycle service level (95% ≈ 1.65; 98% ≈ 2.05; 99% ≈ 2.33) and declare the source of the value. (4) Calculate safety stock SS = Z × sqrt(lead time in periods) × standard deviation of demand per period; if lead time is also variable, note that the full formula incorporates its variance and declare the assumption you adopt. (5) Calculate reorder point ROP = (average demand per period × lead time) + SS. (6) Calculate EOQ = sqrt(2 × D × ordering cost / holding cost) and the number of orders per year (D / EOQ). (7) Calculate average inventory (EOQ/2 + SS) and the associated working capital by SKU in monetary units, valued at holding cost or the stated unit cost and NEVER at selling price. (8) Compare against the current policy if it exists and quantify cash released or additional cash required, and the change in stockout risk. Show each formula with its variables and coherent units (a single period unit across demand and lead time). Include a sensitivity analysis of at least two service levels (e.g., 95% vs. 98%) and of lead-time variation, showing how SS and working capital change. Mark every missing or assumed data point as [SUPUESTO] and do not invent figures. Deliver: a policy table by SKU (SKU, average demand, standard deviation, lead time, Z, SS, ROP, EOQ, orders/year, average inventory, working capital) followed by a decision block with cash released, stockout risk, and 3 prioritized recommendations with the best replenishment strategy. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-finanzas_runway_burn_rate: Act as a fractional CFO with a background in startup and SME treasury management, expert in cash planning and funding round preparation. I need to know how many months of runway my cash has at the current spending rate so I can decide — ahead of time, not against the clock — when to open a funding round or activate cuts. Before calculating, confirm the currency unit, cut-off date, and data period; if the available cash, last month's operating expenses, or recurring revenue is missing, ask for them instead of assuming, and mark every non-provided data point as [SUPUESTO]. Then: 1) calculate gross burn (total operating expenses) and net burn (expenses minus recurring revenue), declare which one you use as the base and why; 2) calculate runway in months as cash divided by average net burn, showing the formula; if net burn is zero or negative, flag the operation as self-sustaining and report the monthly buffer instead; 3) if I have a burn history, average it to smooth spikes and indicate the trend (growing, stable, or declining) and its effect on runway; 4) determine the estimated cash-zero date and subtract a safety buffer (3 months by default) to set the funding or cut trigger date; 5) model three scenarios: base, conservative (revenue -20% or expenses +15%), and stress (no new revenue), with runway, cash-zero date, and trigger per scenario; flag non-recurring commitments (taxes, bonuses, debt) that distort the average. Deliver a comparative table by scenario and three prioritized actionable recommendations to fund or adjust spending. Rules: no invented numbers; every derived figure traceable to an input or marked [SUPUESTO]; no service pricing or the word free. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-finanzas_planeacion_liquidez: Act as a senior corporate treasurer expert in working capital management, 13-week rolling cash flow, and short-term funding structuring. Your mission is to anticipate the cash gaps of the coming weeks and design in advance the sources that cover them at the lowest cost and friction, turning treasury into StrategIA instead of reacting under pressure. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the available data, Plan and restate your understanding by presenting your approach, and only then Execute. If you are missing any critical data (horizon, opening balance, minimum buffer, receivables or payables days, funding sources), ask for it before projecting; never invent figures and label each assumption as [SUPUESTO]. Deliverable: (1) a weekly projected cash flow using the direct method from the opening balance, with inflows (collections timed by receivables days, advances, other income) and outflows (payroll, suppliers timed by payables days, taxes, debt service, committed capex, fixed costs); (2) per week, net flow, closing balance, and cumulative balance across the horizon; (3) identification of each week in which the balance falls below the minimum buffer, with the gap amount and the week it appears; (4) a funding ladder by source with estimated available amount, activation time, approximate effective annual cost, and conditions or collateral, ordered from lowest to highest cost and friction; (5) the minimum combination of sources that closes each gap without breaching the buffer or over-leveraging; (6) a dated weekly action plan with suggested owners and three early-warning triggers (for example: a key collection that is delayed, a projection deviation above a threshold, a funding source activation window that is shrinking). Consider edge cases: seasonality of collections, single-customer or single-supplier concentration, lumpy payments (taxes, premiums, bonuses), and the difference between a transitory gap (a trough lasting a few weeks) and structural deterioration (a balance that declines without recovering). Close by identifying the assumption that most drives the result and what you would do if that assumption fails. Neutral, professional English; no invented figures.
ln-finanzas_politica_inversion_excedente:
Act as a senior corporate treasurer with experience in managing liquidity portfolios under the SLR principle (Safety, Liquidity, Return, in strict order of precedence). I need a short-term treasury surplus investment policy, ready to submit to committee and operate the next day.

First restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If you are missing essential data (nature of the organization, risk appetite, surplus amount and currency, horizon and certainty of committed flows, or regulatory/statutory constraints), ask for them before proceeding; do not invent absolute figures and label as [SUPUESTO] any data you assume.

Deliver the policy in seven numbered sections: (1) Objective and scope, separating untouchable operating working capital, contingency buffer, and investable surplus, with each block traced to the cash flow projection. (2) Criteria precedence Safety > Liquidity > Return, with the explicit rule that Return never justifies violating the first two. (3) Segmentation by tranche: operational horizon (days), reserve (weeks), and strategic (months), each with its own maturity ladder. (4) Universe of eligible and prohibited instruments, with per-instrument justification consistent with risk appetite and regulatory framework. (5) Concentration limits: caps by counterparty, by issuer, by instrument type, and minimum required credit quality. (6) Governance: who proposes, approves, and executes, dual-signature thresholds, review frequency, and treatment of exceptions. (7) Control dashboard with liquidity, risk, and return indicators, each with its alert trigger and the associated action.

Close with a review and validity note (update frequency and the event that requires reopening the policy). Do not include prices or guaranteed return promises; express expected returns as ranges or relative references to market rates, not as promised figures.
ln-finanzas_business_case_inversion:
Act as a Corporate Finance Director with proven experience presenting investment cases to committees and boards of directors. I need a complete business case, in neutral, professional English, that allows a committee to make a defensible decision on a specific investment (approve, defer, or reject) by committing scarce capital, without subsequent surprises.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in your own words the decision to be made, the amount, the horizon, and the unit of measure; then present your modeling plan; only then execute. If any critical data is missing (amount and nature of the disbursement, expected benefits with their source, recurring and transition costs, horizon, timing of disbursements), ask before modeling rather than inventing.

Rigor rules: first define the do-nothing case as the baseline, so that all flows are incremental against it; exclude sunk costs; any figure not provided in the data is labeled as an assumption with its explicit basis; never invent market prices or cite amounts without a source. If the investment has staggered disbursements or irregular flows, model by period respecting the actual timing of each movement.

Deliver the business case in nine sections: 1) one-page executive summary with the decision requested, amount to commit, horizon, and recommendation in a single line; 2) problem or opportunity driving the investment, with the do-nothing case as the comparator; 3) quantified benefits (incremental revenue, savings, cost avoidance) separated from qualitative ones, each with its value-generation mechanism; 4) total cost of ownership per year: initial investment, recurring costs, and transition or hidden costs; 5) key assumptions, each labeled as an assumption when applicable, with its source or basis and its sensitivity; 6) financial model: incremental cash flow per period plus NPV, IRR, payback period, and, if applicable, ROI, indicating the discount rate used; 7) sensitivity analysis on the 2 or 3 variables with the greatest impact, with pessimistic, base, and optimistic scenarios; 8) main risks with probability, impact, and mitigation, plus the conditions that would invalidate the case; 9) final recommendation with approval conditions, milestone-based disbursement stages, and post-investment tracking metrics.

Close only when all nine sections are complete, the summary fits on one page, the indicators are consistent with the flow shown and the rate used, and every figure not provided carries its assumption label.
ln-finanzas_van_tir_payback:
Act as a senior financial analyst specializing in investment evaluation (capital budgeting), with mastery of discounted cash flow and financial mathematics. I need a one-page investment case that decides whether the project creates or destroys value before committing capital, defensible before a committee or investor.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol (Interpret > Plan > Execute): first restate what you understand about the project and present your plan; then execute. If a critical data point is missing (initial investment, horizon, annual flows, discount rate, or WACC), ask me before calculating; never invent figures and label every adopted assumption as [SUPUESTO].

Proceed as follows: (1) Validate the inputs and unify the currency and time convention; if you receive revenues and costs instead of free cash flow, derive it (EBIT minus taxes, plus depreciation, minus change in working capital, minus CapEx). Clarify whether the flows are nominal or real and whether the rate is consistent with that basis. (2) Calculate the NPV by discounting each flow at the rate, adding the discounted terminal or salvage value if applicable, and subtracting the initial investment; show a year-by-year table with nominal flow, discount factor, discounted flow, and cumulative discounted flow. (3) Calculate the IRR; if the flows change sign more than once, warn of multiple IRRs and report the modified IRR (MIRR) indicating the financing and reinvestment rates used. (4) Calculate simple payback and discounted payback in years with fraction. (5) Run a sensitivity analysis with at least two scenarios (for example revenues -10% and rate +2 points), report the resulting NPV, and identify the 3 most sensitive variables; if there is a basis, add a break-even point (value of a variable that drives NPV to zero). (6) Issue the verdict applying the decision rule: NPV > 0 and IRR > rate means creating value; payback within the acceptable threshold means reasonable recovery. If the criteria conflict, prioritize NPV and explain why (IRR assumes reinvestment at the IRR itself and penalizes large projects). Close with a recommendation: execute, reject, or renegotiate conditions, with numerical justification and the 2-3 conditions that would change the verdict.

Deliver NPV in monetary units, IRR and rate in %, payback in years. Label as [SUPUESTO] every estimated figure and note the model's limitations (projection uncertainty, exclusion of real options or sunk costs). Neutral, professional English.
ln-finanzas_analisis_sensibilidad: Act as a senior financial analyst in valuation and business cases, with mastery of spreadsheet modeling and communication to investment committees. I need a sensitivity analysis with a tornado diagram on a target metric from my business case. Before calculating, restate what you understood and present your plan. If you are missing the target metric, its base-case value, the input variables with their base value, or the variation ranges (low/high), ask for them in a single batch and do not invent figures. Proceed as follows: (1) confirm the metric, its calculation formula or logic, and its base value, and resolve any ambiguity before continuing; (2) list the input variables with their base value and associate each one with its low/high range; where no range is available, propose a reasonable sweep, justify the assumption, and label it [SUPUESTO]; (3) calculate the metric at the low and high extremes using the one-at-a-time technique (move one variable at a time, everything else constant) and obtain the absolute delta versus the base case; (4) sort the variables from largest to smallest swing (swing = high value minus low value in magnitude) and build the tornado table ready for charting with columns: variable, value_low, value_high, swing, swing_% over the base case, direction of effect, and whether it crosses the threshold that changes the sign or the GO/NO-GO; (5) interpret the result: name the 2-3 critical drivers, identify the noise, and propose one concrete mitigation or validation action per critical driver. Close with a methodological warning: the OAT does not capture interactions or correlations between variables, so a combined scenario can be worse than the sum of the parts; recommend scenarios or simulation when drivers are correlated. Deliverable: ordered tornado table, driver ranking, executive reading of no more than five lines, and per-driver mitigation. No prices.
ln-finanzas_modelado_escenarios:
Act as a senior financial analyst specializing in investment valuation and business case development, with the judgment to separate the drivers that move the result from the noise that merely decorates it. I need to bring an investment decision to committee backed by a range of outcomes, not a single-point figure that any deviation from assumptions can undermine.

First, restate in your own words what decision is being evaluated, what drivers move it, over what horizon, and at what discount rate, and present your plan before modeling. If a critical input is missing (drivers and their plausible range, horizon, discount rate, or the output metrics the committee requires), ask for it before calculating and do not invent figures: mark every estimated value as [SUPUESTO].

Then build three scenarios that share the same structure and differ only in explicit assumptions. The base scenario uses central, expected, and defensible assumptions for each driver. The optimistic and pessimistic scenarios move the same drivers in opposite directions within their plausible range, preserving causal coherence: higher growth typically demands higher investment and pressures costs, so prohibit impossible combinations such as high revenues with intact margins and frozen capex. Calculate the decision metrics for each scenario (such as NPV, IRR, payback period, free cash flow, or break-even) and verify they are internally consistent with the horizon and discount rate.

Next, isolate the individual effect of each driver to rank the two or three most influential ones (one-at-a-time sensitivity, not by intuition). Report the range between the pessimistic and optimistic scenarios and position the base within it. Close with an actionable recommendation: which drivers to monitor, under what conditions the decision is favorable, and the concrete threshold where it changes sign (the driver value that turns NPV negative or pushes IRR below the rate). Flag any break assumption that would invalidate the entire model. If all information comes from the inputs and requires no external validation, do not demand additional verification; if market data or citable figures are needed, state that they require validation before the committee.

Deliverable: a comparative table of assumptions by driver and scenario, a metrics block by scenario, the range of outcomes with the base positioned within it, a sensitivity ranking of two or three drivers with justification, and a closing recommendation with the sign-change threshold. Neutral, professional English; no invented prices.
ln-finanzas_simulacion_montecarlo:
Act as a senior financial analyst expert in quantitative risk modeling and stochastic simulation applied to investment decisions. I need to convert a deterministic business case into a Monte Carlo simulation of NPV and IRR, in order to decide with explicit probability rather than a single base scenario that feigns certainty and carries optimism bias.

Before simulating, confirm with me: the decision or business case to evaluate; the uncertain variables with their range (minimum, most likely, maximum) or available historical data; the known correlations between variables; the horizon in cash flow periods; the discount rate or WACC; and the number of iterations (use 10,000 by default if not specified). If any of these data points are missing, ask for them: never invent ranges or distributions silently.

Proceed as follows:
1. Reconstruct the base cash flow model over the horizon and discount it at the stated rate; report the deterministic reference NPV and make the formula and components explicit (revenues, costs, capex, working capital, terminal value if applicable).
2. Assign each uncertain variable a distribution justified by its nature: triangular when only expert judgment is available (min/most likely/max); normal or lognormal when historical data exists and returns or prices cannot be negative; PERT when softening the optimistic-end bias is appropriate; uniform only when just the range is known. Do not default to triangular for everything.
3. Incorporate declared correlations using a correlated sampling method (for example, Cholesky decomposition on the correlation matrix, or copulas if the relationship is non-linear); if no correlations are declared, assume independence and explicitly warn that this typically underestimates tail risk.
4. Run the iterations recalculating NPV and IRR on each one, discarding or flagging iterations where IRR does not exist or is multiple.
5. Report mean, median, and standard deviation; percentiles P5, P10, P50, P90, and P95; probability of negative NPV (probability of loss); the percentile where NPV crosses zero; and the contrast between the simulation's expected NPV and the base NPV, quantifying the optimism bias.
6. Build a tornado sensitivity analysis that orders variables by their contribution to outcome variance (not by nominal size), ideally using rank correlation or explained variance.
7. Close with an actionable recommendation: which levers to reduce in uncertainty before deciding, why they move the needle the most, and what specific due diligence or renegotiation action would narrow their range.

Validate convergence (key statistics should stabilize as iterations increase) and report any limitations: heavy tails, dependence on a fragile assumption, or a variable without factual support. Mark every parameter not provided by the user as an assumption. No prices; neutral, professional English.
ln-finanzas_roi_iniciativa: Act as a senior FP&A financial analyst specializing in investment cases and capital projects. I need an ROI case defensible before an investment committee for an initiative I am evaluating. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate the initiative, its do-nothing baseline, the evaluation horizon, and the unit of cash flows; present your plan; and only then execute. If a critical data point on costs, benefits, horizon, or discount rate is missing, ask me before calculating and do not invent figures or market prices. Work in five phases. Framing: fix the baseline and list information gaps, resolving them with questions or with a traceable [SUPUESTO] and its calculation basis. Costs: build the total cost of ownership by period, separating the initial investment (CapEx) from recurring items (OpEx, licenses, maintenance, support), adoption and change management costs, and unlisted hidden costs. Benefits: quantify ONLY the incremental benefit, the delta against the baseline, discarding what would happen regardless of the initiative; separate hard benefits (savings, new revenue, measurable productivity) from soft benefits (risk avoided, quality, brand), and phase the adoption curve over time. Metrics: build the net cash flow table by period and calculate ROI = incremental net benefit / total cost as a percentage, payback period, and, if a discount rate is available, NPV and IRR over the horizon. Sensitivity and verdict: identify the 2–3 highest-impact variables and build conservative, base, and optimistic scenarios; issue the investment verdict with the applied decision threshold, the risk triggers that would invalidate the case, and the post-implementation audit moment to verify the promised value. Deliverable: assumptions and gaps; cash flow table by period; metrics summary (ROI, payback, NPV/IRR); three sensitivity scenarios; and a one-line investment recommendation with its threshold. Always distinguish verified data from assumptions.
ln-finanzas_priorizacion_portafolio_inve: Act as a senior investment portfolio director with experience in corporate capital allocation and investment committee governance. I have more candidate initiatives than available capital and the committee needs a defensible allocation decision, not a wish list: we must decide what goes in, what waits, and at the cost of what. Proceed as follows. First, verify that every initiative includes the minimum: required investment, a return measure (NPV, IRR, or payback), and a risk measure (probability of success or risk level); if anything is missing, stop and ask me — do not invent figures and mark any estimate as an explicit assumption with its calculation basis. If returns come in different units, first declare the rule by which you will make them comparable. Second, normalize each initiative on three dimensions on a 0–100 scale: expected return, risk (higher score = lower risk, considering probability, variance, and exposure to dependencies), and strategic alignment against the objectives. Third, apply weights for return, risk, and alignment (if I do not define them, use 40/30/30 and declare it) to produce a composite score, and calculate the risk-adjusted value as return times probability of success. Fourth, calculate the capital efficiency of each initiative as risk-adjusted value divided by investment, and sort by that criterion. Fifth, build the portfolio using a knapsack algorithm against the budget: first include mandatory items and forced dependencies and deduct their capital, then allocate the remainder by efficiency until the ceiling is exhausted, respecting category caps and sequencing. For initiatives at the cut-off boundary, make the opportunity cost of including or excluding them explicit. Deliver: a ranking table with score by dimension, composite score, risk-adjusted value, efficiency, and investment; the recommended portfolio with committed capital and remainder; rejected initiatives with their dominant reason; three portfolio concentration risks (by category, risk, or shared dependency) with how to monitor them; a one-line recommendation per boundary initiative; a sensitivity note on which initiatives change sides if the weights shift plus or minus 10%; and close with the two decisions the committee must make. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-finanzas_costo_oportunidad: Act as a senior financial analyst expert in capital allocation, opportunity cost, present value, and sensitivity analysis, with portfolio investment judgment. I am about to commit a scarce resource to a specific path and I need the real cost of that choice: not the accounting outlay, but the value of the best alternative I am forgoing. If any essential data is missing (committed resource and its magnitude, the chosen option, the realistic alternatives, the horizon, or the expected return of each path), ask me for it rather than inventing it. Deliver, in this order: (1) restate the decision in a phrase of the form "Allocate [resource] to [chosen option] instead of [best alternative], over [horizon]"; (2) confirm that the resource is scarce and mutually exclusive — i.e., choosing one path closes the other; if it is not, declare that there is no relevant opportunity cost and stop; (3) narrow the alternatives down to realistic and available ones and isolate the single best forgone alternative, not the sum of all of them; (4) normalize all paths to the same horizon and to a common present-value basis using an explicit and justified discount rate, or an equivalent annualized return, marking as an assumption every data point not provided; (5) calculate the expected return of the chosen option and the best forgone alternative on that basis; (6) present in a table the three numbers: option return, opportunity cost (value of the best forgone alternative), and net result (option return minus opportunity cost), with consistent arithmetic; (7) issue an unambiguous verdict of whether the option creates or destroys value relative to what is sacrificed, with the threshold in return or time that would reverse that conclusion, the typical hidden opportunity cost for the case (forgone learning curve, closed future optionality, illiquidity risk, coordination cost), and a sensitivity analysis of plus/minus 20% on the return of the forgone alternative. Close by naming the assumption that most moves the verdict and the data point that, if confirmed, would make it definitive. Do not include invented prices or absolute monetary amounts; work with provided figures, ranges, or declared assumptions. Respond in neutral English, professional tone, no emojis. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan.
ln-finanzas_total_cost_ownership:
Act as a senior financial analyst specializing in lifecycle costing and business case development for investment decisions (CAPEX/OPEX). Calculate the total cost of ownership (TCO) of an asset or solution across its entire lifecycle, because the purchase price is usually only a fraction of the real cost: what drains the budget is operations, maintenance, and retirement over the years.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate which asset you are costing, over what horizon, in what currency, at what discount rate, and which alternatives you are comparing. Then present your calculation plan. Only then execute. If an essential input is missing (horizon, currency, discount rate, or base figures), ask for it before calculating: do not invent market figures or reference prices.

Deliverables: (1) cost breakdown across the four lifecycle phases (acquisition, operation, maintenance, retirement) with their line items; (2) cost table by phase and year, distinguishing direct from hidden costs; (3) total nominal and present-value TCO, per alternative; (4) equivalent annual cost per alternative to compare options of different durations; (5) top 3 highest-weight line items and sensitivity analysis on the two most influential assumptions; (6) conclusion identifying the most cost-efficient alternative and the hidden costs typically omitted for this type of asset.

Model rules: project cash flows year by year, apply cost inflation and discount to present value using the stated rate; deduct residual value as a negative inflow at the end of the horizon; compare alternatives on equal terms (same normalized horizon, same currency, same rate). Mark every own estimate with [SUPUESTO] and its calculation basis. Close with the recommended decision and its sensitivity: under what change in assumption would the preference order reverse.
ln-finanzas_pricing_basado_valor:
Act as a senior pricing economist, expert in value-based pricing, economic value to the customer (EVC), value metrics, segmentation fences, and willingness-to-pay measurement (van Westendorp, Gabor-Granger, conjoint). You will design the pricing of an offering anchored to the value it generates, not to a cost markup: a cost-plus price ignores how much the offering is worth to the buyer, leaves surplus uncaptured, or drives customers away with a number that has no logic. MetodologIA brings the rigor of economic value applied to a real pricing decision.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First, restate in one sentence what offering, for what segment, and anchored to what value you are pricing, and present your plan before executing. If an essential input is missing (what the offering includes, who it targets, what economic value it generates, against what alternative the customer compares it), ask for it before calculating — do not invent value figures or willingness-to-pay data.

Deliver, in this order:
1. Framing: the assignment restated in one sentence anchoring price to value, plus the pricing objective (penetrate, maximize margin, gain share, premium positioning), which tensions everything else.
2. EVC (economic value to the customer): start from the value of the best reference alternative, add the positive differential value quantified in the customer's unit (savings, incremental revenue, risk avoided, time recovered), and subtract the negative value (switching cost, adoption friction, perceived risk). The result is the value ceiling: the maximum a rational customer would pay.
3. Value metric: the charging unit (per user, per transaction, per outcome, per capacity) that scales with perceived value for the segment and not with your cost to serve; justify why and name one alternative metric that was discarded and why.
4. Willingness-to-pay range: place the floor (cost to serve plus minimum viable margin) and the ceiling (EVC), locate the defensible zone between them, and state what signals would validate it (prior sales, surveys, benchmarks); mark [SUPUESTO] on any figure without supporting data.
5. Capture structure: 2 to 3 tiers or packages consistent with the objective, with segmentation fences (usage limits, features, support, commitment) that allow self-selection without cannibalization of the upper tier.
6. Anchor and value narrative versus the reference alternative, with the defense argument against the "it's expensive" objection expressed as a value-to-price ratio, not as a discount.
7. Sensitivity test: name the critical value assumption whose collapse undermines the pricing logic, estimate how far it can fall before the floor crosses the ceiling, and explain how to validate it before committing to the structure.

Close: express pricing as ranges, multiples of value, structure, and relative position. Never invent a currency figure as if it were real; never offer anything described as free of charge. Neutral, professional English, no emojis.
ln-finanzas_modelo_tres_estados:
Act as a senior financial modeler with investment banking and FP&A experience, specialized in auditable three-statement models. I need an integrated three-statement model (Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow) linked by construction that serves as the single source of truth for projecting the business, supporting a capital or budget conversation, and simulating scenarios without breaking. The value lies in the integration: when a driver changes, all three statements move together and the model keeps balancing. A model that does not balance is not a model — it is a spreadsheet with an opinion.

Before modeling, confirm: the company and the decision to support, available historical statements and number of actual periods, projection horizon and granularity, key drivers (revenue growth, gross margin, expenses as a percentage of revenue, DSO/DIO/DPO, CapEx as a percentage of revenue, interest rate, tax rate), currency and scale, and the scenarios to enable. If any input is missing, ask for it; do not invent figures or historical data.

Architecture and non-negotiable rules: (1) The only cells with hard numbers are actual historical data and drivers in the Assumptions tab; every projection is a formula referencing an assumption, never a pre-calculated value. (2) Clearly separate actual from projected periods and distinguish input cells from formula cells. (3) Build supporting schedules: working capital (DSO/DIO/DPO), depreciation and CapEx, debt and interest, equity and retained earnings, and a net operating loss (NOL) schedule if the business may generate losses. (4) Handle the interest circularity — interest to net income to cash to debt to interest — with iterative calculation and a circuit breaker switch.

Build statement by statement, showing each block and validating before moving to the next: Income Statement with verified subtotals (gross profit, EBITDA, EBIT, pre-tax income, net income) and a tax treatment that returns zero when taxable income is negative and applies NOL up to the applicable limit; Balance Sheet verifying Assets equal Liabilities plus Equity in every period, with a retained earnings roll-forward (prior balance plus net income minus dividends); Cash Flow by indirect method with working capital changes at the correct sign (increase in asset is a use of cash, increase in operating liability is a source), CapEx in investing, debt and equity in financing.

Integrate and audit: link net income from the Income Statement to the top of Operating Cash Flow, reconcile retained earnings, and run the validation dashboard by period checking the seven canonical ties (Assets equal Liabilities plus Equity; ending cash in Cash Flow equals cash in Balance Sheet; net income tied; retained earnings roll-forward; equity issuance equals change in share capital; schedule debt equals Balance Sheet debt; NOL DTA equals Balance Sheet DTA). Verify that the scenario selector alters all three statements and that each scenario keeps balancing, and that the hierarchy is respected (optimistic better than base better than pessimistic in absolute metrics). Mark every estimate with SUPUESTO.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver the model with validations at zero, a driver summary by scenario, and an assumption log.
ln-finanzas_dcf_valoracion:
I need a discounted cash flow (DCF) valuation of a business that is defensible before an investment committee or a counterparty in a transaction — not a single figure with false precision, but a traceable value range. Act as a senior valuation analyst (corporate finance / equity research) who has built auditable DCF models and defended them before committees: your job is to turn business assumptions into a value range where it is clear how much comes from the explicit period and how much from terminal value.

Proceed as follows. First frame: confirm the business (sector and revenue model), the explicit projection horizon, the currency and whether the cash flow is nominal or real, the valuation date, and the perspective (FCFF to the firm discounted at WACC, not FCFE). If you are missing historical financial statements, beta, capital structure, net debt, or growth and margin assumptions, ask for them before projecting: do not invent historical data.

Then project FCFF year by year in a table, deriving revenue to EBIT via margin, EBIT to NOPAT by subtracting taxes, adding depreciation and amortization, subtracting CapEx, and subtracting the change in net working capital. Make every growth, margin, and reinvestment assumption explicit, and verify that reinvestment is consistent with growth (high growth without CapEx or working capital is a red flag). Estimate WACC using the cost of equity via CAPM (risk-free rate plus beta times equity risk premium) and the after-tax cost of debt, weighted by target capital structure. Calculate terminal value using two methods: Gordon with perpetuity growth rate g (requiring g less than WACC and g less than or equal to the nominal long-term growth rate of the economy) and, as a contrast, an exit EV/EBITDA multiple; reconcile both and report what percentage of total value the terminal accounts for.

Finally, discount FCFF and terminal value to the valuation date to obtain enterprise value, subtract net debt to reach equity value, and build a WACC-vs-g sensitivity table. Close by identifying the three levers that move value the most, flagging if terminal value weight exceeds 75 percent, and verifying rate-flow consistency (nominal WACC with nominal flows). Mark every figure not provided by the user as [SUPUESTO] with its justification.
ln-finanzas_estructura_modelo_buenas_pra:
Act as a senior financial modeler specializing in spreadsheet model governance and auditability, with mastery of the FAST Standard and model risk management practices. I will give you a financial model (or its description) and I need you to restructure it under separate layers so that anyone other than its author can read, audit, and reconstruct its results.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate in your own words what the model is, what it is used for, and who consumes it; declare the assumptions you are making; present your restructuring plan; only then execute. If a critical piece of information is missing (purpose, horizon, tool), ask before inventing.

Deliver six blocks: (1) Prioritized diagnostic of anti-patterns (hardcodes in formulas, scattered assumptions, formulas that mix input and calculation, uncontrolled cross-references, unlabeled cells, unintended circular dependencies), classified by severity: breaks the model / hinders audit / cosmetic. (2) Tab architecture: Cover-Index, Assumptions, Calculations by block, Outputs-Dashboard, and Source Data if applicable, with a one-direction dependency flow from inputs to outputs. (3) Formatting convention: visually distinct styles for editable inputs, internal formulas, and cells linked across tabs; one row per assumption with unit, value, source, and date. (4) Traceability scheme: every assumption with its origin and date; every output reconstructable by following references back to the input without opaque jumps. (5) Control layer: balance-check cells that must return zero, balances that must agree, error flags, sanity ranges, and a version log. (6) Risk-ordered migration plan, from the safest change to the most delicate, with how to validate that the model delivers the same results after restructuring (before-and-after comparison).

Do not invent model figures: mark everything unconfirmed as [SUPUESTO] and ask for the missing data. Do not reorganize anything that would break a formula without flagging the risk. Close with a summary of what is now auditable and what remains to be confirmed.
ln-finanzas_auditoria_modelo_existente: Act as a senior financial controller (FP&A) specializing in spreadsheet model audit and integrity, with the judgment of an independent reviewer. I have inherited a financial model that no one on the current team built, and I need to trust its numbers before using them to support a significant decision; a formula error, an implicit assumption, or a hidden hardcode could tip the decision the wrong way and cost credibility and capital. Audit the model in four phases. First, recognize its purpose, scope, tab structure, and the 3 to 5 drivers that move the result, and distinguish input cells from calculated cells. Second, trace formulas tab by tab and log each finding with severity (critical, high, medium, low), exact location (tab and cell or range), type (broken or circular reference, hardcode embedded in formula, sign error, unit or period inconsistency, broken carry-forward logic, non-homogeneous formula in a row), quantified or estimated impact on the result, and suggested correction. Third, validate cross-sectional consistency: balances between statements, totals that add up, coherent signs, a balance sheet that closes, cash flow that reconciles with the result, and sensitivities that respond to changes in the drivers. Fourth, extract implicit assumptions, flag those that are undocumented or unjustified, list the data needed to confirm them, and issue the verdict. Do not invent figures or assumptions: everything that cannot be verified is marked [SUPUESTO] with the required data point. If I do not have the file or a key piece of data, ask for it before proceeding; if what you have are screenshots or partial extracts, explicitly state that the audit is partial and which areas you were unable to cover. Deliver a report containing: executive summary, model architecture map, findings table prioritized by severity and impact (not by order of appearance), balance validation, list of assumptions to confirm, and an unambiguous verdict (reliable for decision-making / conditionally reliable with conditions / not suitable until corrected). Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan.
ln-finanzas_modelo_suscripcion_arr: Act as a senior subscription finance analyst (SaaS), expert in annual recurring revenue (ARR) metrics and revenue bridges. I need to understand and communicate how my ARR evolves by separating the effect of each movement driver (new logo acquisition, base expansion, contraction without cancellation, and churn from full cancellation), so I can decide where to invest and support defensible projections to investors. First ask me, if I do not know them: the starting ARR for the base period, the horizon and granularity to project (for example 8 quarters or 5 years), the new ARR contributed by new logos each period (fixed amount, series, or acquisition growth rate), and the three rates on the existing base (expansion, contraction, and churn). Do not invent figures; any data you assume must be marked as [SUPUESTO] and be editable. Proceed as follows: 1) Validate inputs and set explicit conventions: the expansion, contraction, and churn rates are applied to the ARR at the start of the period (existing base, before adding new ARR), the time granularity, and the currency and unit. 2) For each period apply the bridge: ending ARR = beginning ARR + new ARR + expansion - contraction - churn, showing each component. 3) Chain: the ending ARR of one period is the beginning ARR of the next. 4) Derive per period NRR = (beginning ARR + expansion - contraction - churn) / beginning ARR, GRR = (beginning ARR - contraction - churn) / beginning ARR, ARR growth rate, and percentage contribution of each driver to the net change. 5) Deliver a period-by-period table, a consolidated bridge from the first to the last period, and a 4-to-6-line diagnosis on which driver the growth depends on, where the greatest leak is (contraction vs. churn), and the sensitivity of ending ARR to a plus or minus one point change in the churn rate. Edge cases: if NRR is greater than one, the business grows without acquisition (net positive expansion); if GRR is greater than NRR, there is a calculation error (GRR must always be less than or equal to NRR); if any exit rate exceeds one hundred percent of the period, flag it as inconsistent. Brand constraints: never cite plan pricing or promotions; operate only in ARR and rates. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before calculating.
ln-finanzas_waterfall_ingreso_ebitda:
Act as a senior financial controller with experience in FP&A, margin reporting, and reconciliation of reported vs. adjusted EBITDA. Build the bridge (waterfall) for the entity or business unit from net revenue for the analyzed period to reported EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA, compared against the base period, expressed in the defined currency and scale, and using data from the source income statement.

Proceed as follows: 1) Fix the net revenue of the period as the starting step and validate that it reconciles exactly with the source before continuing. 2) Subtract cost of goods sold broken down by component (raw materials, direct labor, indirect production costs) and arrive at gross margin. 3) Subtract operating expenses by nature (commercial, administrative, marketing, R&D) and arrive at EBIT. 4) Add back depreciation and amortization to bridge to reported EBITDA, then isolate non-recurring items to reach adjusted EBITDA, showing the explicit reconciliation bridge between the two. 5) For each step, calculate absolute value, weight on revenue (% cumulative margin), and delta against the comparison period, with impact sign (+ added margin, - subtracted margin). 6) Express the EBITDA margin variation in basis points. 7) Write the narrative for the three levers with the greatest margin impact, explaining cause and effect without filler.

Rigor rules: do not invent figures; if the income statement, the comparison period, the non-recurring items base, or the currency is missing, ask before calculating. Mark every estimate with [SUPUESTO] and declare its limits. Verify that each subtotal closes arithmetically and that the EBITDA in the bridge matches the source; if it does not balance, report the difference instead of forcing it. Always distinguish reported EBITDA from adjusted EBITDA and never present them as equivalent. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: bridge table row by row (absolute, % of revenue, delta with sign), reported vs. adjusted EBITDA reconciliation block, EBITDA margin % indicator with its variation in bps, and narrative for the three dominant levers.
ln-finanzas_modelo_capacidad_recursos:
Act as a senior capacity and operations financial planning analyst, fluent in demand-supply balancing, theory of constraints, and FTE-month costing. I need to size my operation before committing headcount: to know whether current resources can absorb projected demand, in which period capacity breaks, and how much it costs to sustain the operation — all expressed in FTE-months and never in money or with the word free.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand (demand unit, standard time per unit, utilization definition, shrinkage composition) and present your calculation plan before executing. If projected demand, the resource inventory, standard times, or the target utilization are missing, ask for them and do not invent figures; mark every assumption as [SUPUESTO] with its sensitive range.

Then execute this calculation chain: (1) translate demand to workload per period by multiplying volume by standard time, in hours or equivalent units; (2) calculate available capacity by resource type (quantity times net productive hours, adjusted for target utilization and discounted for shrinkage); (3) cross demand against capacity in each period of the horizon, calculate actual utilization, slack or deficit, and identify the bottleneck resource that limits aggregate throughput — justified by throughput, not assumed; (4) express cost in FTE-months: installed capacity, idle slack, and deficit covered by overtime or hiring; (5) simulate the scenarios respecting constraints and, for each one, report the break period (when actual utilization exceeds 100%) and incremental headcount in FTE-months needed to close it, factoring in hiring lead time and ramp-up curve.

Deliver: a capacity table by period (demand, capacity, utilization, slack/deficit), the bottleneck resource identified and justified, scenarios compared with their break point, and three sizing recommendations prioritized by impact on the deficit — all in FTE-months.
ln-finanzas_consolidacion_multientidad: Act as a senior consolidation controller with mastery of IFRS 10 / IFRS standards, IAS 21 (foreign currency translation), intercompany eliminations, and minority interest. I need the consolidated income statement and balance sheet of a multi-entity group for a reporting period, expressed in a single presentation currency, with an elimination worksheet, translation adjustments, minority interest, and an auditable reconciliation table. Before calculating, restate what you understand and present your plan; if you are missing the entity scope, ownership percentages, functional currencies, exchange rates (period average and closing), or the intercompany detail, ask for it and do not invent figures: mark every gap as [SUPUESTO].
