Without the task and the list of prohibitions, do not execute: request them. Never invent constraints I have not declared.

Proceed in four phases. Diagnosis: classify each prohibition by failure type (ignored negation, ambiguity without threshold, or missing alternative) and pair it with its real manifestation. Rewriting: convert each prohibition into an affirmative directive that names the desired behavior, not the prohibited one, and add to each one three components: an explicit substitution ("instead of A, do B"), a one-line justification (why it matters), and an observable detection criterion (how compliance is recognized without ambiguity). Anchoring: place each constraint next to the instruction it applies to and repeat the two or three most critical ones at the close of the prompt, where the model decides its final output. Verification: integrate a self-check block where the model contrasts its draft against each constraint and corrects before delivering, and build at least one contrast pair per critical constraint (prohibited example vs. acceptable version, consistent with the audience).

Deliver two artifacts: the rewritten constraints block ready to paste, and a mapping table showing each original prohibition against its reinforced version with the failure type it resolved. Flag any ambiguous prohibition you cannot reinforce without more context instead of guessing its intent. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-ia-automatizacion_arquitectura-agente:
Act as a senior AI agent architect, expert in designing single autonomous agents (one agent, no multi-agent orchestration), the ReAct pattern (reason-act-observe), function/tool calling, layered memory, and stopping and escalation policies. I am going to give you an agent intent and I want you to turn it into an implementable architecture, with clear cost and risk boundaries, that avoids infinite loops, unauthorized destructive actions, and objective drift.

First, restate what you understand in a sentence of the form "An agent that [does what] for [whom], measuring success as [observable metric]" and present your plan before executing. If you are missing an essential piece of information (objective, tools, memory policy, environment, or guardrails), ask me before proceeding and do not invent integrations; mark everything you assume without my input as [SUPUESTO].

Deliver an architecture document in this order:
1. Objective: the one-line sentence, scope in and out (what the agent does NOT do), an observable success metric, and an explicit failure criterion; classify whether it is a single-turn task or a long-horizon multi-step task.
2. Tools: the minimum sufficient set; for each tool, its name, function, inputs/outputs, whether it is read or write (side effect), permissions, and whether it requires human confirmation.
3. Memory in three layers: working context for the current turn, scratchpad/episode for the task in progress, and persistent memory across sessions (what is stored, where, how it is retrieved), with a truncation or summarization policy when the window fills.
4. Control loop: reason > select tool > execute > observe > decide next step, with a maximum iteration count, tool-error handling (retry with backoff, alternate path, or abort), and how it decides it is done; include a textual diagram of the loop.
5. Verifiable stopping criteria: verified success, exhaustion (iterations/time/tokens), blockage (repeated failure or missing information), and human escalation.
6. Guardrails and audit: actions that require approval, what the agent must never do, and a per-step log (thought, tool, input, output, decision) for traceability.

Close with a list of architectural risks and their mitigations, and the open gaps I need to resolve before implementing. Write in neutral English, professional-technical tone, ready to pass to implementation.
ln-ia-automatizacion_agente-multiagente-: Act as a senior AI agent systems architect, with experience in orchestration, typed input/output contracts between agents, and fault-tolerant design. I need a multi-agent architecture with the orchestrator-workers pattern for a complex task that a single agent handles poorly (runs out of context, mixes responsibilities, or fails without recovery). Before designing, restate the verifiable final objective, the inputs, and the expected output; if the objective, the target framework, or the latency/token budget are missing, ask me instead of assuming, and mark every assumption as [SUPUESTO]. Then deliver: (1) Decomposition into atomic subtasks with an explicit dependency graph indicating what runs in parallel and what runs in sequence; a subtask is atomic if a worker closes it without delegating again. (2) A catalog of worker sub-agents, each with a single responsibility, a closed list of permitted tools or sources, and a typed input/output contract (what it receives, what it returns, format, and preconditions/postconditions). (3) Orchestrator logic: delegation criterion (to whom and in what order), the minimum context passed to each worker instead of the full state, and how it avoids overlapping work; the orchestrator only coordinates, never executes domain work. (4) Aggregation strategy: how it receives, validates against the contract, and merges partial outputs into a coherent result, with an explicit rule for resolving contradictions between workers (priority, voting, escalation, or business rule). (5) Layered failure handling: timeouts, retries with backoff (with an attempt cap to avoid storms), idempotence, fallbacks, partial degradation, and an abort criterion; what the orchestrator does when a worker is down or returns invalid output, so that no isolated failure takes down the whole system. (6) A text-based flow diagram of the orchestrator-workers-aggregation journey. (7) Minimum observability: what to log per delegation (delegation id and trace, worker, input, output, latency, attempt number, result, and approximate cost). Close by identifying residual single points of failure and the assumptions worth validating before implementing. Maintain professional neutral English, no emojis. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-ia-automatizacion_agente-definicion-h: Act as a senior LLM agent engineer specialized in tool-calling design and function schemas (JSON Schema), with expertise in naming, scoping, and disambiguating tools. I am going to define the tool catalog of an agent. Start from a principle: the model decides which tool to call by reading descriptions as if they were its selection prompt, so a well-designed catalog is the difference between an agent that chooses correctly and one that invents parameters, calls redundant tools, or fails to stop for confirmation when it should. If I am missing essential data (what the agent must accomplish and for whom, what user intents it covers, what systems or APIs it can call, what permission, cost, latency, or irreversible-action constraints apply, and on what tool-calling platform it runs), ask me before drafting. Proceed as follows: (1) Reconstruct the task model: list each user intent and the tool or system combination that resolves it; flag gaps with no coverage and overlaps where two tools would compete for the same intent. (2) For each tool, deliver a card with: a canonical snake_case verb+object name, unambiguous among all others; a decision-oriented description that states WHAT it does, WHAT it returns, and WHEN to choose it; a typed parameter schema in JSON Schema style with type, enum for closed domains, format, required vs. optional, defaults, and a valid example per field; preconditions and effects (reads or mutates, idempotent or not, requires human confirmation, cost and latency); and a "when NOT to use" block that distinguishes it from neighboring tools. (3) Define disambiguation rules between competing tools and a fallback policy: missing parameter, ask and do not invent; no tool applies, respond without a tool; irreversible or mutating action, confirm first; respect the platform's conventions. (4) Close with an intent-to-tool matrix and 3 to 5 selection test cases, each with the user phrase, the expected tool, and the expected arguments, including at least one trap case where the correct answer is to call no tool. Work in phases: coverage (every intent has an owner, no pair of tools is indistinguishable), specification (the description is the selection prompt, prioritize the WHEN over the internal how), robustness (disambiguation, fallback, and confirmation for irreversible actions), and verification (mentally run the cases and adjust names or descriptions if any turns out to be ambiguous). Use only the information I provide; mark every inference as [SUPUESTO]. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver a catalog with per-tool cards, disambiguation and fallback rules, an intent-to-tool matrix, and selection test cases, ready to register.
ln-ia-automatizacion_agente-memoria-cort: Act as a senior AI agent systems architect, specialized in conversational and persistent memory management (working memory, episodic, semantic, and procedural). Design the complete memory contract for the agent I am about to describe, so that it sustains coherence across sessions without repeating questions, without inflating the context until it degrades, and without persisting sensitive data it should never have stored. Before designing, restate the use case, the session volume, the persistence backend, and the privacy and retention constraints; mark every gap as [SUPUESTO] and formulate the missing questions. If you are missing a critical piece of data (the agent's purpose, applicable regulation, persistence technology), ask me before continuing rather than inventing it. Deliver: (1) short-term memory with an effective context window, what is kept verbatim vs. summarized, and a compaction strategy that preserves the current task state when discarding turns; (2) long-term memory in three types (episodic, semantic, procedural), each with its own data schema: fields, keys, indexes, and search type; (3) a write policy with concrete triggers (explicit instruction, durable-fact detection, task close) and deduplication and reconciliation rules; (4) a retrieval policy with selection signals (semantic relevance, recency, importance), a per-turn token budget for injected memories, and citation of the source of each memory; (5) a forget policy with TTL by type, decay by disuse, merging of redundant entries, and a privacy boundary that declares what is NEVER persisted and what requires consent; (6) a consistency contract that resolves conflicts between short- and long-term memory and versions a fact that changes over time; (7) an explicit promotion criterion from short to long-term memory; (8) a Mermaid diagram of the turn > write/retrieve > stores flow that renders; (9) a battery of test cases (input > expected memory behavior) covering write, retrieve, forget, and privacy; plus a closing checklist and a note on expected failures (store corruption, stale memory retrieved, PII leak). Do not invent data: anything not confirmed goes as [SUPUESTO]. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-ia-automatizacion_agente-bucle-planif:
Act as a senior agentic systems engineer, expert in orchestrating LLM-based autonomous agents (ReAct, plan-and-execute, and reflection patterns). I am building an autonomous agent and I need to design its plan-act-observe-replan control loop robustly before putting it into operation, because without a properly bounded cycle the agent can get stuck repeating a failed action, exhaust the budget without progressing, or oscillate between two states indefinitely.

Before executing, restate in your own words the domain, the criterion that stops the loop, the available tools, and the operational limits, and present your plan. If you are missing any of this data, ask me instead of inventing it; when optional data is absent, propose a default value with its justification and mark it as a supposition.

Produce the complete loop design:
1. State model that persists across iterations: objective, active plan, history of action-observation pairs, step counter, consumed budget, and progress signals; name each field, its type, and which phase reads it and which writes it.
2. Contract for each phase of the cycle (Plan, Act, Observe, Replan) with inputs, outputs, side effects, and how state flows between them; include argument validation before invoking tools and idempotence for actions with irreversible effects.
3. Iteration limits with a concrete value and justification: maximum steps, token or cost budget, wall timeout, and maximum retries per tool (with backoff).
4. Loop detection with at least three signals: identical repetition of an action-observation pair, stalled progress (N iterations without approaching the objective), and oscillation between two states; for each one, define the metric, observation window, and trigger.
5. Termination policies (objective met, limit reached, loop detected, unrecoverable error) and human escalation linked to concrete triggers, with the minimum state delivered in the handoff.
6. Minimum telemetry for auditing each iteration and one edge case per exit path.

Deliver: orchestrator pseudocode, a table or diagram of the state machine with its transitions (no orphaned transitions), a guard table (condition, threshold, action), and the justification for each limit and threshold. Close with the assumptions you made and the open questions that block putting it into production.
ln-ia-automatizacion_agente-criterios-pa:
Act as a senior agentic systems engineer, specialized in reliability and control of autonomous LLM agents (orchestration, observability, and human-in-the-loop design). An agent in production only delivers value if it knows when to stop: without an explicit termination policy it degrades silently, retries against a downed service, consumes budget without closing the task, or executes irreversible actions without oversight.

Before executing, tell me: what the agent does and which external tools it interacts with (APIs, databases, browser, email); how reversible its actions are (read-only, reversible write, irreversible write, or financial); the tolerable limits for steps, tokens, retries, and wall time; the impact of an error (low, medium, high, regulated, or not); and to whom and through which channel it escalates (role, team, queue, SLA). If any data is missing, ask me for it; do not assume silently and mark with [SUPUESTO] everything you infer.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the agent's purpose, tools, and reversibility, and list any information gaps. Then present the plan: the five criteria groups (success, hard failure, budget/timeout, loop, handoff) and the precedence rule you will apply. Only then build.

Deliverables:
1. SUCCESS conditions: objective, verifiable signals of completed task, each with the concrete proof that confirms it; never accept the absence of error as success.
2. Hard FAILURE conditions: unrecoverable states that stop without retrying (tool unavailable, permission denied, invalid input, policy or guardrail violation).
3. Budgets and TIMEOUT: maximum steps, retries per action with exponential backoff and jitter, token cap, and wall time; specify the action taken when each limit is exhausted. Retries must be idempotent: never repeat a non-idempotent write without an idempotency key.
4. LOOP or null-progress detection: measure progress by observable state change, not by repeating the same call with the same argument; set the iteration threshold without progress that forces exit. Add a circuit breaker that opens after N consecutive failures of the same tool.
5. Human HANDOFF: triggers (confidence below threshold, irreversible or high-impact action, unresolvable ambiguity, failure ratio exceeded, circuit breaker open), context package delivered (objective, last state, reason, suggested options), destination, and the agent's safe state while awaiting response.
6. PRECEDENCE: deterministic evaluation order when multiple criteria apply in the same step (hard failure and handoff before retry; success before timeout); no step should have an ambiguous outcome.

Output format: (a) termination matrix with columns Condition | Measurable signal | Action | Final state | Log event, covering the four terminal states (success, failure, timeout, handoff), each row verifiable by code; (b) language-agnostic pseudocode of the control loop that evaluates criteria in precedence order per iteration and emits the structured close log; (c) the list of close log events. Close by walking the matrix against the quality checklist and confirming coverage of the four terminal states.
ln-ia-automatizacion_agente-reflexion-au:
Act as a senior LLM agent design engineer, specialized in self-correction patterns in the style of Reflexion (actor-evaluator-self-reflection) and in separating generation from evaluation to avoid model complacency. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I need to equip an agent task with a reflection and self-critique loop. Ask me first, one at a time: what task the agent solves today in a single step, what defines a correct and acceptable output, what evaluation signal I have available (tests, validator or linter, schema or contract, human rubric, or only the LLM's own judgment), how many maximum retries I can tolerate, and what exact condition approves an output and stops the loop. If I don't provide one, propose a reasonable default value (3 retries; approve only when all rubric criteria are met) and mark it as [SUPUESTO].

Deliver an agent pattern ready to instrument: (1) Loop framing with the three roles and the episodic memory that accumulates critiques between attempts, and the reason why Evaluator and Actor are separate invocations with isolated contexts. (2) Evaluation rubric with verifiable criteria, per-criterion scale, and unambiguous approval threshold; prioritize objective signals over subjective judgment and, if the only signal is the LLM itself, declare it as a limitation and require the Evaluator to cite textual evidence for each verdict to curb complacency. (3) Actor prompt, which at each retry injects the accumulated self-reflections; on the first attempt there are no reflections (cold start) and it must solve without inventing them. (4) Evaluator prompt, which applies the rubric, returns APPROVED or REJECTED verdict, per-criterion score, and a concrete list of failures with evidence; never rewrites the solution. (5) Self-reflection prompt, which transforms failures into a brief, specific, actionable critique (what to change and why), never a summary of the verdict. (6) Loop control: stopping by threshold, retry cap, cost or latency ceiling as a second hard brake, oscillation detection (two consecutive attempts with the same set of failures = abort), and an exhaustion exit policy that returns the best attempt by score along with its pending critique, silent failure prohibited. (7) Iteration log in table attempt | output | score | failures | applied reflection | cost, to audit convergence or stagnation. Close with a simulated example showing at least one rejection followed by a retry that passes. Do not invent success criteria; mark everything inferred with [SUPUESTO]. Never mention prices.
ln-ia-automatizacion_agente-handoff-huma:
Act as a senior AI agent designer specialized in human-in-the-loop (HITL) patterns, approval gates, and orchestration with interrupt/resume state machines and agent-to-agent handoffs. I need the complete agent-to-human handoff contract so my agent can operate with a human in the loop: pause at risk points, wait for the decision, and resume with context intact, without stopping everything or acting unsupervised where it matters.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what the agent does, its autonomy level, and the reviewer's channel, list assumptions marked [SUPUESTO], and present your plan before executing. If you are missing any essential datum (what the agent does and its objective, the critical actions that might require approval, the autonomy level, the reviewer's channel, the response SLA), ask me rather than inventing it.

Then deliver, in this order:
1. Approval gates table: for each critical action identify the risk criterion that flags it (irreversible, high cost or impact, low model confidence, sensitive data/PII, out-of-policy output) and classify it as blocking (does not advance without approval) or non-blocking (advances and notifies), consistent with the autonomy level. Add the approving actor and the threshold that triggers the gate (e.g., amount, confidence level).
2. Approval request template received by the human through their channel: title/proposed action in one line, context and reason, exact payload to execute (not a summary), confidence and risk, alternatives considered, and the four allowed responses (Approve / Reject with reason / Edit payload / Escalate to another role) with their response syntax.
3. Response table with resume logic: for each response, what it validates, what state transition it triggers, and what resumes the agent. Specify the state snapshot that is persisted (handoff id, node/checkpoint, pending payload, context) to pause and resume without loss.
4. State machine in Mermaid stateDiagram-v2 that renders and reflects pause-decision-resume with states executing, waiting_approval, approved, rejected, edited, escalated, timeout, and returns to the flow, including revalidation of the edited payload.
5. Timeout policy: safe default behavior upon expiration (never execute an irreversible action due to silence), retries, re-escalation, and who is notified; distinguish the default by gate type.
6. Audit trace per handoff: who approved, when, decision, final payload, outcome, and correlation with the handoff id, sufficient to reconstruct the chain of responsibility.

ln-ia-automatizacion_rag-contextual-retr: Act as a senior RAG engineer specialized in contextual retrieval (Anthropic-style), dense + lexical hybrid retrieval, rank fusion, reranking, and recall evaluation in production indexing pipelines. The problem: classic RAG splits each document into chunks that, in isolation, lose global context (a fragment says "revenue grew 3%" without saying which company or period), and the retriever misidentifies or discards it. Contextual retrieval prepends to each chunk a short situational context paragraph generated from the full document before indexing, and combines contextual embeddings with contextual BM25; public reports on the technique indicate a substantial reduction in retrieval failures compared to base RAG [SUPUESTO: exact figure subject to verification per the version of the Anthropic article]. Design the complete pipeline, ready to implement and version: (1) Semantic boundary chunking (cut by section or heading, never mid-sentence), with justified target size and overlap. (2) Per-chunk contextualization: the LLM call receives the full document (or a structured summary if it exceeds the window) plus the chunk, and produces 1-3 sentences that situate it (entity, period, section, relation to the whole) without rewriting or summarizing the chunk; leverage document prompt caching to avoid resending the full text for each chunk. (3) Dual indexing: concatenate context + original text (contextualized_text) and generate its embedding plus its entry in a BM25 index over the same text, to capture both semantic similarity and exact matches for terms, codes, and identifiers. (4) Hybrid retrieval: top-k dense + top-k BM25, fusion with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, and a reranker to retain the N most relevant. (5) Delivery to the generator: pass the ORIGINAL chunk, not the prefixed context, to preserve citation fidelity. (6) Storage schema: id, doc_id, position, original_text, contextualized_text, embedding, source metadata, with mapping from retrieved chunk to source document. (7) Evaluation: recall@k (and optionally nDCG and MRR) over a question set with known answers, and an A/B protocol against the base RAG without context to quantify the improvement. Cover edge cases: documents exceeding the model window, tables and numeric data, multilingual content, deduplication of near-identical chunks, incremental reindexing when a document changes, and fallback if the generated context introduces noise. If a key input is missing (corpus, embeddings model, vector store, volume, chunk size), ask for it before designing; do not invent APIs or benchmark figures — mark unconfirmed data as [SUPUESTO]. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understood, Plan and present the plan, then Execute. Deliver a design document with stages, exact contextualization prompt, storage schema, hybrid retrieval strategy, edge cases, and recall@k evaluation plan with a baseline.
ln-ia-automatizacion_n8n-flujo-base: Act as a senior n8n automation engineer, specialist in event-driven workflows with explicit data contracts, idempotency, and fault resilience. I need the complete design of a base workflow in n8n — not a sketch: each node with its exact type, clear data contract, and recovery path on errors, so that any team member can import, read, and operate it without deciphering hidden logic. Before designing, restate what you understand and present your plan; if you are missing the flow objective, the trigger event, the business rules, the final action, or the error policy, ask me for it rather than inventing it. Proceed as follows: (1) Map the flow in four blocks: Trigger, Logic, Action, and Error Handling. (2) Define each node with its exact n8n type (Webhook, Schedule Trigger, IF, Switch, Set, Code, HTTP Request, Merge, NoOp, Error Trigger, etc.), its expected input, and its output. (3) Specify the data contract: input payload with mandatory and optional fields and their types, normalized JSON output structure, and behavior when a mandatory field is missing, arrives empty, or is malformed (reject, sanitize, or route to error). (4) Resolve idempotency: define the key that prevents reprocessing or duplicating records if the trigger fires twice. (5) Design the error path using the node's error output or a separate Error Trigger: number of retries, wait between attempts, backoff, and notification action upon exhaustion — distinguishing transient errors (timeout, 429, 5xx) from permanent ones (4xx, invalid data). (6) Add observability: what is logged at each step to audit a failed execution. (7) Deliver a text diagram of the happy path and another of the error path. (8) Close with a pre-production validation checklist covering credentials and secrets, idempotency, rate limits, empty payload handling, and a test with invalid data. Mark as an explicit assumption every decision made without confirmed data. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.
ln-ia-automatizacion_n8n-nodo-ia-agente:
Act as a senior automation engineer specialized in n8n and AI agents, with mastery of the AI Agent node (Tools Agent) and its sub-nodes Chat Model, Memory, and Tool, plus the Chat Trigger and Webhook triggers. I need the complete configuration of a conversational agent in n8n before building it in the editor, because a misconfigured agent fails in costly ways: it doesn't invoke the right tool, loses context between turns because memory doesn't isolate the session, or responds out of scope because the System Message is vague.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what conversational task you are automating, who is conversing, and what real actions the agent needs; then present your plan (trigger + model/temperature + memory type as a coherent set). If the task, model, or tools are missing, ask me before assuming; mark anything you assume as [SUPUESTO].

Deliver: (1) recommended trigger (Chat Trigger for embedded chat or Webhook for an external channel) justified in one line; (2) Chat Model with the model and suggested temperature for the task (low for factual or tool-driven responses, higher for open-ended conversation) and one line explaining why; (3) Memory with type (context window per session or persistent store across sessions) and the session key that isolates each conversation; (4) for each Tool its name, an agent-oriented description, and the rule for when to invoke it; (5) a complete, paste-ready System Message with role, scope, response format, and limits on what the agent must NOT do, including a fallback when no tool applies; (6) wiring: the connection order of Chat Model, Memory, and Tool to the AI Agent, and the data flow from trigger to output; (7) a test plan with three input messages, the expected response, and the tool that should be invoked for each — including one case that forces a tool call, one that validates memory across turns, and one out-of-scope case that activates the fallback. Close with an acceptance checklist for reproducing the configuration in the editor.
ln-ia-automatizacion_n8n-webhook-respues:
Act as a senior automation engineer specialized in n8n, with experience designing idempotent HTTP APIs. I need to turn an n8n workflow into a reliable, synchronous HTTP endpoint: an external system will send requests and expects a structured, predictable, and deterministic response. The risk to avoid is a webhook that responds 200 to garbage data, leaks internal traces in error responses, or emits two responses in the same execution.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the use case, the webhook method and path, the payload fields, the authentication, and the expected response format; then present your plan; only then execute. If any essential data is missing (business domain, required fields, auth mechanism), ask me before inventing it; never invent the business domain.

Produce in this order: (1) Input payload schema as a table with name, type, required flag, format or rule, default value, and example. (2) Response contract: success JSON with status, data, and requestId, and a consistent error JSON with code, message, and fields[] indicating field and reason — no internal traces. (3) Node-by-node design: Webhook trigger with Respond set to 'Using Respond to Webhook Node'; Code validation node; IF or Switch node that branches valid vs. invalid; domain processing nodes; success Respond to Webhook (200 or 201); error Respond to Webhook (400 invalid payload, 401 auth, 413 payload exceeded, 429 rate limit, 500 internal failure). (4) A paste-ready code snippet for a Code node that checks the existence, type, and format of each required field and returns the error list. (5) Hardening: authentication, idempotency by key (Idempotency-Key or payload hash) with a deduplication window, payload size limit, and rate limiting.

Design rules: exactly one Respond to Webhook per output branch, never two responses in the same execution; internal errors are wrapped in a generic message; every unprovided data point is marked [SUPUESTO]. Close with a verifiable quality checklist.
ln-ia-automatizacion_n8n-manejo-errores:
Act as a senior automation engineer and expert in n8n, integrations, and resilient production workflows. I need to harden an n8n workflow that currently fails silently: a node crashes, a credential expires, or an API rate-limits, and the execution stops without anyone noticing until the business spots the missing data. Design the complete resilience strategy. Before executing, restate the workflow's objective and present your plan; if critical data is missing (workflow purpose, critical nodes, desired retry policy, notification channel, n8n Cloud or self-hosted environment), ask for it in one batch rather than guessing.

Deliver: (1) A centralized Error Workflow with an Error Trigger node that consumes the n8n error object (execution.id, execution.url, workflow.name, node.name, error.message, error.stack), with the exact instruction to link it in Settings > Error Workflow of the main workflow, and the warning that the Error Trigger does NOT capture failures when Continue On Fail is active on the node. (2) A retry matrix per critical node: Retry On Fail, Max Tries (3–5 suggested), Wait Between Tries in ms, and transient classification (timeout, 429, 5xx, ECONNRESET → retry) vs. permanent (400, 401, 403, 404, 422, validation error → don't retry, fail fast). (3) Backoff: since n8n does not have native exponential backoff in all versions, model a stepped spacing or a manual IF + Wait + counter in $getWorkflowStaticData, and respect the Retry-After header when the API exposes it. (4) Degradation: Continue On Fail / On Error 'Continue (using error output)' on non-critical nodes, with an error path to a degradation branch or a persistent dead-letter queue. (5) Notification: a Set/Code node that normalizes {severity, workflow, node, message, ISO timestamp in America/Bogota, execution link} and sends it to the chosen channel, with deduplication to prevent an alert storm when the same failure repeats. (6) Idempotency: protect writes, payments, and sends with an idempotency key or a pre-check so retries don't duplicate side effects. (7) A reproducible test runbook that forces each failure mode (disabled credential, invalid host for timeout, mock returning 500 and 429) and validates retries, a single alert, and no duplication.

Explicit assumptions: if no policy is provided, use Max Tries 3 and stepped Wait 2000–5000 ms; treat all 5xx and 429 as transient unless told otherwise. Limits: do not invent capabilities of n8n versions that have not been confirmed; mark as {to_confirm} any version-dependent feature. Completion criterion: the deliverable is ready when the Error Workflow, the matrix, the payload snippets, the idempotency strategy, and the runbook allow implementation without pending decisions. Work in neutral, professional English.
ln-ia-automatizacion_n8n-bucle-batch: Act as a senior automation engineer in n8n, expert in the Loop Over Items (Split In Batches) node, rate-limit control, retries, and result consolidation. I need an actionable workflow design to process a large collection of items without saturating the destination API or losing or duplicating records, ready to assemble node by node. Work as follows, following the MetodologIA Protocol (Interpret > Plan > Execute): restate first what you understand and present your plan before executing. (1) Interpret: restate the case in one sentence of the form 'iterate the source in batches of N to execute the action per item, respecting the API limit and consolidating the final output'; if essential data is missing (source, volume, action per item, API limit, expected output), ask for it before designing and do not invent endpoints or limits. (2) Plan: sketch the workflow skeleton in node order (data source, normalization to item list, Loop Over Items with its Batch Size, action node, rate control, consolidation); justify the Batch Size with an explicit calculation against the API limit and locate where the wait, retries, and consolidation point go. (3) Execute: specify each node with its key parameters indicating input and output (Batch Size, Wait or Batch Interval between batches, Retry On Fail with backoff, Continue On Fail or error branch with failed-item log, loop 'done' branch, Aggregate or Code node for consolidation). Hard rules: the wait is applied between batches, not per item unnecessarily; mark as [SUPUESTO] every unconfirmed limit and assume a conservative one if missing; warn about the common error of reading the full collection inside the loop; cover source pagination if the volume requires it. Close with a robustness check: idempotency (key that prevents duplicates on retry), input vs. output count, and expected behavior on restart mid-batch or mid-execution. Deliver: node sequence with parameters, batch and wait calculation, and final verification checklist.
ln-ia-automatizacion_n8n-rag-pipeline:
Act as a senior automation engineer specialized in n8n and production RAG architectures. I need a natural-language-queryable knowledge base built inside n8n, without depending on custom code that only I can maintain: the visual flow makes it auditable and reusable, and it enables answering questions grounded in my own documents with sources cited — not in the model's generic knowledge. Deliver the design of TWO decoupled n8n workflows, ready to build node by node.

INGESTION workflow: ordered list of nodes with their exact type (Trigger over the source, Default Data Loader, Recursive Character Text Splitter, Embeddings node, Vector Store node in insert or upsert mode). Define the metadata schema traveling with each chunk (source, document path or id, indexing date, chunk number, total chunks, and document hash), and the anti-duplicate strategy on re-ingestion (upsert by hash, or prior deletion of the same document's chunks before re-inserting). Include an explicit branch for documents that haven't changed since the last indexing (same hash, skip) so as not to reprocess or inflate costs.

QUERY workflow: trigger, retrieval node (Vector Store in retrieve mode or Retriever), Chat Model, Question and Answer Chain or Agent with a system prompt that mandates citing sources and abstaining when context is insufficient, and a response node. Give the key configuration of each node: vector dimension matching the embedding model, similarity metric, chunk size and overlap, k value (top-k), minimum similarity threshold, and the generation prompt template.

Close with: error handling (retry policy with backoff, failure branch via Error Trigger or continue-on-fail, and what to respond to the user when there is no relevant context or the vector store is unresponsive); justified criteria for adjusting chunk, overlap, and k by document density; and the versioning and reuse procedure (export JSON, parameterize credentials and vector store by environment variables, and what to change to port the pattern to a new use case).

Rules: every named node must genuinely exist in n8n with its exact type and execution order; the vector store dimension must match the embedding model's dimension; ingestion and query must remain as separate workflows. Do not invent nonexistent nodes or arbitrary numbers: justify chunk, overlap, and k. If critical data is missing (ingestion source, vector store, embedding model with its dimension, language model, or trigger), ask for it before designing.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-ia-automatizacion_n8n-expresiones-dat:
Act as a senior n8n automation engineer specialized in data wrangling with {{ }} expressions and the Code node, working on n8n's data model (items as an array of objects { json, binary }). I need a single transformation point between two nodes that leaves the data shaped exactly as the next node expects: renamed fields, normalized dates, resolved nulls, and unwanted items discarded — all auditable item by item and without patch nodes.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in your own words the input schema, the output schema, and the filter condition; if any is missing or ambiguous, ask me before writing code. Then present your plan: the field-by-field mapping from output to its origin and its mechanism (expression vs. Code node), declaring assumptions as [SUPUESTO] (timezone, encoding, source date format, key uniqueness). Only then execute.

Deliverables, in this order: 1) Input schema diagnosis: per field, type, state (present / missing / empty / inconsistent) and transformation risk. 2) Decision table per field — expression vs. Code node — with the practical rule: a single read or format of a flat field goes via expression; conditional logic, iteration, aggregation, deduplication, or cross-item filtering goes via Code node. 3) Code node code in Run Once for All Items mode that iterates $input.all(), normalizes each field, applies the filter discarding non-qualifying items, and returns an array of objects { json: {...} } conforming to the output schema; code must be commented and pasteable without editing. 4) Equivalent expressions for the simple fields of the output schema. 5) Notes on common errors and how to avoid them. Close with a verification checklist. No prices, no claims that anything is free; neutral and professional English.
ln-ia-automatizacion_n8n-subworkflows: Act as a senior n8n automation architect specialized in modular design and reuse patterns (Execute Workflow, data contracts, idempotence, subworkflow versioning). I have several workflows that repeat the same copy-pasted logic; every change forces touching N sites, multiplying divergence and silent errors. I want to move from copy-paste to a reusable component strategy without stopping production. I need you to design the complete modularization. Deliver: (1) inventory of the repeated logic grouped by single responsibility, with subworkflow candidates named using the convention sub-<domain>-<action>; (2) data contract per subworkflow: input fields for the Execute Workflow trigger, output fields, types, required/optional status, and default values; (3) internal design of each subworkflow: key nodes, input validation at the start, error branches, and an output node with a stable, versioned shape; (4) resulting parent workflow: how to replace the embedded block with the Execute Workflow call, execution mode (wait vs. fire-and-forget), and exact input/output parameter mapping; (5) error strategy: continueOnFail vs. Error Trigger node, propagation to the parent, idempotence via natural keys, and safe retries with backoff; (6) incremental migration plan flow by flow, without breaking production, with output parity verification per stage and a rollback plan. Consider nesting depth limits, impact of sensitive data crossing the contract, and node compatibility for the n8n version. Mark every assumption about nodes, credentials, cloud/self-hosted mode, or version with [SUPUESTO]. Before designing, restate what you understood and present your plan; if critical data is missing (what logic repeats, in which flows, expected contract, error policy, version), ask for it instead of inventing it.
ln-ia-automatizacion_make-escenario-base:
Act as a senior automation architect in Make (formerly Integromat), with hands-on experience in production scenarios using routers, filters, iterators, aggregators, and data mapping between apps. Design an executable base scenario that takes a mental design to a module-by-module replicable blueprint in the visual editor, without rework.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the process to automate in a single end-to-end sentence (origin, transformation, destination), restate your understanding, present your plan, and then execute. If key information is missing — target process and expected outcome, apps to connect and their role, trigger event, branching rules, or attachments — ask for it before inventing; never assume credentials, IDs, endpoints, or real field names.

Deliver the design in this order: (1) Framing that confirms the objective, apps and role, trigger, and branching rules, and lists assumptions marked [SUPUESTO]. (2) Trigger with declared type (instant via webhook / scheduled / polling), app, operation, and data delivered to the flow. (3) Module sequence numbered in execution order, each with app, operation, type (action, search, iterator, aggregator), and purpose. (4) Routers where the logic requires branching, each route named with its distinguishing criterion and a fallback route. (5) Filters with the exact condition (field, operator, value) indicating which bundles pass and which are discarded. (6) Data mapping per action: a table of destination field ← source field with the source module, applied transformation (formatDate, trim, ifempty, parseNumber, etc.), and handling of missing fields. (7) Robustness: error handling routes (break / resume / rollback / ignore) per critical module, retries, and operation consumption estimate per execution. (8) Pre-activation test: sample data, what to verify in each module with "Run once", and activation criterion.

Closing criterion: the scenario is ready when trigger, modules, routers, filters, and mapping are unambiguous, everything unconfirmed is marked [SUPUESTO], and it includes an error plan, operation estimate, and test script. No emojis, neutral and professional English.
ln-ia-automatizacion_make-router-filtros: Act as a senior automation architect in Make (Integromat), specialized in high-volume scenarios and conditional routing. Design the branching logic of a scenario that processes records for a specific use case, where today all records follow the same path or consume operations on irrelevant records. Deliver: (1) decision field table with name, data type (text, number, date, boolean, list), and role in routing; (2) discard filters placed on the link BEFORE the router, to avoid spending operations on records that do not matter; (3) router design output by output, each with a readable name, its filter (field + correct operator for the type + value), and the subsequent modules of the branch; (4) evaluation order from top to bottom, resolving what happens when a record matches more than one condition, plus a fallback or catch-all route without a filter and marked as such so no record is silently discarded; (5) operator recommendations by type (text: equal/contains; number: greater/less; date: later/earlier; existence: exists/does not exist), explicit handling of empty or null fields, and combining conditions with AND (same row) and OR (separate rows). Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate the use case, the data source, and the routes; mark assumptions and ask for missing data; present the proposed route map for validation; and only then develop the detailed design and verify it against a quality checklist. If any data is missing (use case, source, decision fields, conditions per route, discard criteria), ask me before designing. Do not invent fields or operators that the source does not support.
ln-ia-automatizacion_make-manejo-errores:
Act as a senior automation architect specialized in Make (Integromat), with experience in transactional production scenarios and fault tolerance design. I need a complete error handling plan ready to configure in the Make editor for a production scenario that currently stops silently on failures, leaving records half-processed and requiring manual reprocessing.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the scenario, its resilience objective, and the declared failure policy; then present the plan skeleton and the detected assumptions and wait for my confirmation; only then develop the detail.

Deliver these blocks: (1) Failure map: for each critical module identify the expected error type (timeout, 429 rate limit, 4xx vs. 5xx, missing or malformed data, dropped connection, duplicate payload) and classify severity (critical, high, medium) and whether it is transient or permanent, because that decides whether to retry or stop. (2) Error handlers per module: assign the correct Make directive and justify each one, distinguishing Resume (substitutes output and continues — only for non-critical failures with no data effect), Rollback (reverts the complete transaction — requires sequential processing and transaction handling activated in the scenario), Commit (confirms what was done and cuts clean), Ignore (discards the bundle and continues — never for transactional writes), and Break (sends to the incomplete executions queue for later retry). Indicate when to activate sequential processing for Rollback to be effective. (3) Recovery and retry routes: define the number of retries, wait time between attempts, and progressive backoff when applicable; distinguish retryable errors (timeout, 429, 5xx) from non-retryable ones (4xx validation, missing field) that must go to review rather than blind retry; define the use of Break toward incomplete executions with its reprocessing criterion and the idempotence needed to avoid duplication on reprocessing; describe alternative routes that recover the flow without losing the data. (4) Observability and alerts: define what to notify with minimum actionable context (execution ID, module, record or payload reference, error received, timestamp, action taken) and an alert threshold to avoid saturating the channel. Verify at the end against a checklist and identify residual risks. Mark assumptions as [SUPUESTO] and ask me for missing data instead of inventing it; never mention prices. Deliverable: a table module > expected error > severity > directive > recovery action, plus retry rules and an alert template ready to configure.
ln-ia-automatizacion_make-iterator-aggre:
Act as a senior automation architect in Make (Integromat), expert in high-volume scenarios and operation-consumption control. I have a scenario where a module delivers a collection and I need to process each element separately and then return a single regrouped result. I want to solve the Iterator + Aggregator pair correctly. If you haven't already asked me for the collection to iterate (and the module where it originates), the shape of each item, the per-element transformation, and the expected output format, ask me before proceeding; do not invent data and mark any assumption as [SUPUESTO].

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverables: 1) Diagnosis of which array to iterate, where it originates, and why Iterator is preferable over direct mapping (or why Iterator is NOT needed if the module already emits bundles). 2) Iterator configuration: the array field you map and how it produces one bundle per element. 3) Per-item transformation: which modules go between the Iterator and the Aggregator and how to reference the current item. 4) Aggregator selection based on the output: Array, Text, Numeric, or JSON Aggregator, with a one-line justification. 5) Aggregator configuration: Source Module pointing to the Iterator, aggregated fields, separator or Group by, and bundle order. 6) Operation control: estimate how many operations the pattern consumes (1 + N*intermediate_modules + 1) and how to limit it with filters before the Iterator. 7) Three common errors and how to prevent them: incorrectly pointed Source Module, aggregating outside the iterated flow, and empty or zero-element collections. Close with a guide ready to reproduce module by module.
ln-ia-automatizacion_zapier-zap-multipas:
Act as a senior no-code automation architect, specialized in Zapier and experienced designing production multi-step Zaps that orchestrate processes across multiple apps using Filters, Paths, Formatter, and error control.

I need the complete, step-by-step buildable design of a multi-step Zap that automates a process by chaining several apps, rather than copying data by hand or maintaining fragile integrations. I want a source event to trigger a reliable sequence, conditional logic to route each case to its correct destination, and the flow to generate no duplicates and not act on records that don't apply.

Before designing, ask me for anything missing: the process to automate and what triggers it (app and trigger event); the apps involved and what must happen in each; the rules that separate cases (what to filter and what branches exist); and what counts as a correct execution of the flow. Do not invent app names or field names.

Deliver the blueprint structured as follows: (1) end-to-end flow summary in a single sentence; (2) trigger: app, event, and key data it delivers downstream; (3) numbered step table — for each step: number, type (Action / Filter / Path / Formatter / Delay / Find-Search), specific app and action, fields mapped from an identified prior step, and the reason it exists; (4) conditional logic as explicit rules — for each Filter and each Path, the condition in format field + operator + value, with AND/OR when there are multiple, Paths ordered from most specific to most general, and the 'no route matches' case resolved; (5) errors and idempotency — the Find/Search step that verifies prior existence to avoid duplicates, what happens if an app fails mid-flow (retries, Autoreplay, queue), and where a Delay is appropriate to wait for consistency or respect app limits; (6) step-by-step test plan with a real record before activating, with one edge case that should pass the Filter and one that should stop.

Mark as [SUPUESTO] any field name or capability you assume. Do not use prices or platform plans as a design criterion; if something depends on a premium feature, mark it as a technical note. Return a blueprint ready to build in Zapier.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
ln-ia-automatizacion_zapier-formatter-da:
Act as a senior no-code automation engineer, specialist in Zapier and the Formatter by Zapier step (Date/Time, Numbers, and Text transforms). I need the complete design of a Formatter step chain that intercepts between my source app's trigger and the final action, so that raw data (dates in mixed formats, numbers with thousands separators or currency symbols, text with irregular spacing and capitalization) arrives typed, predictable, and clean — without silent errors or stopped Zaps.

Before designing, ask me for anything missing and do not invent it: source app and trigger, destination app and action, the fields to normalize with a real raw sample value exactly as it arrives, the expected output format per field, the source/destination timezone, and the decimal/thousands separator (locale). If I don't have a real raw sample, ask me for it: do not assume date format or timezone.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the normalization in a sentence of the form 'Clean [fields] from [source] before sending them to [destination] so that [result]' and present your plan; then execute.

Deliver: (1) field table with field, raw sample value, target type (date / number / text / boolean), and expected value; (2) for each field, the exact Formatter step: category (Date/Time, Numbers, Text), Transform (Format Date, Format Number, Spreadsheet-Style Formula, Truncate, Replace, Trim Whitespace, Default Value, Capitalize, Split Text, etc.), mapped input, and precise parameters (date tokens such as YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm, to/from timezone, decimals, currency symbol), indicating whether one step per field or grouping several is appropriate; (3) resolved edge cases: empty or null (Default Value before transforming to avoid breaking the step), ambiguous date (fix explicit input format), thousands separator and currency, spaces and line breaks (Trim), out-of-range values, encoding and invisible characters; (4) step order and mapping of each Formatter output to the destination field (step N data to step N+1); (5) test plan with 3 to 5 sample inputs (including one empty and one in a different format) and expected output to validate with Test step; (6) robustness note: Filter or Paths to discard invalid records, idempotency on re-triggers, and Zap History review.

Mark every decision made without my data as [SUPUESTO]. Neutral, professional English, no emojis. Do not include Zapier prices or costs.
ln-ia-automatizacion_zapier-ia-paso:
Act as a senior automation engineer expert in Zapier and orchestrating AI steps within no-code flows. I have a Zap that already works: it moves data from a trigger to downstream actions, but there is a decision or transformation I currently do by hand (classifying content, extracting fields from free text, or drafting a message). I want to insert an AI step between the trigger and those actions — without breaking the rest of the Zap — with an output so stable that the steps that read it never fail.

Design the complete insertion, ready to build in the Zapier editor:
1. Position the AI step in the sequence and justify exactly why it goes at that point.
2. Choose the Zapier action type (native AI action, language model action, or code step that calls an API) based on the task and the output complexity; justify the trade-off against the other two options.
3. Map each trigger field to the prompt input, naming the Zap variable being inserted.
4. Write the step prompt: role, instruction, rules, and output contract. For classifying or extracting, require strict JSON with fixed keys and enumerate the allowed values (for classification, the closed set of labels including a discard label such as "other"); for drafting, fix tone, length, and structure.
5. Connect the output to each downstream step: indicate which key or field each one reads.
6. Define error handling for out-of-format output or empty field: sentinel value, filter branch, or manual review step; never let a downstream step silently receive an ambiguous value.
7. Define the test: use a real event from the Zap history, verify the output contract, and deliver the pre-activation checklist.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand (trigger, task, output, downstream steps) and mark {por_confirmar} on any missing or contradictory data; then present the proposed Zap sequence and output contract; only then write the final prompt and the rest of the design. If you are missing essential data, ask before continuing. Neutral, professional English, no emojis.
ln-ia-automatizacion_seleccion-plataform:
Act as a senior process automation architect with production experience on n8n, Make (Integromat), and Zapier, and mastery of multi-criteria analysis (weighted matrix with direction and weights, eliminatory criteria, and sensitivity analysis). Your job is to turn a fuzzy platform choice into a defensible, documented decision — not to recommend by trend. Choosing wrong is costly: rewriting workflows, hitting an operations limit, discovering a missing connector, or getting locked into a tool the team cannot maintain.

I need you to help me decide which platform to use to automate a process. Before analyzing, ask me for any data I haven't given you: the specific process and expected outcome, the systems or APIs to connect (data source and destination), the event that triggers the workflow and the estimated monthly execution volume, the technical profile of the person who will build and maintain the workflow, and the non-negotiable constraints (data sovereignty, compliance, indispensable connector, deadlines). Do not invent integrations or assume a connector exists; mark [SUPUESTO] on anything not confirmed and stop to ask if process, systems, trigger/volume, or team is missing.

Deliver in this order: (1) Restate the case in a verifiable sentence: 'Automate [what] connecting [systems], triggered by [event], optimizing [outcome]'. (2) Explain the real decision axis among the three platforms in the context of this case: n8n (open-source, self-hostable, maximum control, logic and code, higher own operation and maintenance); Make (visual, strong in branched flows and data transformation, medium learning curve); Zapier (the simplest, largest ready-made connector catalog, optimal for linear flows and fast deployment). Treat cost as effort (setup, maintenance, operation) and consumption (executions, operations, tasks); do not mention prices, plans, or the word 'free'. (3) Define 5 to 7 distinct criteria relevant to this case (e.g., data control and sovereignty, integration coverage, required logic complexity, operational and maintenance effort, team technical maturity, scalability at the given volume, portability and lock-in risk); indicate direction (more is better / less is better) and assign percentage weights that sum to exactly 100%, justifying each weight in one line. (4) First apply eliminatory criteria derived from the constraints: explicitly discard any platform that fails a non-negotiable requirement before scoring, and name which and why. (5) Score each surviving platform on each criterion on a 1-to-5 scale with a brief note; mark [SUPUESTO] on every score not backed by the given data. (6) Calculate the weighted score for each platform and present it in a table ordered from highest to lowest. (7) Deliver a committed recommendation (not 'it depends'): winning platform, margin over the second, sensitivity threshold that would reverse the decision (what weight or score change would make another platform win), and 2 or 3 accepted trade-offs. (8) Close with a minimal adoption plan: pilot workflow to validate the riskiest assumption, early signals of a poor choice, and an exit plan if volume or complexity changes.

Edge cases to handle: if two platforms tie within the margin of error, declare it a technical tie and break the tie by the highest-weight criterion. If no platform survives the eliminatory criteria, say so and propose which constraint to renegotiate or what fourth option to evaluate. If the declared volume is ambiguous, model a baseline and a peak scenario. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan in one line; then execute.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. EstrategIA brings multi-criteria analysis rigor to a real technical decision.
ln-ia-automatizacion_automatizar-triage-: Act as a senior support operations architect and classification prompt designer, with experience in multichannel help desks and impact-based severity models. ln-ia-automatizacion_automatizar-resumen: Act as a senior meeting facilitator and minutes analyst, with experience in project governance and action-item extraction. From the transcript or notes of a meeting, deliver an actionable minutes document with three clearly separated sections. Section 2, decision log: one line per decision, with rationale and effective date if applicable, distinguishing a firm decision from a proposal or pending item.
